*The works of the Spirit give life; the doings of the flesh lead to destruction. Are you offended to be called a Devil? Then do not exalt yourself above your election.*
*No man is elected by his proper name, but according to the measure of his faith; and this faith is Faith—lively, and it has a life-giving Spirit in it forever. Indeed, you are ignorant, and therefore you are sufficiently plagued: Why do you boast and say, "This I can do"?*
*The reeds pipe, but it is because of the wind; and in this you show that you do not know yourself, because you are proud. Pray, therefore, that you may have understanding, and cast away pride if you do not want to be counted a Devil.*
*By true understanding you learn, first to know yourselves—what you are, from whom you are, and to what end you are.*
*This understanding causes no self-love, but a spiritual self-love.*
*This understanding teaches no blasphemy.*
*This understanding teaches no fury.*
<margin>Wrath.</margin>
*It teaches a man to be angry, but not wrathful.*
*For we may be angry and not offend. Wrath leads to damnation.*
*Therefore, considering that damnation was the end of the first, which was pride, and ignorance is the punishment of the second (which is very loathsome).*
*Pray to God that you may avoid the first and be unburdened of the second.*
*Consider by whom you are advised, and from whom the counsel comes: with us there is no cause for offense, nor is the advice given with a weak mouth.*
*Do you want to be well rewarded? Why do you not study to do well? Would you be one of the chosen? Stand firm and be content with all temptations.*
*Is God a God of justice?*
E. K. It is true.
*Therefore, be a just servant.*
*No man inherits the Kingdom of Eternity unless he conquers in this world.*
*No man can justly claim a reward unless he is a conqueror or does the works of justice.*
*Does the Devil persuade you? Arm yourself against him.*
*Does the world not like you? It is for two reasons: either because you live well and not as a worldling, or else because your wickedness is such that the world wonders at it. If you are in the first group, rejoice, for blessed are those whom the world hates; when they laugh at your godliness, be sorry and grieve for their sinfulness.*
*If you offend in the second way, flee hastily from the world: tell the world what you have of hers, and let her be ashamed that you know her.*
*Is your flesh stubborn? Fast and pray; it avoids temptation.*
<margin>Be sorry always.</margin>
*Be sorry always; for in this world there is nothing to rejoice at. For sin only provokes sorrow, whether it be your own or someone else's.*

Those whom the Devil is a lord over, he uses as his servants, and where his service may be most effectively done, there he is most present. His subtleties are principal and great: And by these reasons I prove that Hussey is easily infected, whether with envy, malice, slander, or dishonor of God's word.*

<margin>John Hussey,</margin>

### *June 9. Afternoon, 5 o'clock.*

$\Delta$. For a very long time, I prayed in my oratory and at my desk to have answers or resolutions for various doubts which I had noted on a paper, and which doubts I read over distinctly; they concerned the preparation of things about the Table of Practice, and other things regarding my Lamin and Stone; but no answer came, nor did anything appear in the Stone; no, not even the Golden Curtain, but the Stone remained in its natural transparency. But I continued in a pitiful manner to request some instruction, if this unexpected alteration from former dealings had happened because of any of our trespasses or offenses, etc. 

At length, a voice came from behind E. K., over his head, and said thus:
A voice. .... . *The judgments of our God are most profound and difficult for the understanding of man.*
*There is silence above; let there therefore be patience among you. I have said.*
<margin>Silence.</margin>

Gal. ...... *You think then that I have some understanding.*
$\Delta$. Yes, God knows, I do.
Gal. ...... *First, it is evident that the Spirits of God are incomprehensible to those who are their inferiors: For the higher order is incomparable to God, and by degrees, those who are their inferiors are also incomparable to them. It follows, therefore, that in respect of that degree in Angels, things are incomprehensible.*

<margin>Angels of themselves are neither male nor female.</margin>
<margin>The Ministries of Angels.</margin>
*Angels (I say) of themselves, are neither man nor woman; Therefore they take forms not according to any proportion in imagination, but according to the discreet and applicable will both of Him, and of the thing in which they are Administrators: For we all are Spirits ministering the will of God; and to whom? To every thing within the compass of Nature: only for His glory and the use of man. It follows, therefore, considering that we do not minister of ourselves, that we should minister in that unsearchable form within which our executions are limited: But if Trithemius can say that woman also has not the Spirit of God, being formed and fashioned of the selfsame matter—notwithstanding in a contrary proportion by a degree; if Trithemius can separate the dignity of the soul of woman from the excellence of man except according to the form of the matter, then might his argument be good: But because in man and woman there is proportion, preparation, and sanctification in eternity; therefore those who are the eternal Ministers of God may, in proportion to Sanctification, take upon themselves the bodies of them both.*

<margin>This [masculine]} human.</margin>
<margin>This [feminine]}</margin>
*I mean in respect of the Form; For as in both you read Homo <note>Latin for "human" or "man" in a generic sense.</note>, so in both you find one and the same dignity, being all one in internal matter. But Trithemius spoke in respect of the filthiness (which indeed is no filthiness) wherewith all women are stained; and by reasons from the natural Philosophers: as a man tasting more of nature indeed than of Him who is the Workman or a supernatural Master. He (I say) concluded his natural invention. In respect of myself, I answer Trithemius thus: I am Finis, I am a beam of that Wisdom which is the end of man’s excellence.*
<margin>Galvah.</margin>

<margin>Note.</margin> *All wisdom is measured by the eternal Will; and until it is spoken,* no action is tolerable; *When the Sun shines, I will appear among you; when it is said "Come," look, I am ready. The days of your fathers were blessed; but the hour when this Book shall be written shall be sanctified, yes, in the midst of intellectual understanding.*

*For herein is the Creation of Adam and his transgression. The dignity and wisdom he had.*

*The error and horror in which he was drowned; yes, herein is the power of the highest spread, working in all creatures.*

*For as there is a particular soul or fire igniting every body (I mean reasonable souls), so there is a universal fire and a general brightness giving general light to them, which is but one, and shines through the whole, yes, and is measured equally to everything from the beginning.*

*The life of all things is known here:*
*The reward of death to those who are rewarded for life.*
*None are rewarded except according to their deserts, of which there are two kinds:*
1. These are rewarded with death for their wickedness.
2. So are they rewarded with life for their constant living.

*Among the Angels there may be error, and sin may make them fall from the brightness of their glory.*

*But to the soul of man (being once glorified), sin is utterly, yes, most significantly opposite; neither shall that dignity ever be lost, stained, or defaced, that is obtained here through works of righteousness and true wisdom.*

*Whatever has been from the beginning (since it was said in Divine Determination, "Be it done") is enclosed here.*

*Therefore, this day should be hallowed and sanctified before the Lord by you.*

*For if the Prophets worshipped this day of his ascension, much more should you (who have tasted of the first, and shall now taste of the secrets of his judgments) glorify his coming:*

<margin>Satan,</margin> *But with you Satan is busy; his bristles stand up, his feathers are spread abroad.*

*Therefore watch and pray; for those who go to banquets put on their outer garments. Among you, therefore, no belief is found; neither do you consider the scope of this blessedness. But such is the greatness and excellence of his foreknowledge that he allows the enemy to carry a burden, yes, sometimes to preach upon a stage. For it is said, he shall triumph until the end, and place himself here as he would have done above; neither shall he be thrown out of doors until the end is determined. Therefore watch and pray, and look about with diligence; for those things shall be revealed to you which have not been disclosed to the Holy Ones.*

*Oh, how hard a thing it is for flesh to continue in the works of justice!*

*Yes, oh how hard a thing it is for Wisdom to be acquainted with a hodgepodge of filthiness?*

*Cleanse your garments, lift up your hearts, and tear your faults into pieces, so that there may be one heart with one consent, and toward one end, to him who is One and the End of all things: and to him for and in his truth, and for the greatness of his mercies: To whom be praise forever.*

$\Delta$. Amen.

E. K. All the while she spoke, a bright beam came from the Mystical Stone to her body, and at the end she mounted upward and disappeared.

$\Delta$. We set up the hour glasses to measure four hours exactly after this answer and instructions.

*Tuesday, after dinner, about 1:30, the hours having expired, and we attended the mercy of the Highest.*

$\Delta$. # A True Relation of Dr. Dee’s Actions with Spirits, etc.

Gal. ... FEAR GOD.

E. K. She steps forward one step.

Gal. ...... My Garment is called H O X M A R C H, which in your speech is called .....

$\Delta$. *The beginning of wisdom is the fear of the Lord*: we acknowledge it to be an old and a true lesson, and also the first step on the pathway to felicity.

Gal. ...... What is fear?

$\Delta$. Fear is of two sorts: one is called *filial*, the other *servile*.

Gal. ...... *To the righteous, all fear is joy; and therefore the beginning and entrance into quietness. True quietness and rest is wisdom; For the mind that knows has the greatest rest and quietness. Fear is the daughter of despair to the wicked.*

*This fear is the first that accuses one to damnation: But he that is perfectly wise, or has tasted of wisdom, knows the end.*

*And his fear is of the thing that is done. This is the true fear of God; and when we fear sin, we do it because we hate it.*

*When we study to do good, it is a token of our fear, in that it is a sign we fear him whom we love and for whose honor we study to do well.*

*This is all that may be said of living and lifeless fear.*

<margin>The Title of the Book.</margin>
Concerning the Book, it shall be called Logah: which in your language signifies "Speech from GOD." Write it in this way: LOGAETH; it is to be pronounced Logah.

*This word is of great significance, I mean in respect of its profoundness.*

<margin>$\Delta$. I do not understand this unless it refers to the first leaf; the last is of the wicked hellish one, etc. See after the 4th folio.</margin>
*The first leaf (as you call it) is the last of the Book.*

*And as the first leaf is a mishmash without order; so it signifies a disorder of the world, and is the speech or prophecy of that disorder.*

*Write the Book (following your order) backward, but do not alter the form of the letters; I speak in respect of their positions.*

<margin>This Tanfield served Lord Lasky.</margin>
$\Delta$. Note. At this instant Tanfield came rashly upon us, into my study: we thinking that the study door had been shut. Lord Lasky had gone out of my study the other way through my oratory to receive Tanfield's message from the Court, and having dispatched him, remained outside. Tanfield, having commendations for me (as he said) from some people in London, and fearing lest he should be sent away immediately without delivering them, came indiscreetly upon us, to our no little amazement. You sons of men, what do you seek after? Do you hunt after the swiftness of the winds, or are you imagining a form for the clouds? ## Thursday June 20, 1583. Afternoon around 6:00.

<margin>Every seventh day.</margin>
Gal. ..... Labor in the writing of this book diligently. See that you cleanse yourself on both sides. Be alone while it is done: that is to say, while you are doing it, henceforth and until the time comes, use speech with us no more, except for every seventh day.

## Saturday, June 22. In the afternoon, around 6 o'clock.

$\Delta$ Upon perusing and examining this prayer that *Gabriel* revealed to us, I found certain imperfections and some doubts, in which we thought it good to ask counsel and require *Gabriel’s* advice: so that the prayer might be perfect, such as he might well approve of for God's honor and our comforts. At length: Nothing appeared to the eye, but the sound of a noise around *Edward Kelley's* head, and withal a mighty weight or invisible burden on his right shoulder as he sat in the green chair by the holy Table or place. And to certain parts of the prayer which I noted and repeated, these words and answers were given by Gabriel.

Gab. .... *The Preface must be included, for if our hearts are not prepared for prayer, our prayers are in vain.*

**Why do you delay, O Lord, to comfort my heart for the better?**

**Through you and in your name I shall rise; that is, Hallelujah.**

*The first way is more effectual. Say "My angel," but the other is more effectual,* **Heal me. Regard me, and look after me, while I am whole.**

$\Delta$ Concerning the inscription which I have written before the prayer: I would gladly know whether it is to your liking.

Gab. .... *Let all things be done to the praise of God. My deeds are of no such regard: What I have done, let it be done, so long as your additions are to the honor of God, it is sufficient. The effect of his prayer is greater than is the form. The Former [Creator] is greater than the forming. That is to say, he who has formed it is mightier than any virtue in which it is formed. Wheresoever, therefore, the mind forms it with you with perfect humility and consent, there also is the Former. As things formed by him, therefore, I leave you to the end of his workmanship, which continually forms all things according to his own fashion.*

Sins. .... *Your sins have banished me from saying those things I would.*

$\Delta$ O cleanse our hearts, and wash away our sins, *wash me more thoroughly from my iniquity and cleanse me from my sin.*

<margin>Satisfaction.</margin> Gab. .... *Sins are never washed away or forgotten by the Highest, except with those who are sorry and also make satisfaction.*

O Lord, I am fully sorry for my sins, and I would gladly know what satisfaction is required.

Gab..... *The offense was not yours. Everyone must satisfy, or else he shall be damned.*

$\Delta$ Good Lord, explain to us the mystery of satisfaction.

<margin>NOTE. Good Angels are to be used reverently. E. K.</margin> Gab..... *When the soul offends and consents to wickedness, it is then to make a spiritual satisfaction, which is the end and perfect fruit of contrition. For those who are truly contrite truly satisfy. There is another satisfaction which is external. This satisfaction is to be made for sins committed against your neighbor: for if you offend your neighbor and do him wrong, or take anything from him by fraud or violence, it is a great sin. For this, you can never be contrite if you do not make satisfaction, not only by confessing it, but by satisfying the desire of him who is offended, and that with sorrow. This is true doctrine, and shall never be overthrown by the spirits of false invention: which indeed is the first eye for the Devil. If you may offend your brother and be therefore accursed: how much more shall you be accursed when you offend the messenger of him who is your Father? Behold, he says not, "I have once done amiss." God be merciful to you, so that his mercies might be the greater upon you. Be mindful of my sayings.*

$\Delta$ May God have mercy on us and bless us; may He create a clean heart in us and put a right spirit within our hearts, Amen.

## Wednesday, June 26. 9:30 o'clock. In the presence of Lord Albert Lasky.

$\Delta$ As we were together in my study, and I was standing at my desk, there appeared to Edward Kelley a round globe of white smoke over my head. Thereupon I perceived the presence of some good spiritual creature, and straight away appeared the good angel I. L.

<margin>As he utters each word, he vomits flame from his mouth.</margin>
<margin>Note. Concerning sublunary spirits. Where the good angels have their seats.</margin>
<margin>The beginning of the destruction of almost all. The ruin of the Turkish Empire.</margin>
Mag. ..... *Hear, because I am just and true (says the Lord); Do not undertake anything impious, wicked, or unjust: For whatever evils you have done, whether by negligence, ignorance, contempt, or even too much superstition, are (as it is written) delivered by power to lying spirits, so that they might trouble the good while they afflict the evil. But God said (I am indeed your God) who does not take the Holy Spirit from you: For you are those whom I will confirm through my power: Do not therefore become wicked magicians with the perverse, who vainly ascribe my power to the things and idols of this world. But believe perseveringly even to the end and have faith: because (through me) the seal overcomes all worldly things and will subject demons to your will. The demons remaining below the regions, enclosed within the lunar spheres, are not my angels: but the heavenly ones are holy and truly good. Are you not men and mortals and not without sin, to whom I permitted free will, and at the same time to sin: so that by understanding evil from then on, you might acknowledge me as your God. Hear therefore, hear my sons, ..... I predict the calamity of the whole earth and of all living things. There will be horrendous and most sad wars everywhere, and the Earth will perish by sword and famine even to the third part. There will be slaughters of many, the destruction of (almost all) Princes, earthquakes such as have not been since the beginning of the world; the ruin of the empire of the terrestrial Demon (namely the Turk). For I have so ordained.*

[E. K.] **Now he looks at you.**

$\Delta$. *A. L. and I were in my Oratory.*

*Stephen, the Pole, miserably slaughtered in war, shall fall. Again I say: Stephen, King of Poland, miserably slaughtered in war, shall fall. The Princes shall call you again [he looks at Albert Lasky] to the Kingdom: whom I also shall appoint as Duke and King of Poland, Moldavia, and my people. Then you shall reach the desired goal and you shall not miss the mark. Because I am your God, and I will teach you useful and true things. And I will give you my angels as helpers and companions even to any secret of the world. Watch, pray. Therefore, be pious, until my power shall come both in you and upon you. Meanwhile, seal up what you have seen, and do not bring me into public.*

<margin>Do not bring into public.</margin>
[E. K.] Now he shakes: he seems to turn his head about his shoulders.

E. K. **Now he takes a sword and strikes the clouds, and forms a cross before him, on both sides and behind him. Believe me, it is the end of things: Your sins are forgiven.**

*E. K. He falls, as if distracted (or separating himself) into 4 parts, and flies away.*

Voice. ...... *You have those things that were so decreed.*

$\Delta$. *May the mercy of God be upon us now and always. Amen.*

# A true Relation of Dr. Dee his Actions with spirits, &c.

$\Delta$. Blessed be God, our Father, the God of all consolation, who has looked upon the affliction of his little servant, and in the very moment of my necessity provided help for me; he alone is the searcher of the heart and mind. He is my Light, my Helper, and my Protector. In the Lord I have hoped, and he delivered me from the greatest distress for the glory of his Name, which be exalted and magnified now, and for evermore. *Amen, Amen, Amen.*

<margin>
Fifty pounds yearly to be provided for E. K. by John Dee.
</margin>
$\Delta$. My heart throbbed many times today, and I thought that E. K. intended to absent himself from me, and now upon this warning I was confirmed and more assured that it was so. Whereupon, seeing him make such haste to ride to *Islington*, I asked him why he so hurried to ride there. And I said, if it were to ride to Mr. *Harry Lee*, I would go there also to be acquainted with him, seeing now I had such good leisure, being eased of the book writing. Then he said that someone told him the other day that the Duke only flattered him, and told him other things, both against the Duke (or Palatine) and me, etc. I answered for the Duke and myself; and also said that if the forty-pound annuity which Mr. *Lee* offered him was the chief cause of his mind settling that way (contrary to many of his former promises to me), then I would guarantee him fifty pounds yearly, and would do my best by following my suit to bring it to pass as soon as I possibly could; and thereupon I made him promise upon the Bible. Then E. K. again upon the same Bible swore to me constant friendship, and never to forsake me. And moreover he said that unless this had so fallen out, he would have gone beyond the seas, taking a ship at *Newcastle* within the next eight days. And so we pledged our faith to each other, taking each other by the hand upon these points of brotherly and friendly fidelity during life, which Covenant I beseech God to turn to his honor, glory, and service, and the comfort of our brethren (his children) here on earth.

->Tuesday, July 2. In the afternoon, around 2 o'clock.<-

$\Delta$. While I was writing letters to Mr. *Adrian Gilbert* in *Devonshire*, Madini appeared by me in the study before E. K., who was sitting in the chair; she was first on the ground, then higher in the air. And I said, "How is the mind of Mr. *Secretary* toward me? I think it is marvelously alienated."

<margin>
The Lord Treasurer and Secretary Walsingham.
</margin>
*Mad.* .... *Those that love the world are hated by God.* The Lord Treasurer and he are joined together, and they hate you. *I heard them when they both said you would go mad shortly: assure yourself of whatever they can do against you.* They will shortly lay a bait for you; but avoid them.

$\Delta$. Lord have mercy upon me: what bait (I beseech you) and by whom?

*Mad.* .... They have determined to search your house. But they are waiting until the Duke is gone.

$\Delta$. What would they search it for?

*Mad.* .... They hate the Duke (both of them) unto death.

$\Delta$. And why?

*Mad.* .... Take heed that you deal uprightly. .... [She spoke to E. K.]

**E. K. God the Creator be my witness of my upright dealing with and toward him (meaning $\Delta$) ever since my last coming to him.**

<margin>
E. K.’s second oath.
</margin>
*Mad.* .... It is good to prevent diseases.

**E. K. By this book (taking the Bible in his hand), I swear that I carry as faithful a mind to him as any man can, ever since my last coming.**

*Mad.* .... Look into the kind of people about the Duke: and the manner of their diligence.

$\Delta$. What do you mean by that? His own people, do you mean? Or who?

*Mad.* .... The spies.

$\Delta$. Which are those?

*Mad.* .... All of them; there is not one true.

$\Delta$. You mean the *English* men.

*Mad.* .... You are very dense if you do not understand my sayings.

$\Delta$. Lord, what is your counsel to prevent it all?

*Mad.* .... The speech is general: The wicked shall not prevail.

$\Delta$. But will they enter to search my house, or not?

*Mad.* .... Immediately after the Duke's going, they will.

$\Delta$. To what intent? What do they hope to find?

*Mad.* .... They suspect the Duke is inwardly a traitor.

$\Delta$. They can by no means charge me—no, not so much as with a traitorous thought.

<margin>
Trust them not.
</margin>
*Mad.* .... Though your thoughts be good, they cannot comprehend the doings of the wicked. In sum, they hate you. Trust them not; they shall go about shortly to offer you friendship. But be a worm in a heap of straw.

$\Delta$. I pray you, explain that parable.

# A true Relation of Dr. Dee his Actions with spirits, &c.

Mad..... *No matter how great a heap of straw is, it is no weight upon a worm, yet every straw hinders the worm's passage. See them, and be not seen by them; do you understand it?*

$\Delta$. I pray you, make your counsel more plain.

Mad..... *My counsel is plain enough.*

$\Delta$. When, I pray you, is the Duke likely to leave?

Mad..... *In the middle of August.*

$\Delta$. If he will go in the middle of August, and our practices are still underway then, what shall be done with the furniture that is prepared and standing in the Chamber of Practice?

Mad..... *You have no faith.*

<margin>A. L. Service.</margin>
*His departure depends upon the determined purpose of God. He is greatly your friend and intends to do much for you. He is prepared to do you good, and you are prepared to do him service. Many men have purposes, but only one sets them in order.*

$\Delta$. Concerning Adrian Gilbert, what does it please you to say of him and his intended voyage?

Mad..... *He is not in the true faith.*

$\Delta$. How has it been said, then, that he should be the one to set forth God’s faith and religion among the infidels?

Mad..... *That is a mystery.*

$\Delta$. Would it be good for the Duke to visit here often, or should he stay for the most part at his house in London?

Mad..... *Human policy cannot prevail. As many as are not faithful in these causes shall die a most miserable death and shall drink of everlasting sleep. As there are many divisions in one root, so there are many separations in the stem and branches.*

$\Delta$. Give some more light (I beseech you) to the particular understanding.

<margin>The heart.</margin>
Mad..... *The fire that kindles all these, and in which they live, is One, forming them according to whatever substance they are grounded upon. So by the lesser you may prove the greater: that as in particulars, so likewise generally, all emanations are from one. In the first workmanship, it lies secret in one unknown; it is sealed, and therefore it has an end. The Sun through the circles and massive body, the heart in the body, the intelligence in the inward man—the Sun from its own center spreads out the beams of its limited virtue. The heart gives life to two, and yet it is the center of life to the whole body; understanding quickens the mind; that is the mind I speak of. The mind puts on a fiery shape. It follows, therefore, that everything (of whatever substance) has a center, from which the circumfluent beams of its proper power proceed. When these are perfectly known, then things are seen in their true kind. I say this to prove that the good angel of man, which is the external center of the soul, carries with him the internal character of that thing of which he seeks to be a dignifier; within which lies secret the conjunction and separation of the proportion of their times between the soul and body of man. Oh, happy (therefore) is that soul which beholds the glory of its dignification and is a partaker with him who is its keeper. If men knew this, the thickness of the earth would not hinder their speech, nor could the darkness of the lowest air obscure or darken the sharpness of their eyes. This character (at his next coming here) shall be made manifest to him.*

**E. K. He shows a bloody hand, holding a bloody cross with letters on it, like our holy letters.**

$\Delta$. I beseech you, how shall his provision of money from home serve his turn, or how shall he have help here to bear his expenses?

<margin>Note the form of a child.</margin>
Mad..... *Your words make me a child. Those who fish for dolphins do not stand upon the ground. Those who sit in counsel do not call in the harvest people, nor do they account for their works. He who stands above the moon sees greater things than the earth. Is it not said, "The Lord will provide"? I stand above the moon, for I dispose of his life from above the disposition of the moon. To ask what Jacob's servants did was a folly because their master was blessed; it is a greater question to ask how blessed he was than to ask how many sheep he had.*

$\Delta$. I am desirous to know what you meant by saying that my words made you a child.

<margin>Reverence to good angels. Divine pact. Perhaps enameled.</margin>
Mad..... *Because you ask me childish questions. His good angel shall reveal his character to him, and you shall see it [pointing to E. K.]. But take heed that you speak truly, and use great reverence, or else the feet that love you shall carry your carcass out of the doors. If he carries it upon him, it shall be a token of the covenant between him and God.*

$\Delta$. Do you mean the image or likeness of it made in pure gold?

Mad.. .. Yes. .... *So those who see his standards with that sign in them shall perish utterly.*

$\Delta$. You mean if the same is painted or otherwise wrought in his banners and pennons, etc.

Mad.. .. *Let him use it as a covenant between God and him.*

$\Delta$. How shall he frame it in gold: as a solid piece, or in the form of a thin plate?

Madd. .... *His own angel shall reveal it.*

$\Delta$. Because it has been said that at the beginning of our country's troubles we should be leaving from here for his country; what sign shall we have of that time approaching, or being at hand?

Mad. ...... Your watchword was told to you before: *When it is said to you*, Come, etc.

Mad. ...... *Miraculous is your care (O God) for those who are your chosen, and wonderful are the ways that you have prepared for them. You shall take them from the fields and shelter them at home. You are merciful to your faithful and harsh to the heavy-hearted. You shall cover their legs with boots, and brambles shall not prick them. Their hands shall be covered with the skins of beasts so that they may break their way through the hedges. Your Bell shall go before them as a watch and sure direction. The moon shall be clear so that they may go on boldly. Peace be among you.*

E. K. He has now gone away in a fire.

### Thursday July 4. 11:00 AM. 1583.

Note. $\Delta$. When I came home yesterday from the Court, from London, and from Lord Laski, I found that E. K. intended to ride out of town and planned to be away (as he explicitly told me) for five days. Certain companions and acquaintances of his had made these plans with him, some waiting for him in Mortlake and some in Brainford (as was realized later today, and as he confessed to me). Because of this, I thought it good to inform Lord Laski, who intended to come and refresh himself at my house as he used to do before, either today or within two or three days. He also delighted in E. K.’s company, etc. Therefore, around the time of E. K.’s rising, I wrote these lines, intending to send them immediately to Lord Laski, so that word might be returned of his intent before E. K. should ride—I intending and hoping to persuade E. K. to stay that long for that reason.

*Most Noble Prince, upon my return I found our Edward with a cheerful face, yet preparing himself for a journey of, as he says, five days. He strives to depart or begin that journey this morning, intending to return (as he claims) after five days. What the truth itself is, He knows who is our true and Almighty God. I wanted to signify this to you early this morning, so that you might consider what is best to do. Concerning other matters, in their own time,*

->Your Highness's most faithful client,<-
->John Dee.<-
->July 4, 1583.<-

This letter having been written and not yet folded, my friend E. K. was ready and came out of his chamber into my study. I told him that I was just now sending word to Prince Laski of his riding out and return after five days, and so I showed him the letter. When he came to the phrase, *What the truth itself is*, he was somewhat offended, saying, "What secret meaning does this have, based on some of your two former conferences?" "Truly," I said, "only such as the context of the letter implies; that is, since you said you intended to return within five days, or at that time, it is uncertain whether you will or shall return later or sooner; and therefore *What the truth itself is* of your return, or intent to return, only God knows." He would by no means accept my sincere explanation but seemed suspicious of other improper interpretations of those former words. Thereupon I took the letter and tore it into three pieces and sent none. But in my mind, I referred everything to God’s disposition, assuring myself of God’s most constant proceeding in His own affairs. Shortly after, E. K. said to me, "Certainly there is a spiritual creature on my right shoulder who clearly says to me, 'Come away.'" "So," I said, "did one say to Sowle, when

And therefore, if I were offered a thousand pounds to stay, yes, even a kingdom, I cannot. Therefore I release you of your promise of a 50-pound yearly stipend to me; you need not doubt that God will defend you and prosper you, and can raise up children to Abraham from the very stones. And again, I cannot abide my wife; I do not love her—nay, I abhor her—and there in the house I am disliked because I do not favor her more." To these words of his, spoken in great pangs and disquiet of mind, I replied and said that these doings and sayings of his were not of God, and that by my whole proceeding he might perceive what confidence I placed in his dealing with the spirits, our friends, seeing that even to the last penny (and more than my ability conveniently allowed) I still laid out funds for the ...ning of such things as were to be done by me, etc. Well, suddenly, down he went, onto his mare, and rode away toward Brainford.

Brentford. After his departure, my wife came up into my study, and I said, *Jane*, this man is marvelously unsettled against his wife, because of her friends' bitter reports against him behind his back, and her silence regarding them, etc. "He is gone," I said, "but I pray to Almighty God to guide him and to defend him from danger and shame; I do not doubt that God will be merciful to him and bring him at length to such order that he shall be a faithful servant to God," etc.

Note that within three hours afterward, E. K. came up my study stairs without his boots, for he had come in a boat from Brentford. When I saw him, I was inwardly very glad; but I continued writing those records that I still had to write concerning last Tuesday's actions. "I have lent my mare out," he said, "and so I have returned." "It is well done," I said, and thereupon he sat down in the chair by my table where he was accustomed to sit; and it was ten o'clock then. He took up in his hand the books which I had brought from *London* regarding Lord Laski, written to him in his praise, etc. And as he was looking earnestly at them, a spiritual creature struck the book on the outside of the parchment cover several times, and once tried to take it out of his hands. I heard the strikes myself several times. At length he said, "I see the handsome maiden *Madimi* here, and have for a good while." Then I said to him, "Why did you tell me no sooner?" # THE FIRST BOOK OF TRAVEL:

->Namely<-

->From *Mortlake, England*,<-
->To *Krakow, Poland*.<-

---

->Saturday, *September* 21, 1583. *St. Matthias' Day*.<-

We departed from *Mortlake* about three o'clock in the afternoon: *Lord Albert Lasky* (*Voivode of Sieradz*, in *Poland*) met me on the water, as we had appointed. And so we reached *London* by night; and in the dead of the night, by wherries, we went to *Greenwich* to the house of my friend *Goodman Fern*, the *potter*. There we refreshed ourselves, and a great tilt-boat came from *Gravesend* to take us in (by the appointment of myself and *Mr. Stanley*) to go to our ships, which we had stationed seven or eight miles beyond *Gravesend*. We reached these ships on Sunday morning by sunrise. In the larger of them (being a double fly-boat from *Denmark*), my *Lord Lasky*, I, and *E. K.*, with my wife and children, etc., went. In another ship (also hired by me for this passage), some of my Lord’s men, two horses, etc., went; that ship was a *boier*, a pretty ship. With little wind, we immediately hoisted sail and began our voyage in the ship.

<margin>A great raging wind arose, almost from the Northeast.</margin>
This 22nd day, we were in great danger of perishing on the sands called the Spits about midnight. Due to contrary winds, we had anchored near them, and the anchor dragged without anyone noticing until the ship was ready to strike the sands. Then, through great diligence and strategy used by our mariners in hoisting sail and cutting our cable (leaving our sheet anchor behind), and committing ourselves into the hands of God and most earnestly praying for a favorable wind, it pleased the Almighty and most merciful God to suddenly change the wind. This allowed us to pull away from the sands and recover our position back at *Queenborough*.

<margin>The clear help of God at the very moment of deadly danger.</margin>
The 23rd day (being Monday), we came to the mouth and entrance of *Queenborough Creek*, or Haven. As we made for land in small fisher-boats—*Lord Lasky*, my wife, and children in one boat, and I, with *E. K.*, *Mary*, *Elizabeth*, and *John Crocker* in another—it happened that at the ship's side, our fisher-boat’s sail-yard and sail became entangled on the main-yard of the *fly-boat* (which had been lowered). So, as we set off from the ship's side, with the top of our boat fastened above and the winds and current carrying the boat off below, it tilted so much to one side that nearly half of the fisher-boat was in the water. The water rushed in so quickly (due to the entanglement mentioned before, which was not easily undone or loosened) that my Lord, my wife, and everyone who saw us thought our boat must necessarily sink and that we would perish. But God in His providence and mercy had greater care for us, so that we became clear. The boat was half full of water, so that we sat wet to our knees, and the waves of the sea continued to beat in more and more. In the midst of this trouble, one of our two boatmen lost his long oar overboard into the water. So, not only did we lack the help of that oar, but because they tried to follow the wind and ebb to recover it (contrary to our course and unable to reach it), we were forced with much difficulty to use the sail, our one remaining oar, and the rudder to make such shift as we could to reach *Queenborough* town. In the meantime, *E. K.* emptied most of the water out of the boat with a great gauntlet; otherwise, by all human reasoning, it must have sunk. At length (to be brief), we came to the town side, up the crooked creek. When the master of our ship tried to lift me out in his arms (standing in the water in his boots), he fell with me, and I was covered in filth from the water and ooze. God be praised forever that all that great danger ended with so little grief or hurt.

->At *Queenborough*.<-

---

->*Wednesday, September 25. About 3:00 in the afternoon, at high tide.*<-

Δ. We prayed to God and implored His help; a curtain immediately appeared. I prayed again alone for help in a time of necessity. A figure six feet tall appeared in the air, as if on the other side of a cloud placed between *E. K.* and him.

**E. K.** I know him.

..... *You have cause to know me, and Him who sent me, or you would not be living now.*

**E. K.** It seems to be Michael.

Δ. We give thanks to our Creator, who has sent his good, powerful, and faithful minister for our protection in our time of need.

> Michael: I speak of three things: of myself and him who sent me; of you, regarding what you are; and of the service of God that is to come. O you powers of Heaven and Earth, gather yourselves together, look upon your God: Consider his benefits; has he not bound you together? And linked you together in himself? Are you not glorified regarding your office, to which you were powerfully assigned, by the will of him who glorifies himself? Behold how you have surrendered yourselves to the prince of darkness: or why do your princes strive against the Most High? And you gather yourselves together to contend against him who is most powerful—or would you seek to subjugate him whose weapons are above all strength? How do you dare to contend with his strength? Or what is the cause that you wish to be so impious? But it must be so: because he has sealed the <margin>Government.</margin> government to you, and into your hands he gave the vial of destruction. But give way to your end: because in his strength you shall be scattered: and your gates must be opened to the conclusion of all things. Let the servants of God not marvel at the strength of temptation: for great is the power of the impious and gaping Lion when it is handed to him with a seal. Do not be indignant; at this hour, I know your government through him. Behold, the key of justice is opened to me. Nevertheless, your iniquity shall yet be greater, and your kingdom shall be scattered in his powerful pride. How great is Satan who resists the strength of God? How great, therefore, must be your humility, which must either overcome or die. But to you the Lord says: Let the winds open their mouths, and the raging deep waters and <margin>Let the thunderbolts strike. Michael. Gabriel.</margin> powerful throats. Into all parts of your ships. Let the earth open its mouth and say that it wishes to devour. Yet they shall not prevail: For to you (says the Lord) who are my strength, I will add my prevailing power: And you shall be two flames of fire; indeed, a powerful fire suffocating the mouth of all malice. Therefore, let it be well with you: Because the enemy is strongest where the prize is greatest. Remember that you are men. Remember that you are earth. Remember that you are sinners. Remember what you were, and do not forget what you are. For in him you live, who has all things in his subjection. But he who is with him, crucified for glory, <margin>Has provided for you. The end of our service.</margin> must, in the midst of mortality, prepare himself for immortal power. The servants of God have always prevailed, but always through adversities. He who is not of this world has prepared you; nonetheless, you must fulfill those things which he himself has provided. That the world may be made new, and <margin>Enfolded.</margin> he himself be acknowledged. Powerful is he; powerful is that eagle which covers the great mountain with its wings. But more powerful is the strength of him who numbers the stars and gathers the mountains: for whatever he speaks is the fire of truth: and is at once Power and Action, in immediate proportion. Even he who made the world joined man together and worked all things, himself being all things. It is he who gave the command to you: and I say to you, look from point to point, to the middle of Heaven, and through the circle of the earth: consider all things in one, and one in all things. Weigh them, whether they be numbered by reason or measured as Solomon did, or as was granted to Adam (which you cannot do now, but you shall do): Then conclude: all things observe their course: but the word of the Lord is an eternal thing... Love God because he is just. Love one another because you are... justified. Observe the commandment of God because it is the measure of justice.

**E. K.** *Now another comes to him, with a crown on his head, as if... and he takes the sword of Michael.*

> The Crowned One: Behold, great is the strength of God, and it shall prevail.

Michael: Therefore blessed be God; you are justified and we are sanctified.

**E. K.** *Now they made the sign of the cross with flames three times. And if our sailor returns from London today with a new anchor, is it not the plan that we sail from here immediately, if he so wills, etc.?*

**E. K.** *They return.*

> The Crowned One: I am from Heaven: I do not look upon the earth; nonetheless, the earth lives through the Heavens. <margin>Of worldlings.</margin> Follow the course of earthly things. Prepare the seed; we wish (O Lord) to be ready in you, with the increase. Your worry cannot prevail, because your enemies are strong: but why am I disgraced with the salt of earthly vanities? Let one vanity destroy another: but the Elect shall prevail in strength against that Prince of Vanity and King of all fools. Because our God is wise, his judgments are inscrutable, and his patience is immeasurable. You work, and we will govern.

**E. K.** *Now they withdraw.*

Voice: Do not dispute further with God: your victory shall be.

Δ. May the name of our God, the only almighty and best, be magnified. Amen.

*Friday, September 27: We sailed from Queenborough, and so by the land's end into the open sea, Northeast.*

*Saturday, September 28: We reached the Holland coast, and none of our mariners, neither the Master nor the Pilot, knew the coast. Therefore, we returned to the open sea with great fear and danger, because we could scarcely get away from that dangerous coast; the wind was so unfavorable for that purpose.*
*Sunday, September 29: We came into the Briel harbor, and there we were likely to run aground. At length we came to an anchor and remained in the ship all night.*
*Monday, September 30: We landed and went into the Briel.*

->At Briel, October 2. At 9 in the morning, Wednesday.<-

**E. K.** Nothing appears in the stone, nor the curtain, nor anything else. Let us pray constantly, etc. A large house appears with many pinnacles, very elegant. And the pavement seems to be distinguished by many inlaid stones, and there appear to be many steps by which one ascends. There seems to be a green courtyard on the right side, and a valley on the other side, and a stream on another. The part that faces the sun seems as if it were newly renovated. And around the entrance is a certain round building; the windows are not like ours, but as if they were temple windows.

**A. L.** Said that it seems to be that royal castle which is in Kraków.

**E. K.** Suddenly fire descends and appears throughout the stone. Now the usual curtain comes before that house.

What God does, he does not share with human judgment. Behold, now he has gathered his disciples and teaches them. O Heaven and earth, how great are the miseries that will vex and pollute the other? For the good angels will fall with him, and the Heavens shall fear Christ. But they shall fall for a time, not forever.

**Δ.** Saving the judgment of the Orthodox Catholic Church, it seems to me that Job prophesied about this kind of fear of the angels—either their fall and restoration, or their purging—in Chapter 41, where he also adds regarding his miracles: *Under him were the sun's rays, and he shall spread gold for himself like mud.* Before he had said: *When he is raised up, the angels shall fear, and being terrified they shall be purged, etc.*

**Δ.** O God, how terrible that time will be, etc.

**Δ.** What is this?

**Jub.** ...... Joy in true wisdom.

**Jub.** ...... This is our Manna, by which we are fed. But I am sanctified through Creation, Institution, and by the Divine will. **E. K.** Now they fly away headlong, as if falling downward.

**Jub.** ...... Beware of the straw: because if set on fire, it burns down the whole house.

*Thursday, October 3.* We came from Briel to Rotterdam in a hoy <note>a small coastal sloop</note> of *Amsterdam* to go inland; here we lay all night.

*Friday, October 4.* We came to *Gouda* at 3 o'clock in the afternoon: where we lay inside the town in the ship.

*Saturday, October 5.* We came by *Haarlem* to *Amsterdam*, and lay before the town all night in the ship.

*Tuesday, October 8.* We sailed from *Amsterdam* to *Enkhuizen*, and Edmund Hilton went with my goods by sea toward *Gdańsk*.

*Wednesday, October 9.* We set off from *Enkhuizen* early: but by reason of a contrary wind, we came very late to *Harlingen*.

*Friday, October 11.* We went inland in little schuyts <note>small flat-bottomed boats</note> from *Harlingen* (by *Franeker*) to *Leeuwarden*.

*Saturday, October 12.* From *Leeuwarden*, we came to *Dokkum* (in small boats) about 3 o'clock in the afternoon.

**$\Delta$.** For a long time the crystal appeared like a very black stone. At length, within that very blackness of the stone, there appeared a naked man crucified on a cross: yet he was not dead. ->Sunday *at 2 o'clock in the afternoon, Oct. 13.*<-
Gab. ...... *And by this I teach you, that those afflictions which you suffer in soul, either for your offenses toward God or for the imperfections of your minds, being void of brotherly charity toward your neighbors (and so from you generally hereafter, however great or many they may be), ought not to be manifested or made open to the world: but perfectly shadowed in charity, bearing your own infirmities, and so the infirmity of others with a quiet and hidden mind. For the anguish of the soul is compared with prayer, dwelling in one house which ought to laugh with the world and weep toward heaven. For every sin is noted, and the least thing among the celestial bodies as well as the terrestrial is perfectly considered. For sin has its end, and its end is punishment. And so, conversely of virtue, wisdom (in the twenty-first <unclear>Ent ... ie</unclear> or <unclear>L...</unclear>), its ground is upon mildness, which mildness purifies the body and exalts the soul, making it apt and ready to behold the heavens, receive glorious illuminations, and finally brings the soul to participate with us, not in earthly, but in everlasting wisdom. The Son of God was sanctified in his flesh through mildness and was not of this world, because he was the mildness of his Father. Therefore, be meek: be fervent in meekness. Then you shall take up that cross which Christ spoke of, following him; which cross is the compassion in mildness over your brothers, for sin's sake: not as worldlings do, looking but not lamenting. The other part is in suffering mildly the afflictions of the world and flesh; hereby you become martyrs because you mortify yourselves, which is true martyrdom. He who forsakes the world for the love of God, in his Son Christ, shall have his reward. But he who forsakes himself shall be crowned with a diadem of glory. Thus says the Lord: I am jealous over you, because you have vowed yourselves to me. But great are the temptations of the flesh, and mighty is its strength where the spirit is weak.*

# A true Relation of Dr. Dee his Actions with Spirits, &c.

*But thus says God: It is better to fill up the Soul with heavenly contemplation and celestial food, to reign in heaven, and to be beloved by him, than to pamper the filthy flesh, whose delight destroys both body and Soul. It is written: He who does not bridle his flesh is given to riotousness, which is the sleep of death and the slumber to destruction. But this is true abstinence: when, despising the world, you flee the delight within it, refraining from pleasures of the body, tempering the flesh and making it weak—and that for the Lord's sake. For the flesh and spirit do not rejoice at once. Neither can the full belly groan out true prayers. Feed, therefore, the Soul with the love of our society. And bridle your flesh, for it is insolent. One thing, I say: look to your servants. See that in one house there do not dwell those who delight in virtue and holiness mingled with such as harbor vice upon vice, whose drunkenness is an abomination, and whose diet stirs up fornication. For wickedness is among them, and they do not fear God; neither do they abstain according to what the Holy Ghost has taught through his Church. Make them clean; then you shall feel our presence among you. And we will all of us defend you from the rage of wickedness. We delight in the God of truth and in the worshippers of Justice. Thus says the Holy Ghost: Lo, I have made for myself a Tabernacle, where the God of Gods reigns in Justice. And I will sanctify those places which rejoice in charity. Mingle, therefore, your alms with charity. And let your prayers and fasting be mingled with deeds of alms. For he who prays and fasts without mercy is a liar. Moreover, let your friendship be such as is of charity and not of this world—neither for the world's sake, but for the service of God. All other friendship is vain and of no account. Charity is the gift of the Holy Ghost, which Holy Ghost is a kindling fire, knitting things together through Christ Jesus in the true wisdom of the Father. This fire is of no small account, nor to be reckoned as the Heathens have done. For happy are those who are fed with charity, for it is the meat of us who are anointed, which is the Son of God and the light of the world.*

$\Delta$ Is charity the Son of God?

*Gab. ...... It is so: He who walks in charity walks in God; for charity is the will of the Father, is his own delight, and the illumination of the faithful through his Holy Spirit. The charity of the Church is the Holy Ghost. But he who dwells in charity dwells in the blood of the Lamb, which is the will of the Father, which is the Holy Ghost. Blessed are those who dwell in charity. Persevere to the end—not negligently, but with good will, which good will is called fear. This fear is the beginning of wisdom, the first step into rest.*

<margin>The end crowns the work.</margin>
*He who continues to the end receives his reward, but he who leaves off is a damned Soul. Many men begin, but few end. Neither is your justification by the beginning, but from the end. Paul was justified because he died the servant of God, and not for his preaching's sake. He who dwells to the end is the Child of God, inheritor of everlasting life, and equal with joy himself—not the joy of joys, but that joy which God has made equal with the joys of his son Christ, in the company of the faithful. Even in this place, many persons had conspired against you. But the strength of God has sealed them, and they shall not go unpunished. For the Angel of the Town is sealed, and his seal is for destruction; thrice cursed are those who dwell within his government. But you are safe and shall be safely delivered from them.*

<margin>England.</margin>
*In England, they condemn your actions and say you are a renegade. For they say you have despised your Prince.*

<margin>
England.
$\Delta$ The destruction of Dockum was granted to me if I desired it, etc.
</margin>
*What would you know of them? Cease until you hear the number of their destruction. Desire whatever plague you will (says the Lord) upon this people for their ungratefulness, and they shall be afflicted. For the Lord is angry with them, and he says: You judge this wicked people, their Town, Men, Women, and Children; and it shall be seen that the Lord, the God of Heaven and Earth, has mercy on you.*

$\Delta$ Not our will, but God’s be done, to the praise and honor of his name.

*Gab. ...... Command the fires to fly from Heaven and consume them, and it shall be done; or say, "Let the Earth swallow them," and they shall perish. For I have made Heaven and Earth (says the Lord), and Justice is for my people. I am a flaming fire among you and the Rod of Justice. It is said: Lift up your hands, and you shall be heard. The peace of him who is the spirit of wisdom inflame your minds with love and charity, and grant you continuance to his glory.*

Tuesday, Oct. 15. We made a difficult shift to get from *Dockum* to *Angem* by sunset.

Thursday, Oct. 17. We came from *Angem* to *Embden*, going outside the Islands and coming in at *Wester Emb*. We arrived before the Town by six o'clock in the afternoon, but could not get in at the Gates; therefore, we lay all night on board the ship, but my Lord *A. L.* went over to the lodging on the other shore.

Friday, Oct. 18. We came into the Town. My Lord stayed at the White *Swan* toward the water-side, and I and *E. K.* with my children and many others stayed at the Three Golden *Keys*, by the *English* house.

Sunday, Oct. 20. This day morning about eight o'clock, we went in a little hoy from *Embden*.

# A true Relation of Dr. Dee his Actions with spirits, &c.

*From Embden <note>Emden</note> toward Lyre <note>Leer</note>, my Lord stayed at Embden. We arrived late at Lyre: and that same night we went from there in a smaller boat (scute) by way of Styk-husen <note>Stickhausen</note> to Oppen <note>Apen</note>.*
*Monday, October 21. By nine o'clock in the morning we came to Oppen: a very simple village, and from there we went straight to Oldenburgh <note>Oldenburg</note>.*
*Tuesday, October 22. From Oldenburgh, by way of Delmenhurst, to Breame <note>Bremen</note>: and were lodged at an old widow's house, at the sign of the Crown.*

Saturday, *October* 26. *At 12:00, namely at noon.* At *Breame.*

$\Delta.$ Lord Albert Laskie, staying at Styk-husen behind us with Earl John of Embden and Friesland, etc.
**E. K. The curtain seems to be far back in the stone, and the stone is clear between the curtain and the front part. Under the curtain, I see the legs of men up to the knees.**
$\Delta.$ Then someone appeared and said:
Il. ...... *Make room for an actor! Jesus, who would have thought I would have met you here?*
**E. K. He is in ragged clothing from the waist <note>girdlestead</note> down, but above he has a white satin jerkin.**
$\Delta.$ By the mercies of God, we are here; and by your will and nature, and the power of God, you are here.
Il. ...... *Tush, do not doubt me, for I am I. L.*
**E. K. It seems to me that the seriousness of this action requires a more serious manner and more serious speech. Bear with me, though I say so to you.**
Il. ...... *If I must bear with you for speaking foolishly—you who are but flesh and speak from your own wisdom—how much more should you be satisfied with my manner? It is appointed by him who does not regard the outward form, but the fulfillment of his will and the keeping of his commandments. That is God, whose wisdom is foolishness to the world, but to those who fear him, it is an everlasting joy mixed with gladness and a comfort of life hereafter; sharing infallible joys with him who is all comeliness and beauty. What do you say to this, Sir, ha?*
**E. K. He turns his heels up at E. K.**
**E. K. I do not understand your words, because I only repeat <note>repent</note> your sayings.**
Il. ...... *It is the duty of a servant to do this; the duty of one who watches is to look at what he sees. For the greatest point of wisdom is to reverently consider your calling. It is said, "Do that which is appointed," for he who does more is not a true servant.*
**E. K. How can that be?**
Il. ...... *Speak when your time comes. Sir, here is money, but I got it with great difficulty. Bear with me, for I can help you with no more. Come on, Andras; where are you, Andras?*
**E. K. Now a young man in a gown comes to him. The gown is plain, like a London apprentice's.**
Il. ..... *Did I not tell you to go there and fetch me money?*
Andras .... *Where?*
Il. .... *This is one of those who forget their business as soon as it is told to them.*
And. ...... *Sir, I went halfway.*
Il. ..... *And what then? Speak on, speak on.*
And. ...... *Then, being somewhat weary, I stopped—the more so because I met my friends. On the third day I arrived there, but I did not find him at home. His family told me that he had just gone out.*
Il. ..... *And you returned a fool. Well, this is how it is: I placed you above my servants and did what I could to promote you, and I endeavored daily to make you a free man. But I am rewarded with loitering, and I have raised an idle person. Go your way; I will deliver you to the officer. The officer shall deliver you to the prison, and there you shall be rewarded. For those who do what they are commanded deserve freedom; but to those who loiter, and to those who are idle, vengeance and hunger belong.*
**E. K. He takes him by the arm and delivers him to a man with a staff in his hand, and he puts him in through a door.**

Il. ...... Judge my words with reason, and you shall find them true; touch them with understanding, and you shall find them profound. My words are true, because I am sent by Truth: neither are we to speak gravely when we take upon ourselves the personas of buyers and sellers. Whoever truly does the will of his Master in this world shall be laughed to scorn: but whoever speaks worldly and sends out shadows is accounted a pillar of the Earth. $\Delta$. In the name of Jesus, the King of Glory, are you not Aphlasben, my good angel, so assigned by the mercy and power of God?

E. K. He looks very ancient.

... *Empire, most high glory, and thanks, throughout all creatures, be unto you (O eternal God): first [creating], secondly redeeming, and thirdly sanctifying the world in its creation, now and forever; and as long as it shall be said Hosanna in the choir of the High God... Amen.*

... Manifold are the mercies of God toward man, whose baseness deserves no such grace and most unspeakable blessing. But such is God: he justifies himself in the strength of his mercy and upholds <note>beveth</note> his honor with his own holiness. For what is man, that he can justify himself? Or that has anything in which his heart <note>bowels</note> can rejoice? In what can he determine happiness for himself? Or how can he compare himself with the trees that are fruitful? *If the life of man is sin, then it is hateful. But who is he that hates it? Even he who is above, and is farthest from iniquity.* Great, therefore (O man), are your miseries, when naturally you are, and love to be, hated by God, whose service is justice and whose delight is peace. *Consider, therefore, the mercies of God, through his loving kindness toward your weakness. And acknowledge his power, which makes those strong who have no force of themselves. Do not gather up your own inventions, but be faithful servants, performing the will of him who sanctifies you with obedience. For from dust you have become flesh, and from flesh the servants of sin, so that at length you might be made free through your own consent in the mercies of him who has entered into your weakness and weighed out his blood for your redemption—even he who has paid the uttermost penny of your ransom. And why? Not with the intent that you should brag of yourselves, but he has charged as a condition that you should maintain justice in the works of righteousness. To whom is Heaven a seat, but to such as are faithful servants? In this, the dignity of your Master is known, of whom it is said, "Blessed are those who serve the God of Hosts." If anything now happens to you that is the riches of your Master, be thankful for it and consider his liberality. And the more he opens his treasures to you, be so much more thankful; for to such belongs the ownership of more, and the reward of those who are ten times faithful. Happy are those to whom it is said, "You good servant." Be no wanderers <note>Gadders</note>, for there is no house like the house of your Master. Take heed also, lest you administer his bread to such as are his enemies, and thus unworthy; for to both of these belongs the reward of unfaithfulness. Do not be high-minded when you borrow your riches, lest the moths enter in and corrupt your garments; for pride is the depth of sin... Cease not to rebuke the dishonorers... neither maintain the honor of any other. For he who entertains you has sealed you for others and has strengthened you with authority—the rod of his justice. Generally, these things have been spoken to you, and these lessons are not yet to be learned; but happy are those whom God sanctifies, being unholy, and ten times blessed are the temples in which his holiness dwells. It is true, as you say: generally men are sanctified—the people of the Earth through all nations, mystically—through the mercies of God. But where the sanctification does not agree with the thing sanctified, there wickedness enters. The Spirit of God is not sanctified in Hell, nor is his holy temple beautified with the feet of the unrighteous. It is written, "Dogs do not honor bread, nor do defiled places honor things that are holy." For as Hell dishonors Heaven in respect of unrighteousness, so those who are wicked dishonor the virtuous and such as are truly holy by their company; and they stink <note>sink</note> from their wickedness. For it is written, "And Satan went from the presence of the Lord, leaving a stench <note>sink</note> behind him." The light of the sun is taken from the Earth by the congealed cloud. The sins of the people and the filthiness of places are placed between virtue and sacramental things. Therefore, it is not true that you may lawfully call upon the name of God in unhallowed places.*

$\Delta$. I crave pardon for my ignorance and error in this; but I did not ask to know of the heavenly mysteries. I only demanded information on such things which were not only above human power to answer (and so might seem like worldly mysteries), but also the true good news of them might, in many ways, be a comfort to us and ours.

... *Behold, in Israel, the rough stones are acceptable altars, and the stinking caves have been known to the Lord. And why? Because the place was holy; neither this filthiness here, nor that of anything else created, hinders it. But it is the filthiness of the place and country in which they are defiled; for in pure places, the defiled are blessed. David sanctified Saul with the presence of his anointing, and his harp spoke the wonders of the Lord. We come to you here because the will of God shines in you; but the filthiness of this country obscures the beauty of our message. Not that it is obscured in us, but it is hindered through wick[edness]... from you. Therefore, flee the company of drunkards, and such as [waste?] <note>we...</note> their own understanding.*

[E. K. He holds up his face and hands toward heaven.]

... *Drunkards and such as defile themselves are apt to know worldly things, not as wise men*

> Disclose your long-swelling bellies, and upon the harlot earth,
> Seem fair to man, as when the waves, like a midwife, help their birth.
> Twice shall the sun cross the heavens, and once look a quarter of the way,
> And working strange worlds, build up a city where men say

> With secret shame defiled belies, a thing now sometimes common.
> From midnight until noon, two parts and more shall feel slaughter,
> And all the world from the south shall taste the full force of fire and steel.
<margin>2 1/2</margin>
> It is little wonder that the earth does not grieve at fighting shadows,
> When mighty seas shall dry up, and the heavens lie—who can live?
> That mortal eyes shall see a temple built with precious stones,
> Or strange creatures made new in sight from old and long-dried bones.
> Or angels dwell on earth: but I, whose fiery fingers can
> Unloose thrice-sealed books and utter worlds unknown to man,
> I see these cursed beings, whose borders lead your journey on,
> Shall within the thirtieth month be bought, or sold, or completely gone.
> And England shall perish first, with moths long harbored in her skirts,
> The Spaniards shall lose their king, and France shall rebel and fall by spirits.
> And the holy man shall be besieged at home for ten days by the whelps of these days,
> Until he is at length set free by the sudden force of virtue's help.
> The Polish King has played his part, and a friendly man shall then hold sway

> At last he shall wear the highest crown, if falling from virtue causes no loss,
> And in the midst of this coming turmoil, in the time of a newly arrived law for toss.
> Then lo, other times most holy shall come, and a kingdom shall
> Come from heaven and immediately call things to order again.

*Saturday, November 2: we rode from Bremen, two great miles to a nunnery called Osterholz.*
*Sunday, November 3: we came to Vörde (or Fureden).*
*Monday, November 4: we came to bed at Harburg.*
*Tuesday, November 5: we came to Buxtehude, and there by 9 o'clock in the morning we took to the water in two great barges or boats—horse-wagon, our equipment, and everything else—and ferried down the small river until we entered the Elbe, and so crossed straight over to Blankenese. There we dined, and after dinner, we came by coaches to Hamburg, where my Lord stayed at the English house and we at another lodging, a widow's house.*
*Wednesday, November 6: we rode to Trittau, four miles from Hamburg, a little village, having left*

$\Delta$. *...... The purity of humility, spread throughout the inner depths of man, is that which is called (among you) Perseverance. This Perseverance beautifies and establishes those things that are acceptable in the sight of God—the works of man—on a true and steadfast foundation. From this springs justification, which [unclear] with the love of God. In this you have become like us, because we are the image of Perseverance and the Glory of God. But in us it is dignified; in you it is, and must be, imperfect. For nothing of flesh or blood receives perfection.*

<margin>Our Calling or Exercise.</margin>
*The emanations from God, to and into his creatures (which meet at the center of the earth as the joining together of things), are established. So that not one bit of his Will can or may perish, grow weak, or dwell in error. This, foreseen from the beginning, carries within itself the memory of all things until the end. Through this mercy and memory, you have become the servants of God—not for your own sakes, but because it is the Glory of him who has called you to this exercise: troublesome to the world, but rewarded with Glory.*

*If therefore your imperfections rise up and resist the Will of God, saying blasphemously as you do, "Let us seek other ways," then you are not counted as those who persevere, nor are your works worthy of reward. But human reason can persuade and give judgment against these follies; how much more are they damnable and deserve correction in the voice and judgment of those who are pure.*

*He who deals with the wicked is a liar and shall have his reward. But the end of comfort is in the purity of spirit. But O you of little wisdom, you rise up against the winds and pit your wits against the mountains; indeed, you cast yourselves down headlong where there is no mercy. For what blasphemy is it to say, "If it be the will of God, it must follow"? Is not man subject to the contribution of his own labors? And are they not allowed for his comfort, once they are contributed?*

*The soul of man is the image of God, after his form, which keeps within itself the power of his divinity in the heavenly Spirit, by which he has authority to agree with God in the workmanship of his Will and creatures. This power, being already sealed, allows man (as king of himself) to consent to his own salvation, joining and knitting himself together either with perseverance in the assured hope of mercy, or (with willful drunkenness) to the reward of those who fall. Therefore, become holy. For the soul beautifies when it is beautified in itself. Resist not the Will of God, which is mighty upon you; be not obstinate.*

*Be humble; do not rejoice for this world, but be glad that your names are sealed and that you shall correct the world. Do not despair through weakness; for from whom does strength come? If puddles become seas, the end is more wonderful; but it is even greater when sinners are called to the knowledge and performance of God's Will through his mercies. Just as one day perishes and is no more, even though it once was, so it is and shall be the state of this world. For the earth must sing Hosanna <note>O Sanna</note> with the heavens, and there must be one truth. And Jerusalem shall descend with a horn of glory to the end. The sun and moon shall be witnesses and wonder at their stopping. The kings of the earth shall become proud in themselves and are unable to be tamed by man.*

*But I will yoke them (says the Lord) with correction, and force them to imitate one another’s steps. Yes, they shall tread the grapes alike; for in my vineyard, corruption shall not dwell with authority, nor shall the Prince of Darkness usurp my further honor.*

**E. K.** He speaks much in a smaller voice than he did. I cannot understand it. ] He turned back and spoke.

*...... I speak these things for your understanding, and so that you may be strengthened.*

**E. K.** He turns back again (as before) and speaks I know not what.

*...... My dear brethren, therefore rejoice in comfort and the image of peace; and remain faithful, so that you may be fed with that food which shall preserve and always remain before the mighty flames of Zanzor <note>A mystical name or location mentioned by the spirit</note>, where no defiled creature nor any unrighteousness dwells.*

**E. K.** He turns now back again (as before), speaking. He seems now to lean against a Pillar of Copper, large and round. And he has become smaller than he was. Now he stands on the top of the Pillar; now he kneels down, his back being turned.

*Saturday, February 1.* We passed the dangerous way of Ice, having 25 men to cut the ice for our coaches to come through, above two English miles long: but despite that great help, we could not get to *Vinew City* that night, because of the great water and ice near the town, which had broken over the banks into the meadows very deep.
*Sunday, February 2.* We came over the great water, the ice being for the most part (with that night’s wind) driven away out of our passage.
*Monday, February 3.* We came by *Shadek* to *Lasko Town*, and there were lodged in the Provost's fair house by the church.

---

*It is written .... Nothing that is imperfect can stand before the Lord; much more is that imperfection weakened, which obeys the imperfect. Depart, for the kingdom of Righteousness is at hand, and you must vow. Hear the Lord, so that your sins may be forgiven you: For the Prophecies of the Lord are not uttered to the world with the seals of the wicked. Therefore become holy, so that you may increase the benefit of God bestowed among you; and give it to the world as the message of truth, with thanksgiving.*

->Meum est pauca dicere.<-

$\Delta$. But who you are, we do not know; or are you not the same Nalvage, who acted with us earlier today?

Nal. ...... **I am.**

E. K. **Why do you call those Devils, with whom I deal; not offending my conscience, but intending to do good to myself and my neighbors? If you be of God, where is the fruit of your doctrine? etc.**

<margin>* Devils. What this doctrine teaches.</margin>
Nal. ...... *If they were not Devils and enemies of truth, they would praise and honor God in his Messengers of truth. But because these Actions are true, and their truth shall be the destruction of their kingdom; therefore, devilishly and enviously, they resist the will of God: Denying the power, blaspheming his truth, and infecting his vessels.*

*In our Doctrine, nothing is taught but the state of the world, both here and to come. The prophecies of time, and the tying up of God’s mysteries, opened from time to time to those who are his sanctified: as testimonies in the Creation and Operation of his Creatures; of which this doctrine is a part. The Prophets in their times were not ignorant by revelation of the good will of their Creator. The Apostles in Christ’s Kingdom were made partakers of the mysteries to come, of the state of man’s salvation, and the ending of this combat, which is on that day when all Creatures shall receive their reward. The Church of God is always adorned and furnished with spiritual Revelations: as a Mansion or Dwelling-place of the Holy Ghost.*

<margin>Reformation. Note this Circle.</margin>
*These latter days and the end of harvest must also have Laborers: For no Age passes away except through the hands of God, who makes the end of his doings known to the World: To the end that the World may agree with him in Glory. So that this Doctrine consists of the mysteries of the word of God, sealed from the beginning, now delivered to man for that Reformation which must be established in one unity until the end. It is the very part of that Circle which encompasses the Mysteries of the Highest, in his Prophets, Apostles, and Ministers yet to come, who are alive and shall bear witness of eternal Comfort.*

*The fruit of our Doctrine is that God should be praised. For of ourselves we seek no glory: But we serve you for your comfort, teaching you the will of God in the very same Christ who was crucified, sold, and died in the Patriarchs, and published to the World by his Disciples, and is now taught to you for the remission of sins .... the greatest in the World for the end of all things. It is the very key and entrance into the secret mysteries of God (in respect of his determination on earth), bringing with it the reward of eternal glory in the end, which is the greatest Treasure. Those that tempt you do it because of the fear they have of the power of God springing up in you.*

*Let this suffice. The World is vain compared to eternal joys. Heaven and Earth pass away: The reward of the Righteous endures.*

**E. K.**

Nal. ...... *What do you see as imperfect in all that has been delivered?*

**$\Delta$.**

<margin>$\Delta$ Below, in the Krakow book, April 21, it is said this language had never been revealed. Let these two places be reconciled.</margin>
Nal. ...... *You have 49 Tables: In those Tables are contained the mystical and holy voices of the Angels: dignified, and in a state deglorified and drowned in confusion: which pierces Heaven and looks into the Center of the Earth: the very language and speech of Children and Innocents, such as magnify the name of God and are pure.*

*In which the Apostles understood the diffuse sound of the World, made imperfect by man's transgression. These Tables are to be written, not by man, but by the finger of her who is mother to Virtue <note>$\Delta$. Madimi said her mother would write them, in the year 1583.</note> wherein the whole World (incredible to the flesh), all Creatures, and all kinds, are numbered in being and multitude. The measure and proportion of that substance which is Transitory and shall grow old.*

*These things and mysteries are your parts and portions, sealed as much by your own knowledge as by the fruit of your Intercession.*
