### The knowledge of God's Creatures.

<margin>Five parts of a time.</margin>
To me are delivered five parts of a time: wherein I will open, teach, and uncover the secrets of that speech, that holy mystery. To the intent that the **CABALA OF NATURE**, in voice, substance of body, and measure in all parts may be known. For there is nothing secret that shall not be revealed, and the son of **GOD** shall be known in **POWER**, and establish a Kingdom with righteousness on the earth, and then comes the end.

<margin>The future Kingdom of Christ on earth.</margin>
For the earth must come under subjection, and must be made pure, so that death may be swallowed in its own Kingdom, and the enemy of righteousness find no habitation. The word of God endures forever. His promises are just. His spirit is truth. His judgments are inscrutable. He himself is Universal. He is the one for whom you labor. The promises of God in this earthly nobleman <note>Referring to Albert Laski</note> shall be fulfilled. Solomon used the places of honor, and was exalted.

->Thus says the Lord.<-

I have sealed him against hatred; and have made his seat open. Let him therefore arise, so that the people may see him. For mortal men have places of honor, and in their own Courts, they come to be exalted: Who is he that made the earth, and dignified him with a living Soul? Even he it is that exalts, and in whose hands the Kingdoms of the earth are settled.

Behold, the fifth time shall come, (in respect of the parts of time) and it is the day that has been promised. Then shall your eyes be opened. Then shall you see.

A voice. *Stay there, . . . . .*
Nal. *I obey.*

**E. K. Now I see him pass away over the Crystalline Table, which is round like a cartwheel, having a great knob in the middle.**

$\Delta$. Concerning our ordering of the Table and the rest of the furniture, we are desirous to know what is now to be done, seeing we have now come to the end of this first journey.
A voice. *Be it your charge.*
$\Delta$. Do you mean it to be my charge to order these things as my imagination shall be instructed by God’s favor?
A voice. *It was so said before.*

> $\Delta$. **Glory, honor, and thanksgiving to God Almighty, our God, Lord, and Father: now, and for ever and ever. Amen.**

$\Delta$. In reading?
Nal. *Yes.*
$\Delta$. I read to the end.
Nal. *The finger of the Highest examines nature among you by himself and in her own motion. Through this action, things come into being that were not (by Generation), and at the same time vanish as though they were not (by corruption). It is a year in which nature looks with many eyes through . . . . . dwelling places: to some as a nurse, and to the rest as a stepmother. And so it is meant in the Scriptures. For a "time" is a year, intended by determination in the judgment of God, which is not known to man, how or when it shall happen. Another year is a "time," established and presently delivered as the present judgment of God. This is what I speak of. A "time" is a year. The parts are known among you.*

There is a difference between a year mystically promised and unknown, and the time that is mystically promised and known. <note>A mystical year is understood in two ways: One, which is a time known to God and not revealed to man; this is called "Time" with God. We calculate that as a year. The other is pre-ordained, known to God and the Angels, and revealed to man; and that year is the present one.</note> This last is the year I speak of.*

$\Delta$. The questions necessary to be asked of *Madimi*.
1. Good counsel for recovering and strengthening my health.
2. If the pedestal (for the holy table) being made here should be carried with us to *Cracow*, rather than making a new one there—both to save time and to keep our activities more secret?
3. What is your knowledge and judgment of *A. L.*'s wife, regarding her life past, present, and future? For we doubt she is not our true friend.
4. K.*), might be brought here very speedily, so that *A. L.* might redeem the mortgaged lands of *Keysmark* <note>Kežmarok</note> and *Lasko*, and also pay his debts in and around *Cracow*.
For otherwise, he can neither come to *Cracow* with any credit (as he is commanded), nor can he come to us there as conveniently and often as our meetings may require. And thirdly, the date of *Keysmark*'s forfeiture (without the Emperor's favorable help) draws near: specifically next April on *St. George*'s Day.

So it is that from Heaven springs health, and from below come infirmities of body and soul. By this we find two direct powers, bringing forth two qualities: the one is Comfort with Joy, and the other is Infection with sorrow.*

> *But this may be objected: Has it not been seen that the wicked cure diseases and restore health? Whatever comes from death is sorrow, which is the basis of spiritual and bodily infection, so that evil cannot work good. How can it be, therefore, that the dead revive or health is restored? The cure, therefore, of all spiritual infection (I mean the infections of those who are spiritual in respect of their weakness and not their strength; because Satan, while infecting, may become weak (whereby he cannot prevail) and so allow health by reason of that weakness; otherwise, with power, he brings death in every possible way).*

Those who do not know wine become drunk, but to those who do know it, it brings health. Even so is this doctrine. 5. Just as your desire is, so are all things in England. Nothing is held back. But for your sake, those who belong to you are treated in a friendly manner by them.

<image-desc>A large decorative drop cap 'A' at the beginning of the text, set within an ornate square woodcut border featuring floral motifs and a central design of the letter A.</image-desc> After our various prayers and declarations of our humility, obedience, and trust in these Actions: and having now come to Cracow, the sanctified place where we were commanded to make haste, etc. At length appeared *Nalvage*.

E.K. He has a gown of white silk, with a cape with three pendants with tassels on the ends of them, all green: it is fur, white, and seems to shine with a wavering glitter. On his head is nothing; he has no beard. His physiognomy is like the picture of King *Edward* the Sixth; his hair hangs down a quarter of the length of the cap, somewhat curling, yellow. He has a rod or wand in his hand, almost as big as my little finger: it is of gold, and divided into three equal parts, with a brighter gold than the rest. He stands upon his round table of crystal, or rather mother-of-pearl: an infinite number of letters appear on the same, as thick as one can stand by another. The table is somewhat tilted on one side: he stands in the very middle; his garment covers his feet: his breast seems smooth as the down remaining on a swan when all the feathers are off, as is his neck, etc. He is lean and long-faced.

$\Delta$. *The infinite mercies of God be on us: and the light of his countenance shine on us; and his favorable countenance be on us.*
Nal. ...... *Amen, unto him who is, and was, and lives forever.*
E.K. He looks earnestly on his table, and turns himself to view it.
Nal. ...... *All things are in order. Thus says the messenger of him who is the God of Wisdom. Is your worthiness such that you can merit so great mercy? Or are your vessels cleansed and made fit to receive and hold the sweet liquor, pure understanding itself?*
$\Delta$.
> *Has the sun entered into your bowels, or have you tasted of the night-dew? Where are your wedding garments; or in what way do you provide for your marriage? You are unseasoned and withered flesh, partakers of those things which make you holy: through which partaking and the secret providence of him who is the Highest, you became dignified for the purpose, and are sufficiently washed for the time of entrance. O stiff-necked people, you deserve nothing, and yet you have the wages of those who labor. But, what, can corruption be partaker of those things that are incorruptible? Or man, who savors in himself, can you savor also of the Almighty?*
> *O you weaklings, O you of no faith, O you cankers of the earth; Where is the shame you have; Where are the tears you let fall; Where is the humility you are taught? Nay, you are such as say in your hearts; if the spring is fair, the harvest is likely to be good: If these things come to pass, it is the finger of the Lord. But such is your imperfection, such are the fruits of the flesh, and the vanity of mortality.*
> *Notwithstanding, consider that you are servants: Do therefore the will of your Master. You have become free: Be faithful and thankful to him who is the giver of liberty: Nay, you have become children: partakers of the counsel of him who sits and sees, and says, I am. Therefore be sober, faithful, and waver not, for the inheritance of your Father is great: your freedom is without price, and your Master the King of Justice.*

<margin>The end makes all.</margin>
*Where are the people, or in what generation did they dwell, who have been thus acquainted and drawn into familiarity with the true servants and angels of God? To whom have those mysteries been opened? Is it not said of those who are sanctified, "The Lord appeared to them in a vision"? But he comes to you when you are awake. To them he came unexpectedly; to you he comes by request. Arise, therefore, and do not forget what the Lord has done for you; for the things of this world do not exist until they are completed, nor is anything certain except by its conclusion.*

<margin>Faith.</margin>
It was said to Abraham, *And I will destroy them*. He believed it; but he did not ask *when*. Great is the reward of faith, for it gives strength; but those who are faithful are not of this world. <margin>When faith.</margin> Nevertheless, you have said (*as it was said by the disciples to Christ, when they were still impure and blind*), *When shall these things happen? Lord, what is meant by this or that?* Simple faith excels all science. <margin>Idea.</margin> For, *heaven and earth shall perish in their corruption, but the voices of the Lord—and much more his promises—become angels forever. For just as the sun begets in the earth and is the father of many things that live in corruption and have an end, so is the God of heaven the bringer forth and begetter of celestial things with life and forever. For why? Dixit & factum est; every Idea in eternity has become forever, and what is thought has become a living creature.* I teach you a mystery.

*Just as the tree in its sappy life, watering itself thoroughly, brings forth the ornaments of its own beauty, so the spiritual part of man, being good and dignified, burnishes itself with his sound and faithful thought—I mean the glory and show of his own beauty. For the soul of man grows either with beauty toward salvation, or with dishonor and filthiness toward damnation.*

I have fulfilled my commandment. I have warned you as a schoolmaster and counseled you as a friend; I will also teach you.

$\Delta$. After some delay following our prayers, Nalvage at length appeared in the same shape and attire as before: He stands still.

The Godhead, keeping in his Almighty bosom the image and form of all things universally in his secret judgment, looked down upon the Earth; for he said, Let us now go down among the sons of men. He saw that all things grew contrary to their creation and nature; either keeping their dignities and secret virtues shut up in obscurity, or else riotously perishing through the weakness and perverseness of ignorance. So it was said, "Behold, I do not delight in the World." The Elements are defiled, the sons of men are wicked, their bodies have become dunghills, and the inward parts (the secret chambers of their hearts) are the dens and dungeons of the damned. Therefore I will withdraw my spirit from among them, and they shall become more intoxicated, and their ignorance shall be such as never was—no, not since the fall of the heavens.

<margin>In the wilderness.</margin>
...become a serpent in the wilderness: for I have tucked up my garments and have fled away, and She shall mourn on the mountains without comfort.

Look, the thunder spoke, and the earth became misty and full of fog, so that the soul of man might sleep in his own confusion. The second thunder spoke, and there arose spirits, such as those for soothsayers, witches, charmers, and seducers; and they have entered into the holy places and have taken up their seats in man. Woe be unto the earth, therefore, for it is corrupted. Woe be unto the earth, for she is surrendered to her adversary. Woe be unto the earth, she is delivered into the hands of her enemy. Yes, woe be unto the sons of men, for their vessels are poisoned. But even then, said the Lord, *L*, I will be known in the wilderness and will triumph in my weakness.

And look, he called you, and you became drunk and foolish with the Spirit of God. And it was said, *Descend*, for he calls and has called. And *Raphael*, who brought up the prayers, descended; <margin>Raphael's</margin> <margin>This Doctrine.</margin> and he was full with the power and Spirit of God; and it became a doctrine such as never existed from the beginning: not painted or carved, filed or imagined by man, or according to their imaginations, which are of flesh; but simple, plain, full of strength, and the power of the Holy Ghost. This doctrine began, as man did, nakedly from the earth; but yet, it is the image of perfection. This very same art is what is delivered to you as an infallible doctrine, containing within it the waters which run through many gates; even above the Gate of Innocence, where you are taught to find out the dignity and corruption of nature; also made partakers of the secret judgments of the Almighty to be made manifest and to be put into execution. This knowledge in you is to be made perfect in two ways: by power, both mediate and immediate. Immediately from God, in respect of his will and secret judgments, as it was for the Apostles. By means and tradition, as from us, opening the substance and body of nature according to our own image, which is the thing I have now in hand. I am therefore to instruct and inform you according to your delivered doctrine, which is contained in 49 tables. In 49 voices, or callings—<margin>48 Keys, or calls, and their use.</margin> which are the natural keys to open those—not 49 but 48 (for one is not to be opened)—gates of understanding, by which you shall have knowledge to move every gate and to call out as many as you please or shall be thought necessary; those who can very well, righteously, and wisely open to you the secrets of their cities and make you perfectly understand the things contained in the tables. Through this knowledge, you shall easily be able to judge, not as the world does, but perfectly of the world and of all things contained within the compass of nature, and of all things which are subject to an end.

But behold, this charge of mine is tied to time. Therefore, be diligent to learn, diligent to listen, and do so with patience; for it is neither a free school, nor a school of long duration. <margin>Note: Take time while time is, for time will pass away. August next.</margin> For as power is not given to me beyond the first day of *August* next, so you have no strength to learn after that, because I am the staff of your doctrine.

Nal. ..... I am for the comfort of the world and not for its hindrance. Thus says the Lord: to those who have a harvest, let them reap, and to those who have labor, let them work. As for me, I am tied to time and am ready at all times; for I measure not your night nor day.

$\Delta$. Thanks be to the highest.

Nal. ..... Cease now with me, for no more descends.

**E. K.** Now all the fingers are gone.

$\Delta$. <note>John Dee</note>

<margin>
Second Table.

The covenant of God. Obedience.

Many keys.

Note these three degrees.

Faith.
A key of the first seven.
A sign to make an end.
</margin>

**Nal.** ..... It is the meaning in your tongue of the holy and mystical Call delivered before : which follows in practice for the moving of the second Table, the Kings and Ministers of government : *The utterance of which, is of force, and moves them to visible apparition : moved and appeared, they are forced ( by the Covenant of God delivered by his spirit ) to render obedience and faithful society. Wherein, they will open the mysteries of their creation, as far as shall be necessary : and give you understanding of many thousand secrets, wherein you are yet but children; for every Table has his key : every key opens his gate, and every gate being opened, gives knowledge of itself, of entrance, and of the mysteries of those things whereof he is an enclosure. Within these Palaces you shall find things that are of power, as well to speak, as to do; for every [(1) Palace] is above his [(2) City] and every City above his [(3) entrance.]*

*Be you therefore diligent that you may enter in, not as spoilers, but as such as deserve entertainment in the name, and through the power of the Highest. For great are the mercies of God unto such as have faith. This is therefore the key of the first seven, according to the proportion of the first Creation. No more for this time.*

*A sign always to make an end.*

->Tuesday, April 17. Cracow.<-

After various short prayers appropriate to the action, and while the curtain of white water still remained, E. K. thought several times that he saw through the white veil, and the stone and everything, with nothing appearing within it. E. K. immediately fell into a new doubting of the truth of these actions, and said he had a vision from a good creature last night, who said these creatures with which we dealt would no longer appear to him. Thereupon he said that both the scorner of the previous days and these instructors of ours were all devils; and that he would no longer sit to receive any doctrine of theirs by letters (A.B.C.), unless they would otherwise expressly and vividly deliver a plain rule for it. With many other arguments to disprove the truth of our actions, he then said, "John, your boy, can well enough deliver you their letters, and so you do not need me," etc. I referred everything to God, His will, and mercies: For, as I had requested wisdom and true knowledge at His hands only, and by His order, and for His service, so I do not doubt but God will, according to His accustomed goodness, provide for me what is best for my vocation here on earth, etc.

E. K. rose and went away, and left me alone in my study, appointed for these actions.

> O God, come to my assistance; O Lord, make haste to help me. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, as it was in the beginning, and is now, and always, and into the ages of ages. Amen.

---

->Thursday, Around 9:00.<-

As I was in my upper study, and had gathered the holy words of the second and third call, and had compared them with the English translations also delivered to us, E. K. came up the stairs and went into his study, then came out again. As he was going down the stairs, I opened my study door and greeted him. He thereupon came up again and entered my study. There I showed him what I had done, and how I had some understanding of those holy words and their meanings by means of correctly applying the English to the word *Christus*, intending thereby to have induced E. K. to better like the due and methodical manner of our friends' proceeding with us. I told him that unless I had these words of this strange language delivered to us letter by letter, we might err both in spelling and also, for want of the true pronunciation of the words and distinctions of the punctuation, we might further miss the expected effect. 

But as on Tuesday last, so now again he said our teachers were deluders, and not good or sufficient teachers, who had not in two years' space made us able to understand or do anything; and that he could have learned all the seven liberal sciences in two years if he had first learned logic, etc. Therefore, he would have no more to do with them in any way, wished himself in England, and said that if these books were his, he would burn them immediately. He said that he had written to my Lord (by *Pirmis*) that he took our teachers to be deceivers and wicked, and not good creatures of God, with many such speeches and reasons (as he thought) powerful enough to dissuade himself from any further dealing with them. But he told me to use John, my boy, as my skryer, for these spiritual creatures were not bound to him, etc. 

I answered all these points and reasons as time allowed, declaring my *perfect trust in God*—that since I have for many years desired and prayed for wisdom (such as these actions involve) at His hands, and by such means as seems best to His Divine Majesty, He would not either dislike my prayer or misuse my constant hope in His goodness and mercy. Therefore, I concluded that I referred everything to the merciful will of God, and doubted nothing that in the end I would be satisfied in my request and prayer made to Him. So he went from me this second time.... God enlighten his heart with knowledge of the truth, if it be His Divine will and pleasure.

Note, *Pirmis* left last Wednesday morning, and had received our letters on Tuesday afternoon; but on the Monday before, the wicked prince of darkness did what he could to hinder our progress.

On Thursday, *Tabius* (brother to my Lord *Laskie's* wife) brought news to Cracow that Lord *Laskie* was coming toward Cracow. *Emericus* came from Kesmark and returned back again. *Tabius* rode from Cracow toward Kesmark.

---

->Saturday, April 21, in the afternoon.<-

After our prayers were made, *Gabriel* and *Nalvage* appeared shortly. E. K. proposed six questions in order, which had bred great doubt in his imagination, and requested their answers.

He never heard of any man who would ask if God would fulfill His promises.

What if it were a hundred Augusts? You may be weary before next August, just as the children of Israel were of their manna.

Numbers.
Formal Numbers.
Pulius.

<margin>
Note the property of this method and language.
</margin>

Gab. ...... Every letter signifies the member of the substance of which it speaks. Every word signifies the essence (quiddity) of the substance. The letters are separated and in confusion; therefore, they are gathered together by numbers, which, when gathered, also signify a number. For as every greater thing contains its lesser, so are the secret and unknown forms of things enclosed within their origins (parents). When known in number, they are easily distinguished, so that herein we teach places to be numbered, letters to be chosen from those numbered, and proper words formed from the letters—signifying substantially the thing that is spoken of in the center of its Creator. Thus, just as the mind of man is moved by ordered speech and is easily persuaded of things that are true, so are the creatures of God stirred within themselves when they hear the words with which they were nurtured and brought forth. For nothing moves that is not persuaded, nor can anything be persuaded that is unknown.

<margin>
Understanding, Persuasion, Motion.
</margin>

The creatures of God do not understand you; you are not of their cities. You have become enemies because you are separated by ignorance from Him who governs the city.

E. K. Is this language known in any part of the world or not? If it is, where and to whom?

<margin>
Adam.
</margin>

Gab. ...... Man in his creation, being made innocent, was also authorized and made a partaker of the power and Spirit of God. By this, he not only knew all things under his creation and spoke of them properly, naming them as they were, but was also a partaker of our presence and society—yes, a speaker of the mysteries of God, even with God Himself. Thus, in innocence, the power of those who partook with God and us, His good angels, was exalted, and he became holy in the sight of God until Coronzon (for that is the true name of that mighty devil), envying his happiness and perceiving that the substance of his lesser part was frail and imperfect in respect to his pure being (esse), began to assail him and so prevailed. In offending, he became accursed in the sight of God and so lost the garden of happiness and the judgment of his understanding—but not utterly the favor of God. He was driven forth (as your Scriptures record) onto the earth, which was covered with brambles. There, being as if mute and unable to speak, he began out of necessity to learn the language which you, E. K., call [ א Hebrew ]—and yet not that [ ב Hebrew ] used among you. In this language, he uttered and delivered to his posterity the closest knowledge he had of God's creatures. He divided his speech from his own self into three parts: twelve, three, and seven. The numbers of these remain, but the true forms and pronunciations are lacking. Therefore, it is not of the force it was in its own dignity, much less to be compared with this which we deliver, which Adam truly spoke in innocence and which was never uttered nor disclosed to man since then until now. In this, the power of God must work and wisdom in her true kind be delivered; these are not to be spoken of in any other way, nor discussed with human imaginations. For as this work and gift is from God, who is all power, so does He open it in a tongue of power, to the

### E. K. Gabriel sits, and Nalvage stands.

**Gab.** ... My brethren, listen to my voice, for I am the true servant of the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob; the dignity of which is sufficient both for the truth of the doctrine and the confirmation and persuasion of your minds. For as God is the Father of the faithful, so He shows Himself to the faithful, by which you may experience great comfort and consolation. From this you may rightly gather the mercies of God regarding your election.

For at what time has God appeared to the unrighteous? Or where do you read that He ever visited the reprobate? For the reprobate has no visitation except by the rod of justice.

<margin>An objection.</margin>
But you may rise up among yourselves, saying, "Look, we are perverse; we lack faith."
<margin>Answer.</margin>
It is true regarding the acts of faith, but not the roots of faith. But I say to you that the power of God in His election is the basis of man’s purity and acceptance.

But here there is a *Caveat*.

That a man imagining his predestination and perfect election does not justify himself; for wherever this is found, or this doctrine is preached among you—whether simply in a man or publicly in a congregation—it is a sure sign and token of their perpetual ignorance and confusion. For the will and power of God do not belong to our measure (for it was the cause of rebellion among us), much less among men, who are still fighting for the glory of their reward. Behold, it is a sin in him who judges his brother's conscience; much more is it a threefold error to form imaginations of sin, by whose imaginations they are created.

Do not be proud, therefore, of the gifts of God, but become humble. Do not justify yourself because this is the word of God delivered to you for your own sake. But the more you receive, be the more thankful; and the more you are in the strength of God, the more you should practice the purity of humility.

<margin>Good angels.</margin>
Of whom it is said, "Behold, my Spirit has entered, even into my servants, and they have become humble and meek in the sight of men." But if we are the servants of the God of Abraham, then we are the spirits of truth and understanding, for our faith is honored in the sight of the heavens, and we have become mighty in the power of the Almighty. Therefore we ought to be believed.

Now, if you will confess yourselves to be the children of Abraham, then you must also accept our doctrine. For the food by which Abraham lived is the same food we administer to you; of whom it is said, "He believed God, and it was counted to him as righteousness." Even so should you do,

1. There appears a Partridge, but it has one leg like a Kite: This Partridge seems to sit on a green place under the gate, one leg is much longer than the other, being like a Kite's leg. This Partridge seems to limp.

He bids one of his company take it up. There goes a bridge to the top of that hill, all upon arches, and under it goes a River.

He takes the Partridge and pulls all its feathers, and they fall into the River: He cuts off the longer leg exactly to the length of the other. They about him cry, *O just judgment.*

Now he turns it off over the bridge, and it flies away, for the feathers of its wings were not pulled.

2. He goes on, and comes to another gate; and there the third man unlocks it, as the second next him unlocked the first Gate; he himself having the Key first delivered to him, as is noted above. There appears a thing like a Kite, all white, very great; it has a foul, great head. It seems to be in a very pleasant garden, and flies from place to place in it, and beats down the rose trees and other fruit trees. The Garden seems very delicate and pleasant. They go all into the Garden: and he says, *You are of the wilderness; your feathers and carcass are not worthy the spoil of the garden.*

Now the Kite scratches and gasps at this man; but he takes the Kite and cuts its carcass into two equal parts, from the crown of its head, and throws one half over one side of the Bridge, and the other half over the other side, and said, *Fowls must be devoured by fowls.* The rest say, *O justitia divina* <note>O divine justice</note>, clapping their hands over their heads.

# LIBRI MYSTICI APERTORII
## CRACOVIAN SABBATH BOOK, Year 1584.

---

->Saturday at Kraków, May 7, Morning, 6 o’clock.<-

<image-desc>A large ornamental woodcut initial A, featuring foliate and geometric patterns, begins the first paragraph.</image-desc>
After prayers, Gabriel and Nalvage appeared with the Table, and Gabriel had his Dart in his hand. Moreover, there appeared a similar furnishing of a Table with a white cloth, a candlestick, and a taper on it, with a desk and cushions (which I had caused to be made with red crosses on them). Also, E. K. himself and I appeared in the same Stone. In effect, all things were as we had them before us; after about seven and a half minutes, that show of our furniture and ourselves disappeared.

**E. K.** Gabriel stands up and speaks as follows:

> *....... A mighty city was built on the top of a mountain, in which many thousands lived. Round about the hill ran a fresh river, which was the only comfort of the town; for from it they drank—their wives, their children, their male servants, their female servants, their camels, horses, mules, and all the beasts of their fields. The beginning of which river was a spring, which was unknown to the city, because of the <unclear>...yth</unclear> from where it descended. It happened that a serpent groaned for her time, and behold, she brought forth: and <unclear>...</unclear> were such as herself. And she lifted up her head and leaned upon her twice-coiled tail and beheld the sun steadfastly (for her envy was toward that city). And she said within herself: "My children are yet young." Time passed, and they became large. And she went to the spring, and smiled and said with a laughing voice, "The earth has fallen into you; you are choked. But listen to my voice: You shall receive comfort." But the spring would not. And she lifted up her voice and roared, for she was full of craft and deceit. And she said to the shingles <note>small stones or pebbles in the water</note> through which the spring runs (or rather lies), "You are full of emptiness and void places. Let my children (therefore) hide themselves within you for a season." And they were contented. And she departed willingly, and says within herself: "Now I know I shall be Lady of the city."*
>
> *And after a few years, the young serpents became great, so that one half of their bodies lived within the shingles, and the rest troubled the passage of the spring. So the spring groaned; for the injury that was done against her was great.*
>
> *A great misery, for the hill has become desolate without the water, and the city and the beasts perish for want of drink; for the people groan and are full of sorrow.*
>
> *This city and serpents are <unclear>60..</unclear> now, and judgment must be had between the shingles and the spring, for between them lies the life and death of the city.*
>
> *Thus says the Lord to you [pointing to E. K.]: "Gird yourself and sit down. Consider both parts and give judgment: for your mouth shall this day be the judgment of the Lord."*

**E. K.** Do you mean me?

**E. K.** As the Lord has put the authority of judgment into my hands, so I beseech him to give me wisdom and understanding to judge rightly. And because the judgment of this is committed to me, I suspect some other mystery lies hidden in this judgment required of me. But if it shall please God that my friend here, Master Dee, shall give me his advice, I shall think myself well satisfied.

> *...... Consider with yourself (says the Lord) and give judgment against the shingles, for the fault is plain. Consider two points: the necessity of the spring, that it must come that way; and secondly, the health of the city.*

**E. K.** My judgment is that the shingles and serpent should be removed away by an earthquake from the place which they encumber and block, so that there may be a fit new place and course for that spring, for the relief of that city as it was before.

*...... Let it be so as you have said, for it is a just judgment.*

*Now listen to what the Lord says. The people and City of the Hill are the world, who are from time to time relieved and quenched by the mercy and spring of God's wisdom, according to the extreme necessity of their thirst. But the people and City are those who belong to the Temple and Church of God, who drink of His mercy for their comfort. The camels and other beasts are the people of the Earth who delight in sin and in their own imagination, who are also relieved along with those of the City; but the diversity of their bodies causes the diversity of the outcomes of their comfort. The Hill in which the Spring is signifies His prophets, and such as are drunk in the Lord; through whom the mercies and will of God and of the Highest are opened inwardly from time to time, according to the secret will and determination of those who are within the City of His Elect. But the frailties and affections of their flesh and outward man are their foolish imaginations and loose shingles wherein the Serpent, the old Devil, has harbored her children—the spirits of darkness and deceit—which always resist the Will of God and are placed between the mercies of God and His people. Moses, Daniel, Esdras, and all the rest of the prophets; Christ’s twelve, and Paul the messenger of God: they all harmed the congregation of the faithful in their flesh, until they pronounced judgment against themselves (as you have done) with the amendment of their lives. For who is worthy to know the secrets of our God, but he who delights in righteousness, is obedient, full of faith, and possessed of the spirit of understanding? Let it be therefore to you as you have said. Let the shingles and serpents be separated, so that the fountain may feed as before. All the trash that you have from the wicked, burn it.*

**E. K.** I do not know if they are wicked.

*..... Their dealings with you are the hindrance of the Will of God, and therefore they are wicked.*

*..... You have given judgment against yourself: take care that you do not offend your own soul.*

**Δ.** Send down Your Spirit, O Lord, and illuminate E. K.’s heart with the perception of his wrong opinion, etc.

**E. K.** If Moses and Daniel were skilled in the arts of the Egyptian magicians, and were not thereby hindered from being the servants of God, why may I not deal with these without hindrance to the Will of God?

*...... Darkness yielded to light; the greater excluded the lesser. The more a man knows wickedness, the more he shall hate it once he is called back. The more they knew the shadow, so much more they delighted in the body. For the works of the Egyptians seem to be something, but are not. The works of the Lord are, and continue; for as the painter imitates the gestures of man in his skill, so does the Devil imitate the substances and things created and made by God.*

*Stand up and look into the whole world, into her youth and middle age, for they are past. Where are the monuments that Satan has built?*

**E. K.** Has Satan built any monuments?

*...... Yes. Has he not built himself a fort upon the whole earth? Has he not the victory over the saints? Does he not dwell in the Temple of the Highest? Does he not triumph in the cities of the whole world?*

*Yes. But his victories are without comfort; his dwelling places are without pleasure. For he knows his time is at hand. He who now gives freedom shall become bound; and for him to whom the whole world is as a garden, there shall be not one foot left. Therefore all his pleasures are vanity, all his triumphs are smoke, and his authority is nothing indeed but a mere shadow. For that which is not, cannot be; where it is said by the Lord, it shall not be. Neither can truth, light, or wisdom ascend from the earth, but they descend from the heavens.*

*Compare the earth (into which the Devil is thrust as into his dwelling) with the heavens, which are provided for the holy. Consider the pain of the one, and the pleasure of the other: the seat of God’s Justice, and the fountain of His Mercy; the cave of darkness, and the diadem of light. And then cry, woe, woe, woe to those who err and whose lives are but shadows. For their happiness is exactly like that from which it came, and their reward is the same as that of the spirit and prince of darkness.*

<margin>His life penned.</margin>
*Compare foolish knowledge with true wisdom; your spirits of lying with us, who are the voice of truth; the vanity that they lead you into, and the reward of our message. And say within yourself, <term>peccavi</term>. Will you be persuaded by experience? Consider your imprisonments, your affliction, and the shame of your body. Consider the love of a few, and the envy of a multitude. Weigh within yourself the vanity of your life; your rash footsteps; all that happened to you by that society and (as you think) comfort, which were indeed the stinging pricks of your enemies.*

*..... Since we came to you (sent from the Lord, and calling you to God), you have been delivered from them; from a place full of fornication and the wrath of God; you have been raised to the outskirts of worldly honor; and you have been satisfied regarding the necessities of this world. Holy is the money that is gotten righteously; but accursed are the evils that are reaped with wrong.*

->The curtain is now pulled shut.<-

A voice: That is all.
Blessed be the Creator of all, *who has mercy on all.*
E. K. Now he is here, dressed as he was accustomed to appear.
<margin>Promise of God confirmed again. 14 to be received next Monday.</margin> Nal. ...... Thus, has the Lord kept his promise with you: and will not forget the least part of his whole promise with you. Therefore, keep your promise with the Lord; for he is jealous, and not to be defiled. Proceed as you now do. Next Monday you shall have as many.
Δ. Will it please you to deliver to us the English translation of these 14 now, as you were accustomed to do?
Nal. ...... The English translation will have a day of its own.
Nal. ...... The [ Δ. ] third Monday to come, you shall have them all. So you have only three days to labor, etc.
Δ. You speak of the next Monday, and the third; and say nothing of the second Monday: and you said that the English will have a day of its own: And you say we have only three days to labor, etc.
Nal. ...... What I have said is so. Go also, and refresh yourselves.
->[*E. K. The curtain is drawn.*]<-
A voice. ...... Stay there.
A voice. ...... Give God thanks, and make an end.
E. K. Prayed the 145th and 146th Psalm, kneeling reverently; and I likewise in heart consenting to it, listening attentively.
Note ..... E. K. is very well persuaded of these Actions now, thanks be to the Highest, who is Almighty.
> Δ. Laudate Dominum de Cælis, laudate eum in excelsis: laudate eum omnes Angeli ejus, laudate eum omnes virtutes ejus. Quia ipse dixit, & facta sunt nobis. Non fecit taliter omni nationi. Soli Deo nostro, laus omnis, Victoria, Triumphus, & Jubilatio, Amen. <note>Praise the Lord from the heavens, praise him in the heights: praise him all his Angels, praise him all his powers. For he spoke, and they were made for us. He has not done so for every nation. To our God alone be all praise, victory, triumph, and rejoicing, Amen.</note>

->Monday, Cracow, May 21, 1584. Morning, 5:00 AM. Third Action, Lunar.<-

E. K. There appears neither a veil, nor anything else in the stone.
Δ. At length one appeared, but none of the usual ones: he is joyful and green, with a long robe (like green velvet): his hair is long, like yellow gold: nothing on his head but his hair. He stands as though he stood in a cloud, above the usual ground in the air.
<margin>... regarding Δ. God is not tied to time. ... performance ... means dwelling with him. ... are mansions. ... faithful ... faith ...</margin>
..... Look, the sun shines, and men fear no rain; the clouds are dispersed, and they do not look for a storm: But when it rains mightily, or the heavens frown, then they keep to their houses, saying one to another, "What an unreasonable storm is this? What hail-stones are these? Good Lord, who ever saw such winds? Were there ever such winds?" So shall it be of the power of God, who holds the winds in his hands, and scatters clouds abroad with his feet: For of his coming, it shall be said among you, "My spirit has troubled me, and I am troubled: Why have you brought in things greater than yourself? Or where shall this power dwell that overshadowers me?" Lacking, you shall desire (as you do), and being filled, you shall think you have too much.
Flesh can never be thoroughly mortified except by death. Think not that the Lord is like the Sun, which keeps his continual watch through the heavens; which, because he is made for a time, is also tied to time.
He who sits and judges keeps no set course, but a continual performance of his long-held providence: For he who treats him otherwise shall be rejected: because his [ Δ. ] dwellings are not in the mansions of the faithful. Lift up your ears therefore; for thus says the highest:

# A true Relation of Dr. Dee his Actions with Spirits, &c.

> *Who made the heavens, or spread them like a garment? Who breathed into man the spirit of understanding? Who overthrew the proud world with waters? Who smiled at the ruin of Pharaoh? Who rooted the wicked out of their seats and made them become vineyards for my people: even the stiff-necked generation? Who threw down the Towers of Babylon and the great Harlot? Who dwelt upon the Earth and became flesh to pay for your wickedness? Who tumbled the stone from the Well, so that the Sheep might drink? Even he it is who gave all these their times. He it is who is as able to make you understand as those who cast into the waters and said, "Let us draw up our fish," who always deals with the weakest so that he might prove himself the strongest.*

[E. K. He speaks a great deal to himself, which I do not perceive.]

<margin>A wedding garment is needed.</margin>
...... *Even he it is who will make you strong and wise, if he finds you with garments. He it is who says to you: "Waver not, be steadfast; for the faithful are never unrewarded."*

[E. K. He puts his right hand out of the Stone, with the hand grasped together. Now he opens his hand, and there is writing in it; it is so far from me that I cannot read it, yet he seems to be much nearer to me than his hand is. The writing seems to be like the leaf of a Book. Thus it was written:]

<margin>.. L. Poison.</margin>
...... *Have an eye to my foretelling.... Troubles. Sudden sorrow is at hand in all the earth. No, his Ship is almost built. Laski, if he serves me, shall be King of Poland. If he serves another, his bowels shall fall out before him with poison.*

E. K. Now he clasped his hand together and stopped the reading.

$\Delta$. Whom is Laski to serve (O Lord) but you? To keep your Laws, Statutes, and Commandments? Not to depend upon any creature.

<margin>
Turks.
Not to Laski.
A. L.
One must go to the Emperor.
Return by warning.
</margin>
...... *The King and Chancellor have sold the people of this Land and are sworn Turks. Return not home to Lasko (Laski); for if you do, you shall offend me. Go to the Emperor; for I will comfort you with his favor. Let him not return from there until he is warned by me.*

$\Delta$. You mean from the Emperor's Court?

$\Delta$. I beseech you, by what token shall he receive your warning?

...... *Be his right hand to his body, and his mouth to me. I will be merciful to him and hold up his head. Cease until the seventh hour of the day; then comes the Action.*

$\Delta$. Do you mean the seventh hour as calculated from last midnight?

$\Delta$. That begins at noon, if you make but 12 hours in the day; or at 11:00 if you reckon common hours.

->Tuesday at Cracow, May 22, 1584, in Whitsun-week, morning around 7:00.<-

<margin>
A deceiver.
</margin>
After our sitting, and after some prayer was used, a very little creature appeared on the cushion by the stone, saying: Put out your candle; for you shall have nothing to do today.
$\triangle$. What is your name, so that we may allege your message as our excuse, seeing we were told yesterday to labor today?
**E. K. He is gone.**
$\triangle$. After that, about half an hour later, our instructors appeared as they had before.
Gab. ...... Move, move, move not, for the place is holy.
**E. K. Gabriel stands up; and after a while said:**

<margin>
Obedience.
</margin>
> ...... *The heavens are called righteous because of their obedience. **The earth is accursed because of her waywardness.** Those, therefore, who seek heavenly things ought to be obedient; lest with their waywardness they be consumed in the end, burnt to ashes with fire, as the Earth shall be for her unrighteousness.*

<margin>
Faith.
</margin>
> *Therefore, be obedient and full of humility, using the instrument of righteousness (which is faith), so that you may be partakers of the celestial comforts, which are the reward of those who forsake their waywardness. It has been said to you... Measure not out God's building. It has been said to you... Continue to the end. It has been told to you... That the determinations of God are not as yet established upon you.*

<margin>
See the 1st Book of Kings, chapter 2 regarding the revoked determination of God over the Tribe of Levi: See also the words of David in the 3rd Book of Kings, chapter 2, so that the Lord may confirm his words, etc.
</margin>
> *For it is written, it may again be * undetermined. I speak this for your instruction: For many have the power of God, but not unto righteousness, as was evident among the Jews in the choice of their Kings. In the very house of God, among those who entered into the holy place. For not all whom the Prophets anointed were good. Not that they were evil at the time of their anointing, but because their anointing and the dignity of their office was defiled in them in the end through their own waywardness. The High Priests also were chosen in righteousness and by the Spirit of God, but they became rebels in the holy house, and were those of whom it is said, "But the Most High was a stumbling block to them." Even so, my brethren, may it be with you.*

$\triangle$. Jesus defend us from that trouble.
> *For although it has pleased God to show himself to you, yet you are not ashamed to say: "If the harvest does not come in at the time appointed, I will become a renegade."*

<margin>
For what?
</margin>
> *But well done (my brethren)! Has the Lord need of you? It does not need to be told to you; you know the contrary. Then it follows that you have need of God. But for what? and why? So that your souls may overcome this world, and overcome the body, to attain the dignity of an Angel.*

> *And because you are miserable and turned out into the field, full of brambles and misery, lean, naked, and unarmed to fight against him who resists the might of God. Consider these last two, and then answer yourselves for the rest.*

<margin>
Beware.
The promises of God are confirmed.
Note the second instruction: or Gift of the Highest.
</margin>
> *I give you a short warning. God will fulfill his promises: And (as he has said) by this August, you shall understand:*
> 1. *How to know and use God's creatures, good and bad.*
> 2. *But when, and for what, is the gift of the Highest, and it shall be fulfilled in you (if you will be obedient) when it pleases him: even with a sound from his own mouth, saying, "Come and hear."*

<margin>
The Actions are the greatest.
Move not from this place.
</margin>
> *For these Actions are twofold: Consider it, if you can. And they are the greatest because they are the last, and they contain all that has been done before them. If you consider this well, and to what you are called, you shall perceive that the judgments of God are not a tennis ball.*
> *Thus much I thought to warn you, my brethren. Have a little patience for the Action. He who stirs from his place shall find the reward for it.*

# THE SEVENTH BOOK OF THE CRACOVIAN OPENING
# MYSTICAL, SABBATICAL,
## Part Four; Year 1584, May 23.

---

->Wednesday, † at Krakow, May 23. In the morning, at nearly 7:15. After our prayers.<-

<margin>The Curtain appeared, at the first looking.
$\Delta$. There occurred a great storm or temptation for E. K. involving doubting and disliking our instructors and their actions, and of scorning and condemning anything that I knew or could do. I bore all things patiently for God's sake, etc. At length the Curtain was opened, and they appeared.</margin>
There occurred a great storm or temptation for E. K. involving doubting and disliking our instructors and their actions, and of scorning and condemning anything that I knew or could do. I bore all things patiently for God's sake, etc. At length the Curtain was opened, and they appeared.

E. K. I am content to see, and to make a true report of what they will show; but my heart stands against them.

Gab. ...... The time shall come when the oak that is beaten by every storm shall be a dining table in the Prince's Hall.

<margin>.. able doubting 1/2</margin>
Gab. ...... Do not move, for the place is holy. He who doubts acts according to the nature of the flesh, but he who has faith has the gift of the Holy Ghost. The swallow flies swiftly, but where she lands, there is no memory of her being: such are the words of man. But our words are like a swift arrow that enters and sticks where it lands.

### Thursday May 24.

Δ. Because E. K. did not come (as was commanded yesterday) to continue the action, I went to his study door and knocked for him. I requested him to come, but he refused to do so and gave me a short and resolute answer: that he would never again have anything to do with these actions. I asked him the reason why; he would give none, but earnestly refused to proceed. I told him that his words * last night (that he could not deal today) very much grieved me, etc., of which he made little account. So I went into my study again and committed the cause to God.

<margin>* Those words he spoke more than an hour after the action ended, in the chamber in front of my study of practice.</margin>
After less than half an hour, he came quickly out of his study, carrying in his hand one volume of *Cornelius Agrippa’s* works. In one chapter of that book, he read the names of countries and provinces collected from *Ptolemy* (as the author notes there). From this he inferred that our spiritual instructors were *frauds* for giving us a description of the world taken out of other books; and therefore he would have nothing more to do with them. I replied and said, "I am very glad that you have a book of your own in which these geographical names are expressed—such as our instructors had delivered to us for the most part."

# A true Relation of Dr. Dee's Actions with spirits, etc.

of various times before, but a very hearty and sincere conversion, such as without any doubt will be found very acceptable to the Most High.

Moreover, he declared that about nine or ten days ago, he intended to have escaped *secretly by the spiritual help* of those with whom he had dealt for so long; and therefore, that until now, he had acted hypocritically.

But, whereas previously they were always accustomed to threaten him with poverty (a thing which he most hated and feared):

That now he does not care if he should be in want; indeed, he considered it to be neither a shame nor a sin to beg. He stated that he now valued God’s favor and eternal life more than he does all transitory wealth and riches, or being entangled within the danger of the snares of these wicked spirits.

Also, he now perceived the great error he was in recently, when he would have forsaken dealing with the wicked for the sake of an assured temporal maintenance, and so would have more willingly followed these actions without complaining. He says now that he is no perfect Christian who must be hired with money to forsake the Devil and his works, etc.

And as for the outcome of these actions, he would never either doubt or dislike however they turned out, assuring himself that God would do all things for the best and for His own honor, etc. Many other of his very godly sayings I omit, thinking these sufficient here.

> Δ. O Almighty, eternal, and most merciful God, we thank, glorify, and praise you; O blessed and most glorious Trinity, we will forever magnify your unspeakable providence, favor, election, and conversion unto you.
>
> O Blessed Jesus, we will forever extol your loving-kindness and long-suffering toward us, and your triumphant proceeding against Satan and his ministers for the sake of your elect.
>
> <margin>Conversion and confirmation prayed for.</margin>
> O Holy Spirit, the director into all truth and comforter of your elect, confirm and establish our hearts with your gracious and continual zeal, and love of truth, purity of life, charitable humility, and constant patience to your well-pleasing until the end: That after this life (through the mercy of the Father, the merits of our Lord Jesus Christ, and your charitable embrace of us), we may forever enjoy the heavenly kingdom among the blessed Angels and all the dignified company of mankind. Amen. Amen. Amen.

-> Monday, June 11. Morning, 7:30. Krakow. <-

Δ. After our due prayers and thanks to the Almighty for His great mercies and power shown in the conversion of E. K., we stayed still, attending some show as we were accustomed to receive. Among our various short discourses on our faith, hope, patience, constancy, humility, and our other duties required in this action and in the service of God, *E. K.* himself spoke these sentences, which are worthy to be recorded as the evident token of his sound and faithful turning and his intent to cleave unto the Lord:

1. *E. K.* *I acknowledge my sins have deserved that for these seven years I should have no show or sight of His good creatures.*
2. *E. K.* *If I should sit thus for seven years, waiting for the pleasure of God, I would be contented.*
3. *E. K.* *I do not repent at all for what I have done in forsaking those with whom I used to have dealings, etc.*

*E. K.* In the stone, nothing appeared during all the time of our sitting here.

<margin>Δ. At 11:00 we stopped; thus, we waited for 3 hours and 45 minutes.</margin>
Δ. *Nothing visible appeared in the consecrated crystal, except for the visible form of the crystal itself, as E. K. said.*

Δ. I will affirm nothing in this case, but let this conjecture of mine be recorded: The cause of the non-appearance last Friday, and now this Monday, may be this:

<margin>The Justice of God.</margin>
1. That, just as we lost and refused the three days assigned by our instructors to finish everything, so now we shall call and request for three days and have nothing—as it has turned out these two days; and it is possible that for one day more we shall have the same lack of appearance.

->*Or else:*<-

<margin>See above.</margin>
2. According to the premises: only three days before our journey begins shall that be delivered to us which we should have received in the last three days, etc.

### Monday, June 18th. Morning, 8:00 AM. Krakow.

$\Delta$. After the Lord's Prayer and some other special prayers and thanksgivings for the exceedingly great mercies shown in the converting and reforming of E.K., and my promising to record the act of it as well as God should give me grace; and also earnestly praying for comfort to be given to A.L., who is somewhat oppressed with sadness to see his own subjects and servants triumph over him in his low estate from on high, and all for lack of money and wealth, etc.

### Wednesday, June 20, in the Afternoon. 1584. Krakow.

Dee: It is first to be noted that early this morning, while E. K. was lying in his bed and awake, a vision appeared in the following manner: someone stood by the head of his bed and patted him gently on the head to make him more alert. He seemed to be clothed with feathers, strangely twisted all over him, etc.
Four very beautiful castles appeared to him [E. K.], standing in the four parts of the world, out of which he heard the sound of a trumpet. Then it seemed that out of every castle a cloth was thrown on the ground, wider than a tablecloth.
Out of the one in the East, the cloth that was cast seemed to be red.
Out of the one in the South, the cloth seemed white.
Out of the one in the West, the cloth seemed green, with large knobs on it.
Out of the one in the North, spread or thrown out from the gate underfoot, the cloth seemed to be very black.
Out of every gate, one trumpeter then emerged, whose trumpets were of a strange form, twisted and growing larger and larger toward the end.
After the trumpeter followed three ensign bearers.
After them came six elderly men with white beards and staves in their hands.
Then followed a handsome man with a great deal of clothing on his back, his robe having a long train.
After him came five men carrying his train.
Then followed one great cross, and around it four lesser crosses.
<margin>These crosses did not seem to be on the ground, but in the air in a white cloud. The great cross seemed to be made of a cloud, like a rainbow.</margin>
These crosses each had ten figures like men on them, their faces appearing distinctly on the four parts of the cross, all over.
After the crosses followed 16 white creatures.
And after them, an infinite number seemed to emerge and spread themselves in an orderly circle, nearly in front of the four aforementioned castles.
Upon this vision being declared to me, I immediately wrote down a note of it, trusting in God that it signified good.
In the afternoon, as E. K. sat by me, he felt a strange movement on his head, by which he judged that some spiritual creature was visiting him. As we continued together, and I had read to E. K. some rare material from the epistles of *Ignatius*, *Polycarp*, and *Martial*—some concerning the Sacrament and some concerning the cross—a voice answered and said, "That it is true: the sign of the cross is of great force and virtue."
After this, the spiritual creature seemed to E. K. to be very heavy on his right shoulder as he sat by me in my study. And as E. K. considered the numbers of those he had counted passing out of the four gates (namely: 1, 3, 6, 1, and 5), the spiritual creature said, "The number 16 is a perfect number, consisting of 1, 3, 6, 1, and 5." He said furthermore, "**God the Father is a standing pillar.**"
Dee: At those words, I asked him if I should write the things he was to speak. And he answered E. K. at his right ear.
.... *If you wish.* Dee: His voice was much like a man's voice, neither deep nor hollow.

### Note.
->June 22, 23.<-

On Friday, and especially Saturday, E. K. had great temptations not to believe this Action, and was told by a voice how our instructors would use the quibbling of our disordered lives as an excuse to forsake us, and not to perform the former promises we expected from them.

<margin>The 24 Seniors of the Apocalypse.</margin>
A voice said, likewise, to him, that *A. L.* should not go to the Emperor’s Court for lack of money: for he should get none here. Likewise, it commanded him to go up into his study and he would show him all the results of the instructions we received. E. K. complained to me how he was thus grievously troubled by such means, and almost brought to despair. But I comforted him as well as I could (being inwardly most sorrowful myself) and made my moan to God by prayer when I was alone: for him, and for our cause. Moreover, he could not be 
<margin>The names of God. The Angels of the 4 angles.</margin>
persuaded by me that good Angels would undertake to help us to any relief by money or treasure: affirming that it belonged to the wicked ones, seeing they were the Lords of this world; and the kingdom of God was not of this world, etc. ... I said that the wicked were in the world and of the world: but the Elect were in the world, but not of the world.

<margin>John, chapter 15.</margin>
> *If you were of the world, the world would love its own: but because you are not of the world, but I have chosen you out of the world, therefore the world hates you.*

<margin>John, chapter 17.</margin>
> *Therefore I have given them your word, and the world has hated them, because they are not of the world, even as I am not of the world. I do not pray that you should take them out of the world, but that you should keep them from evil. They are not of the world, even as I am not of the world, etc.*

To be of the world was to be in love with the commerce of the vanities of this world and to follow them. And that money and riches were neutral things: good if they were well used, and evil if they were evilly used. And that, *all things worked together for good to those who are good;* therefore the godly (like the Patriarchs and many nowadays) might have money, but to use it, not abuse it: and that such is our case and necessary request to God, etc.

So that she might see what effort her worms can make, which, stirred up with fear and missing their mother, learn to hide themselves in the crevices of the earth. At length, after silence, the mother thrusts herself out and doubles her tongue (with the sound of which she is accustomed to call them). They come together and rejoice, twisting themselves in various ways about her body for joy. As a reward, she allows them to hang upon her back and so slithers to her hole, where she gathers the leaves of the earth; and after she has chewed them small and tender with her teeth and mingled them with the dust, she spits them out again and begins to lick them little by little, as though she were hungry—which she subtly does so that her worms might eat and forget their hunger.

Finally, in 20 days, they become large and as skillful in the characteristics of their kind... she (I say) leads them out into a fertile place, full of dew and full of bushes, and places apt to cover them, where they feed, dwell, observe their craft, and at last forsake their mother. ->**Thursday, † Kraków, July 5. In the morning, nearly 8 o'clock.**<-

*After the Lord’s Prayer was finished along with other extemporaneous prayers to God, and after the promise of the final words concerning the Angelic interpretation of those 14 invocations (which we received since last May 14) was repeated, Gabriel in his Chair and Nalvage finally appeared.*

Gabriel in his Chair, and Nalvage with the Table, or rather a Globe with the letters in it, etc.

$\triangle$. Blessed be our God always for his mercies: his graces be with us, now and ever.

E. K. Gabriel stands up.

Gab. ..... *It has been said to you often: persevere until the end.*

$\triangle$. God give us that ability.

Gab. ..... *And why is it said so? It is because you shall have many temptations and afflictions: after which come consolation and comfort.*

*If the smith tests and tempers his gold by fire, his intent is to excel in the work he has in hand: so that it might be tried, refined, and made suitable for the purpose for which it shall be used. Much more, do you think, does the God of wisdom forge, try, and beat out those whom he intends to use in the execution of his divine and eternal purposes. How therefore can you find fault with the Lord? How can you say he deals not justly with you, when he allows you to be tested to the uttermost? If you pay the uttermost farthing, are you not become free? If you feel affliction and temptation and withstand it, are you not the more pure? The more justified for the Vineyard and Harvest of the Lord? O yes, my Brethren; for the more the wise man is afflicted, the more he rejoices; and the greater his adversity is, the more he prospers.*

*Is it not written? No man comes to the Lord but he is justified, purified, and accepted. Whence therefore (if you seek to come before the Lord, that is to say, to appear, to be blessed) shall your justification or purifying arise? From your own nature it cannot, for you were born sinners. But through Christ you may, in whom you are justified through patience and resisting temptations. This is the true proof and touchstone of man. But it seems to me I hear you say, "O, if we were rich, or had the ability."*

<margin>
Our great privilege with God.
</margin>
*It is true that many men excel you in the dust of the earth; but in the fact that you speak with God through us, his Angels (that is to say, messengers), you are not only happy (a happiness which others lack) but you excel all the creatures of the Earth.*

*O my Brethren, their joy is a bittersweet; but the comfort that you have is eternal, is sweet, and is a food forever. Therefore, if you will be eternal and in perpetual comfort with joy, despise the world for the world's sake, and delight in God for his mercies. If you truly do this, then no tempest can prevail, no affliction can come amiss, nor can any burden be too heavy for you. For it is written: Christ is the joy of the blessed, whom the world treated with all evil.*

*O my Brethren, be contented and endure the world; for as Christ, in vanquishing the world, proved himself the Son of God, so shall you, in resisting her, at last overcome and be accounted the sons of God.*

God in Christ, of whom you are a follower. John Dee, be comforted, for you shall overcome.

Gab. ..... But unto you [E. K.] says the Lord, take heed how you meddle with hell, lest it swallow you. Have patience for a time.

E. K. Why should it be holy?
$\Delta$. ------ The Court is wherever the King is; so, where the Lord is present, the place is considered holy, and it is so.
E. K. Now they are out of the cloud.
$\Delta$. After this, they made another pause, longer than before.

# A true Relation of Dr. Dee's Actions with spirits, etc.

<meta>catchword: ner.</meta>

->Saturday, July 7. Morning, 6:15 am. Cracow.<-

*After the Lord's Prayer was finished, and other petitions both to God and to Ave himself, I requested Ave's judgment regarding my prayers made both to God and his good angels. After barely a quarter of an hour, he appeared.*

*Ave ...... If the words or truth of our testimony and message were, or were contained within the capacity of man, then might the Devil thrust himself in and simulate the Image of Truth: But because it is of Truth, and of him that bears testimony of himself, it can neither have affinity with the flesh, nor be spoken in this sense.*

*Look, thus, deceitfully, has the Devil entered into man.*

$\Delta$. Blessed be the Lord of all truth.

*Ave. ...... Therefore seeing the word is not corruptible, those that minister the word cannot dwell in corruption. I do not speak this without a cause, my brethren.*

$\Delta$. I pray you to proceed accordingly, so that we may know the cause, if it be your will: or else leaving this warning to us, to proceed to the matter wherein we required your helping hand to correct or confirm, or to do that which is beneficial.

*Ave. ...... For, which of you has sought the Lord, for the Lord's cause or sake?*

$\Delta$. That, God can judge.

*Ave. ...... Or in which of you has due obedience—either to the word, or unto us who are sanctified by the word—been faithfully performed?*

$\Delta$. I beseech you to notify my points of error and disobedience, so that I may amend them.

*Ave. ...... It may be, you will say, "we have labored, and we have watched, yes, we have called on the name of the Lord." What have you done that you ought not to do, yes, a thousand times more?*

$\Delta$. We boast nothing of any of our doings, nor claim anything by any perfection of our doings.

*Ave. ...... Shall the hireling say, "I have labored hard"? or does the good servant think he merits his wages? It is not so. But you do so; therefore you are neither worthy of your reward, nor the name of faithful servants.*

$\Delta$. No Lord, we claim nothing upon any merits; but fly unto your mercy, and that we crave and call for.

*Ave. ...... You do wickedly and unjustly: yes, you trust the Lord as you do yourselves: your faith is the faith of men, and not of the faithful.*

*Many things have I said to you from the beginning (says the God of Justice) which you have heard and not believed: But you tempt me, and provoke me; yes, you stir me up to be angry with you.*

$\Delta$. If your anger shall be on us, besides the sorrow of this world, temptations of the fiend, etc., then we are not able to endure.

...... *Answer me not, and hear what the Lord says to you: Satan laughs you to scorn; for he says to the Lord, standing before him, "Are these they whom you delivered from the great perils of the seas, and from the hands of the wicked, to whom the winds were a comfort, and your peculiar countenance a lantern?" But the Lord seems not to hear him: for he knows it is true.* <margin>Mercies of God shown to us.</margin> *My brethren, you seek the world more than you seek to perform the will of God: as though God could not rain gold and pearls among you: as though the breath of God were not able to beat down the whole earth before you. Oh, you faithless creatures: Oh, you hypocrites in the vineyard of the Lord: Oh, you unworthy servants of such a Master. Neither to Abraham, nor to Noah, nor to any other patriarchs or prophets, has God been more merciful than to you. To Abraham he said, "When I return at this time of the year, you shall have a son." To Noah he said, "Build yourself a ship: make up the Ark, thus and thus it shall be: for the people shall perish."*

<margin>Genesis 27.</margin> *You do not remember that Joseph was sold by his brethren; or if you do, it may be you think it is a fable: If you think it to be true, then consider how he escaped the pit; consider he was sold, and so became a bondman: But who changed the imagination and sense of his brethren? Who (I say) came between their tyranny and his innocence? What was he that made him free? That brought him before Pharaoh? Yes, and what is more, made him reign over Pharaoh: Was it not the same God who deals with you?*

*Oh, you of little faith, and starvelings, withered grass, and blasted willows: what and if you were in hell, could he not deliver you? If you become bondmen, cannot he make you free? If you be in prison, cannot he deliver you? Cannot he encompass your neck with a chain? But Satan says, "Look, they say they have a long journey: it is necessary that God comfort those who put their trust in him." Bravo! Oh, oh, you beggarly starvelings, has not the same God the same Raphael that he had... Yes, truly, a thousand hundreds, and a thousand and a hundred thousand thousands that are, and more than Raphael for the help and comfort of the faithful.*

*When Herod sought to kill the son of God, in that he was man: his Father delivered him not with a mighty wind, nor by beating down lords' palaces; but by a dream appeared to Joseph, saying, "Flee, Herod seeks the child's life." Note the manner of his warning, the manner.*

<summary>The spirit Ave rebukes John Dee and Edward Kelley for their lack of faith and misplaced priorities, comparing their current doubts to the miraculous deliverances of biblical figures like Joseph, Noah, and Abraham. Ave emphasizes that God's power to provide and protect is absolute, regardless of their worldly fears or physical circumstances.</summary>

Specific Temptations.

You shall enlighten me, and I will become a seer; I will see your creatures and will magnify you among them. Those who come to you have the same gate, and through the same gate descend those whom you send. Lord, they do not prescribe laws to you, so it is not fitting that I prescribe laws to them. What it pleases you to offer, they receive; so what it pleases them to offer to me, I will also receive. Behold, I say (O Lord): if I shall call upon them in your name, let it be done to me in mercy, as to the servant of the Highest. How, therefore, can the heavens enter into man's imagination? Your creatures are the glory of your countenance. # A true Relation of Dr. Dee's Actions with spirits, etc.

<margin>[Δ] There were no Kings in Enoch's time; Consider therefore how to ask about this doubt regarding this prophetical phrase. In Samuel I find chapter 8, that unjudged Nations had Kings long before Saul's time. Therefore there might be some in Enoch's time: or he prophesied of them.</margin>
[Δ] Kings: But to command Kings by a subjected commandment is not wisdom, unless it comes from you. Behold Lord, how shall I therefore ascend into the heavens? The air will not carry me, but resists my folly; I fall down, for I am of the earth. Therefore, O you very Light and true Comfort, who can, and may, and do command the heavens; Behold, I offer these Tables to you. Command them as it pleases you: and O you Ministers, and true lights of understanding, governing this earthly frame and the elements wherein we live, do for me as for the servant of the Lord: and to whom it has pleased the Lord to talk of you.

<margin>Ave. three times a day.</margin>
Behold, Lord, you have appointed me 50 times; * Three times 50 times will I lift my hands to you. Let it be to me as it pleases you, and your holy Ministers. I require nothing but you, and that is to say, through you, and for your honor and glory: But I hope I shall be satisfied, and shall not die (as you have promised) until you gather the clouds together, and judge all things: when in a moment I shall be changed and dwell with you for ever.

*These words were a talk three times a day between Enoch and God: In the end of 50 days, there appeared to him those who are not now to be manifested nor spoken of: he enjoyed the fruit of his promise, and received the benefit of his faith. Here the wise may learn wisdom: for what does man do that is not corruptible?*

I have nothing more that I may say to you: But believe me, I have said great things to you: If you want me hereafter, I will come.

Δ —

..... Consider my words well, and what I have now said to you: for here you may learn wisdom, and also see what you have to do.

Δ. I will, if it pleases you, read over some of these Invitations which I have made and written here in this Book.

Ave. ...... You may not use that word *Obedientes* <note>Obedient</note>.

Δ. You spoke of a first word to call, and of a second to constrain.

Ave. ...... It signifies, it urges them more in God. I have spoken.
