# A true Relation of Dr. Dee's Actions with spirits, etc.

<margin>Of the second coming of Christ.</margin>
closed. So likewise the Scriptures speak of the coming of Christ, but the day and hour, the Son of man knows not. *But because in time to come, and for this action (the message of the highest), an assured and infallible Doctrine (in respect that God appointed you no certain time) is necessary. For this cause you waver, my brethren, and may lose the benefit of God's favor and mercies. O weaklings, examine the Prophets, look into the actions of the Apostles: There always went a promise before the end: But the end was the benefit and fruit of the promise. Some allege Paul, some Peter, some Daniel: But in this case shall you allege the sayings of God, spoken in the spirit of truth by me Gabriel, the servant of the highest. God, for three causes, hides the end and the very time of his heavenly purposes. As after a little silence you shall shortly hear.*

->E. K. A cloud covers him.<-
->E. K. Now he appears again.<-

Gab. ..... *First, by reason of his own inexplicable being and not being <note>Est & non est esse</note>, which is beyond the circumference, strength, capable virtue, and power of man's intellect, whereby he appears to be truly one God and incomprehensible.*
*Secondly, because Lucifer with his followers <note>yea sayers</note>, (justly damned) should never taste of his light, nor understand his secret judgments: which he would and might do if they were delivered to man's imagination and discourse, because it is within the circumference and scope of his creation. Consider these two.*

->E. K. Now he is covered in a white cloud again.<-

$\Delta$. The first reason or cause we do not sufficiently understand or conceive.
> God is being <note>Deus est esse</note>, to the Saints.
> God is not being <note>Non est esse</note>, to the Impious.
For, on the judgment day, God in his son Christ shall shut up his perpetual and everlasting justice, wrath, and anger with Hell and damnation. Leaving them and forsaking them, and in no case to be called their God. Brothers, [they] shall not have God <note>Fratres [mi] non habebunt Deum</note>. But they shall be without a guide and without a center. Hereby you may understand, *Being and not being*. To the purpose.
*Thirdly, that man, firmly persuaded of things spoken of by God above his capacity to come and unknown, might worthily in the strength of faith and through the effect of his promises merit his favor in Christ and receive eternal salvation, justly before God and his Angels. These are the three causes.*

$\Delta$. This last cause, if it would please you to make it plainer, it would greatly inform us and confirm us.

..... *These are the only three causes why the ends of God's determinations are secret.*
**1.** *In the first, that God might appear omnipotent.*
**2.** *In the second, sealed up in himself from the knowledge of such as have rebelled to their destruction.*
**3.** *In the third, that man might justly be made worthy of the places prepared for him.*
<margin>Wednesday following.</margin>
*Nalvage is called away and cannot be in action with you until Wednesday. Then shall you have the Calls that you look for. And so enter into the knowledge and perfect understanding of the 49 Gates and Tables if you will.*

$\Delta$. O Lord, may your will and mercy be shown upon us.
Gab. ..... *But understand that it is a labor, the hardest and the last.*
$\Delta$. To the determined, nothing is difficult <note>Violenti nihil difficile</note>: God strengthen our will and faith.
Gab. .... *I have nothing else to say to you. But may God be merciful to you and forgive you your sins.*
$\Delta$. Amen.
Gab. ..... *And as you go from here, make haste.*
$\Delta$.
->E. K. He is gone.<-

$\Delta$. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, as it was in the beginning, is now and ever shall be, world without end, Amen.

$\Delta$. I read it .... ter from the beginning until now.

Ile. ..... *About what do you doubt?*

$\Delta$. Is it true that before the creation of man this kind of malediction was pronounced, or at what other time shall we understand it to have been spoken?

A voice. .... *It is true that one man weeds out another. To avoid which fault it is said, [love] your brother as yourself, after God.*

> One kingdom rises up against another, the servant against his master, the wicked son disdains his father. All this fell upon man when God cursed the earth: for, perfect love was taken from among them, and the spirit of malice came among them, to the intent they might be always at variance, and one weed out another; and so it must be, and shall be until the end. Answer me, why did God turn Adam out into the earth?

$\Delta$. Because he had transgressed the laws that were to be kept in Paradise.

<margin>If.</margin>
> .... *It is true. Then Adam, by offending, received punishment for his offense in that he was turned out into the earth. If he had been turned out to a blessed place, then you could not aptly say he was turned out, for he who is turned out goes to dishonor: even so Adam, from innocence through his fall, was turned out to corruption into a prison prepared for him beforehand, in case he offended. God (my brother) knew he would offend; he knew also how to dishonor him.*

<margin>Note. In the same instant, angelic watchmen, keepers, and princes of the earth.</margin>
> *As Jesus Christ brought all blessedness and comfort into the world, so did Adam, accursed, bring all misery and wretchedness into the world. And in the same instant when Adam was expelled, the Lord allowed the earth to be accursed for Adam's sake; and then the Lord said these things, and gave to the world her time, and placed over her keepers, watchmen, and princes for years, months, and days: [I am easy; you may understand my rule.]*

$\Delta$. Note: All this was answered by a voice concerning my question or doubt expressed before.

> ...... *After this, there was a great pause, during which time I discussed in my mind the angelic ministry—that not all of it had been committed to their charge at their creation, but afterward at various times and in various offices, both toward God and man.*

A voice. ..... *Tomorrow morning I will meet you here at the third hour.*

->A N N O  1584.<-

On *Wednesday*, the first day of *August*, in the afternoon (*at 3 o'clock*), we entered on our journey toward *Prague*, in the Kingdom of *Bohemia*, where we arrived on the *Thursday* a week later, by three o'clock—that is, exactly in eight days.

We traveled by coach—I, *E. K.* and his brother, and *Edmond Hilton*—so that we came to *Prague on August 9th* by the new calendar; but by the old calendar, it was *July 30th*, two days before *August* in the old calendar.

->P R A G U E  1584.<-

On *Wednesday, August 15th*, we began on the day of the Assumption of the blessed *Virgin Mary*, in the excellent little *stove* <note>A heated room or study</note>, or study, of *Dr. Hájek's* house, which he lent to me, by *Bethlehem* in Old *Prague*. This study seemed in times past (in the year 1518) to have been the study of some student, or <unclear>A--</unclear> skillful in the holy stone. A name was noted in various places of the study in letters of gold and silver: *Simon Baccalaureus Pragensis*. Among many other things written very fairly in the study (and very many hierarchical notes *philosophical*, involving birds, fish, flowers, fruit, leaves, and six vessels for the philosophers' works), these verses were over the door:

> *Immortale Decus par gloriaque illi debentur*
> *Cujus ab ingenio est discolor hic paries.*
> <note>Immortal honor and equal glory are owed to him, by whose genius this wall is of many colors.</note>

And regarding the philosophers' work (on the south side of the study), in three lines, the following was written at the top:

*Candida si rubeo mulier nupta sit marito: Mox complectuntur, Complexa concipiuntur. Per se solvuntur, per se quandoque perficiuntur: Ut duo quæ fuerant, unum in corpore fiant: Sunt duæ res primo, Sol cum Luna, tamen in imo, Confice, videbis, fit ab hiis lapis quoque Rebus.*

*Lunæ potentata, peregit Sol Rebis actu: Sol adit Lunam per medium, rem facit unam. Sol tendit velum, transit per ecliptica Cælum: Currit ubi Luna recurrit hunc denuo sublima. Ut sibi lux detur, in sole quæ retinetur. Nec abiit vere, sed vult ipsi commanere: illustrans certe defunctum corpus aperte: Si Rebus scires, quid esset tu reperires. Hæc ars est cara, brevis, levis atque rara. Ars nostra est Ludus puero, labor mulierum; scitote omnes filii artis hujus, quod nemo potest colligere fructus nostri Elixiris, nisi per introitum nostri lapidis Elementati, etsi aliam viam quærit, viam nunquam intrabit nec attinget. Rubigo est Opus, quod fit ex solo auro, dum intraverit in suam humiditatem.* And so it ended.

A. <image-desc>Decorative initial F with floral and beast motifs</image-desc> It may be that the calculation of the year 1588, and of other years, takes its beginning from the very day of the Passion of Christ or His Ascension into Heaven. Therefore, add <margin>A note concerning the Year.</margin> 34 to the year 1588, and from that emerges the year 1622. This number comes closer to the time of the years of the flood and the Ark; the significance of this number around the second coming of Christ is taught by the Scriptures:
Or, if after the creation of Adam, in the Year of the World 1655, a Flood of Water destroyed all living things, then after the restoration of Christ (our spiritual Adam) into Heaven, in the Year 1655 (which will be in the year 1688), we expect a Flood of fire, by which all things are to be changed—or a great future example of Christian Charity and fervor.

But those whose minds are illuminated by the light of Divine truth, and who are more attentive to considering the multiple consequences of things separated by long intervals, will most clearly perceive those things which must have preceded as necessary causes and occasions at another earlier, and sometimes very different, time. And to omit now the variety of examples (which I could bring from the lives, conditions, and deeds of other men compared among themselves), this single, sufficiently clear example may serve: namely, that (almost incredible) combination and Divine conspiracy which now seems to be imminent between your sacred Imperial Majesty and your most humble servant (in God), arising from multiple preceding occasions on both sides. Two most illustrious Emperors sought me out as a young man: the most victorious *Charles V*, and his brother *Ferdinand*, your Imperial Majesty's most magnificent grandfather. $\Delta$. Welcome be the light of the Highest.

<margin>* Something is perhaps missing.</margin>
URIEL. ...... *Woe be to the world: for her light is taken away. Woe, woe be to man, for the eye of light has forsaken him. Woe, woe be to the understanding of man, for it is led out with a threefold spirit,* <margin>The Spirit of Pride. This Testimony is to be believed upon great displeasure, etc.</margin> \* *the spirit of error and ignorance. And woe be to such as do not believe the glorious and supereminent light of this Testimony: for they are not written with the life, nor shall their portion be with the living.*

<margin>Heavens of Glory, Chastity, Angels.</margin>
*Thus says he that is a mere stone (who sits between the seat of light and darkness), whose wings are great and more than mighty, with which he gathers the stars and the powers that hang upon the firmament of the first and lesser light: placing them and powering them in the Spirit of Truth; and through his own power—the power of the word, by which all things are and are comprehended—in that he is as much in the heavens of Glory, Chastity, and Message, as also in places unknown to us.*

*Behold, those who dig into Nature with dull mattocks and dull spades are such as can imagine but not judge regarding every congealed substance: they are foolish and of the world; their imaginations have become the instruments of vanity and the piercers of him who is the father of ignorance. Woe be to them, for their disputations and doctrines are dogmas and dull. Woe, woe to them, for they are such as please themselves and have become fathers to many wicked children, of whom it is written: They have become stiff-necked and proud, and the followers of their father. Therefore have I gathered myself together and am hidden from them, because they are proud and haters of innocence. These do not teach a doctrine to you, nor are you partakers of their banquets; for the Spirit of God is plain, pure, and most perfect. These do not breathe upon you, nor are the ornaments of your garlands interlaced by these. But by him are you lifted up, who is the God of Justice, the discloser of his own secrets, and the headlong drawer of things to an end.*

<margin>God to us is the discloser of his own secrets.</margin>
*Therefore believe, and do not dream with the world: For the world shall perish, and all her adherents, and shall be cast into the pit of everlasting woe. Read the Scriptures and understand them, but do not twist them with the wicked. Look into the simplicity and nakedness of God’s promise. View the innocence of some who received them, and let not the wickedness of those whom the Lord made virtuous go out of your remembrance. But so triumphs true power; so he gathers himself together to discomfort the Serpent. Of the lightest he makes the heaviest, and of the weakest the strongest; and in the weakest vessels he works his mercy. And why? Behold, lest the world, in her proud imaginations, in the ornaments of her pearls and most precious wits, should brag, saying: I can compare with the Lord. Hear my voice, for it is of God. The world brings forth no good thing, nor are the doings of man accepted, except where the spirit of humility dwells. Out of the depth of darkness, God has made light; and lo, the light is great, and the darkness does not comprehend it. So, in the weakest will he be exalted.*
<margin>Humility.</margin>

<margin>Uriel has a Tower to build, etc. Δ and E. K.</margin>
*The Spirit that speaks to you is he who has a tower to build, a strong tower and a mighty one; yes, such a one as has not been from the beginning: no, not from the beginning. Great is the foundation of it, for it is of iron; but greater are her walls, for they are of diamond. Most great are her turrets, for they are the seven heads that behold, judge, and gather; and they are made of Truth, the Spirit of Eternity. You are made privy to the laying of every stone, and you are provided for this tower.*

1. *For lo, the first has appeared and showed himself mightily.*
<margin>First Son, the Holy Spirit.</margin>

3. *And lo, the third appears and shall visibly show the power of God to all nations.*

<margin>The desolation of which the Prophet spoke. Revelation, chapter 18. F.</margin>
*For now comes the desolation of the world and the fall of her pride. And this is the last rod that measures, and it shall be broken. For it is said: Now I will hear you from under the altar; now I will revenge the blood of your brethren.*

*O you ignorant and of weak faith: Do you not know the times that are to come? O you that spit out the meat of comfort, even when it is put lovingly into your mouths. Why are you sorrowful? Why do you not rejoice that the God of Justice is girded and has whetted his sword upon a thousand thousand mountains of fire? Why do you not laugh the world to scorn and deride her fornication? Do not weep over her, for she is accursed; nor wonder at her, for she will be more wonderful.*

<margin>2.</margin>
Uriel. ...... There are others who go the middle way, because it is the closest and straightest, and those are such as enter with their own ornaments, which are very poor and bare, and upon whose garments no pleasure can hang.

<margin>3. Note. The indispensable cause, and the immediate and proper cause, as they differ here.</margin>
Some there are that enter [1] from me (for without me no one enters into that Garden); and because I am the light of him who gives light by Creation, there is therefore a perfect way that bears testimony from me, by which they are thought worthy and are [2] clothed for that place of pleasure, and so enter worthily.
Look, they enrich themselves, being made rich with the beauty of such pleasant flowers: and they always drink of the water of wisdom for their comfort and endurance. Blessed is he who enters in this way.

<margin>A Defiler of the flowers. The Garden of Wisdom.</margin>
1. He who defiles the flowers was worthy to enter into our Garden: but because he did not come here to my Throne, and so took the way descending from the Hill <note>to me</note> and brought his worldly apparel into the Garden of Wisdom; which, look, is always like a mist between him and true wisdom, yet he thinks himself satisfied.

2. He whose coat is bare was also worthy: But because he thought himself worthy and did not visit my seat, he took the middle way, where there are no ornaments. Therefore he brought in his own nakedness, which is so threadbare that the flowers fall off it as from a marble stone, and the water glides off it as from the back of a falcon.
Behold, I sit: happy are those who come to me.

<margin>Three types of wise men. Fury and Revenge. Open to Rudolph.</margin>
Look, you see, you may become wise: wise with the [1] cloudy, wise with the [2] bare, and wise with those who are [3] advanced; and dwell in true wisdom.
The Gate that you shall enter into is a fire of fury and of revenge:
But let it be to you according to your choice. Even from the beginning, nakedly.

After dinner, as we [E. K. and $\Delta$] were in my study and discussing my choice, being very sorry that we had not chosen the best, E. K. saw *Uriel* in the stone, which still stood unpacked; and he said he had seen him there ever since we began. So, coming to the stone, he spoke as follows:

### Friday, August 24, Afternoon. Prague.

Being directed to deal with Rudolph, first by letter and then by speech, I thought it best to send the letter written previously for the Emperor by the noble Don Wilhelm de St. Clemente, the King of Spain's Ambassador [term: *Præfectus Negotiorum*] to this Emperor. Thereupon, by Emericus Sonntag, Lord Laski's secretary, I wrote this to the aforementioned Don Clemente and sent it on this St. Bartholomew's Day.

<margin><unclear>Answer / good / angel / ...</unclear></margin>
Such is the condition of men on earth (most noble man) that no one seems to be born for himself alone: indeed, no one receives all things that are most necessary for him as if they grew spontaneously or were offered freely by others. From this, mutual societies of men have emerged—mutual friendships, mutual labors, mutual gifts, the exchange of things, and contracts for buying and selling. Various other states of men exist, from which multiple duties and trades are arranged among and with men. Nor is the sole utility or (perishing) pleasure of all these the goal or end which they strive and study to reach: but some have another purpose, which is indeed Divine, which we can call Virtue or Honesty; which, sent down from heaven, enters and adorns the minds of men and fits them to itself, so that it makes them worthy of heavenly seats. 

That, that, therefore, most illustrious man, is what made your excellence so attentive, kind, and humane to me yesterday; that is what will refresh your memory and notably sharpen your wit in my cause, to be proposed and commended to his Imperial Majesty. It should be handled in that manner in which those secrets ought to be handled, which are believed by few and understood by fewer—though they are most true and in themselves most useful. The sooner his Imperial Majesty embraces this wonderful and greatest goodness of God (not only His providence), the sooner and more abundantly the sincerity, goodness, and utility of my mission to him will be established. I would indeed have wished to bring this enclosed booklet and these enclosed letters to your excellence myself. But (if I may say so) because of a hurt on the skin of my toe, I cannot so conveniently come on foot today. Therefore, I have placed this burden on my friend so that (with the kissing of your excellence's hands) he may offer all my services to you and deliver this small gift, whatever it is, for his Imperial Majesty.
<margin>Prague, 24 August 1584.
John Dee.</margin>

### Monday, August 27. In the morning around 9:00. † Prague.

After prayers were finished, I propounded four things to God, through Madimi.
First, what was the cause of the error recorded on February 18, 1584, at Łasko concerning the death of Sir Henry Sidney?
Secondly, In what sense is this to be understood, which Madimi willed me to say to Rudolph: *An Angel of the Lord has appeared unto me?*
Thirdly, Madimi said concerning the time for my wife, children, and household to be moved here: *Let that be my charge to answer you.*
Fourthly, Madimi willed me to write to Rudolph: And I have done so, and caused it to be delivered to Don Wilhelm de St. Clemente, the Spanish Ambassador, to deliver it to the Emperor.

-> May God prosper it. Amen. <-

## E. K. Here she is.

$\Delta$. The eternal roots of truth bring forth fruit for the comfort of those who delight in pure truth for the service of God, etc. And you Madimi, as a Minister of the Highest in truth, are welcome to me.

<margin>
The essential cause.
Note this phrase concerning sound.
</margin>
Madimi. ...... Just as a man's fingers [or a thing] touching, moving, or forcing a musical instrument is the cause without which it cannot sound or drink up the air; which again seeking an exit and feeling a stay, is the [object] cause of concord or dissonance, according to the inward spirit and imagination of the thing that moves, or of the finger moving: So the earthly part of man, which has no motion of itself (radically), moves by the touch or finger (of whatever sort) of the spiritual, and sends out sounds; not according to itself, but according to the fiery, indeed invisible, and spiritual power by which it is moved.

<margin>
Three movers in man concurring.
$\odot$ Splendor in all moving.
</margin>
By this we learn that man's body and his organic motions have three types of movers: centrally, by the property and perfection of the Soul; from above, and by descent, from the Angels or participants of understanding; and on the contrary, and ascending, wicked spirits and tempters, using the soul as a root or first cause of the motion.

<margin>
On the day of the setting light of the moon, even above the horizon.
Note the manner of the Diabolical working in, or by man.
</margin>
But here you must note that as the Sun deprives the Moon in respect to her end, which is to give light, but not of herself; so do the Angels and higher powers drown and overshadow the soul in man when they are present: working from God and in themselves (as from above) and not through the soul as any root or first cause of the motion.
But when the Devil enters and ascends, he works not by force, but by enticement, and so allures the soul to grant him possession: whereby he enters and becomes strong.
Those who have ears, let them hear; for my words are wisdom and the foundations of many sciences.

<margin>
The world, the human body, etc., are like wax.
Impression { Superior, Human, Inferior.
</margin>
Then, by a metaphor, the world is wax: Man's body is wax: and the natural motions of things, naturally extended, are wax also: But our purpose concerns man; who at one instant receives three impressions: Missive, Natural, and Offensive.

<margin>
Pray against Temptation.
The predominant impression is to be considered.
$\Delta$. By the same things through which a man sins, he is punished: he who said "I will ascend," etc. Now from the infernal state, he always tempts by ascending.
</margin>
By this you may perceive that man greatly needs to pray against temptation: For the last Seal is the sign of him who owns the wax. Happy are those who can watch and pray: for such are they who grant no room or interest to the wicked ascender.

...heard by the Spanish Ambassador; and also of my zealous mind towards his Grace. # A true Relation of Dr. Dee his Actions with spirits, &c.

I thought it good to record this letter here, so that the resulting outcome might be understood in light of its original cause (both divine and human) annexed to it.

->To the Illustrious and Magnificent Lord, Lord Octavius Spinola,<-
->most respected Lord of the stables and chambers of his sacred Imperial Majesty.<-

**I**llustrious and Magnificent Lord: I cannot give sufficient thanks to your Magnificence for the singular kindness and benevolence with which you welcomed me yesterday; I am a man unknown to you, but nevertheless most studious of virtue and truth. I have decided (God willing) to spend the rest of my life’s journey in this pursuit, so that his sacred *Imperial Majesty* may clearly perceive that the tremendous Majesty of Almighty God will be (almost) incredibly favorable to him. And although I see that his sacred *Imperial Majesty* is very often kept very busy with the multifaceted affairs of many regions, and cannot conveniently have the time, nor perhaps should he for any evident reason, for other causes—specifically those to be proposed by me to his sacred *Imperial Majesty*—NEVERTHELESS, if some way could be devised, according to the occasion of place, time, and matters, by which his sacred *Imperial Majesty* would deign to see those things in my possession or understand from me those things which would be pleasing to him, I would most willingly hear or receive information and judgment from your most Illustrious Magnificence in that matter. For I will be entirely devoted to this, so that in due time it may appear that I am and will be the most dedicated, devoted, and faithful servant of his sacred *Imperial Majesty*, for the service of Almighty God and his sacred *Imperial Majesty* (and especially for the illustration of the most holy Orthodox Catholic and Apostolic faith, and for the defense and expansion of the Christian Republic).

->September 4, 1584.<-

> *The flower of opportunity must be gathered early:*
> *For it will soon become withered.*

->*Your most Illustrious Magnificence’s*<-
->*Most ready servant,*<-
->*John Dee.*<-

<margin>* This was done on the following September 11.</margin>

->The Emperor’s Response, through Lord Spinola.<-

His Sacred Imperial Majesty has kindly understood what Mr. *John Dee* arranged to be proposed through his Majesty’s Chamberlain, Lord *Octavius Spinola*. To which, his Majesty has graciously resolved thus: That since he is not entirely fluent in the Latin language in every respect, and is moreover occupied with various and multifaceted business, he cannot always find the time for an audience. It seems best to his Majesty that the same Mr. *Dee* should be willing to treat with and entrust his business to the Magnificent Lord Doctor *Kurtz* (who is also of his Majesty’s secret council, is sufficiently faithful, and also possesses distinguished learning). His Majesty will see that this is announced to his aforementioned Counselor, *Kurtz*. However, if it should seem otherwise to Mr. *John Dee*, his Majesty will satisfy Mr. *Dee’s* desire in whatever way he can eventually manage through his busy schedule.

1584. September 12.

->*Emericus Sontag, by his own hand.*<-

$\Delta$. When nothing appeared or was heard for the space of a quarter of an hour, I suspected some of our misdeeds were the cause of the Lord refraining from answering. He said he was so reconciled to God that neither Satan nor any other wicked accuser could make him doubt God's mercy, etc. And he spoke very well regarding repentance, God’s mercies, His justice, and these Actions.

Indeed, he confessed that by reason of his own nature, he himself was an unsuitable person to come before the Emperor or Princes, etc., and therefore if it would please God to discharge him of further involvement, he might, by reason, seem well at ease, etc. At length, after an hour, Uriel appeared, but with a scarf before his face, as he had the last time.

->Thursday, September 13. Morning. † Prague.<-

Emericus brought himself into the sight of the Chamberlain, the Noble Octavius Spinola, as I directed him. And he called Emericus to him and told him that today Doctor Curtz should understand the Emperor's pleasure to confer with me, etc.
Around 10 o'clock in the morning, while Emericus was in the Ritters Stove (or Guard-Chamber), he saw Doctor Curtz come out from the Emperor.

---

->Friday, September 14. Morning, around 10.<-

I sent Emericus to Doctor Curtz's house in the *parva parte* <note>The Little Quarter of Prague</note> with my commendations; and to say that I previously understood from Doctor Hageck of Doctor Curtz's desire to be acquainted with me, which I was very glad of and desired. And now I trust that the Emperor's Majesty, by his authority, has given him orders to begin our acquaintance and (God willing) our perpetual friendship. The Doctor was at home, and to Emericus (stating the effect of my message noted before), the Doctor declared that he had previously sought various occasions to establish a friendship with me, etc., and that now he is very joyful for the occasion offered by the Emperor's Majesty. He said that today various affairs hindered the opportunity of our meeting, but tomorrow at any hour (of my choice) he would be ready to welcome me to his house. And so, with the usual phrase of offering all his services to my pleasure, he sent Emericus back to me with his answer.

> Whom God joins, let no man separate. Amen.
> Moreover, whom God and Caesar join, let them remain most closely joined. Amen.

---

->Saturday, September 15. Afternoon, (almost) at one o'clock. † Prague.<-

I came to the aforementioned (called Doctor) Curtz around one o'clock in the afternoon. He had been ready all day to have heard me if I would have had it; but I sent him word in the morning by Emericus that I would come to him in the afternoon (as I have now at this hour). Being come, he entertained me courteously, and since two chairs were at the table's end, he gave me the place of honor (with a friendly kind of earnestness). Then he told me that long ago in Germany, he had heard of my fame and had seen my writings, and that he was very glad for the opportunity of my coming to this city. He said that otherwise he was already desirous of my acquaintance, but especially seeing that the Emperor's Majesty *ore tenus* (for that was his phrase)—by the word of his own mouth—had commanded him to hear what I had to say to his Majesty.

<margin>Δ. The goal of my studies.</margin>
I began and declared my long course of study over forty years, always moving forward by degrees and desiring the best and purest truths in all kinds of studies I had undertaken. I mentioned that I had passed through as many as are commonly known, and more than are commonly heard of. But at length, I perceived that only God (and through His good Angels) could satisfy my desire, which was to understand the natures of all His creatures and the best way to use them for His divine honor and glory, the comfort of the elect, and also for the rebuke and confusion of the adversaries of His name and honor. In this, I had dealt in various ways, and at length found the mercies of God to be such that He sent me the instruction of Michael, Gabriel, Raphael, and Uriel, and various others of His good and faithful messengers. I told him I had brought books here (about 18 of them) to show him the manner of their proceedings, and that I thought it good to begin with the last book, which also most concerned the present Emperor Rudolph.

<margin>From Δ to Rudolph.</margin>
And so I did; and thus, moving lightly from book to book by degrees, I gave him a taste or sight of most of them, and also let him see the Stone brought to me by angelic ministry, etc.

<margin>My counsel to Doctor Curtz:</margin>
Once all things that I could show him in six hours had been seen and heard, he finally asked me what conclusion or summary report he should make to the Emperor. I answered that he should report according to what he had seen and heard; but if he would follow my counsel (being somewhat expert in these divine and angelical matters), I suggested that his Majesty should thank God for His great mercies and graces offered. I told him that I was one who most sincerely and faithfully gave his Majesty to understand the will of God in this matter, and that his Majesty should do as Mary (the blessed Virgin) did: lay up all these informations in his heart and say, *Ecce* <note>Behold</note>

## P R A G U E

<margin>Note: the Emperor is inclined to hear, etc.</margin>
On Monday and Tuesday, the 17th and 18th of September, I sent Emericus up to the Castle to wait for an answer regarding Doctor Curtz's report to the Emperor about what he had learned from me. (But on Monday, Octavius Spinola had sent into the town for Emericus and told him that the Emperor *cared and desired to understand my dealings with the Doctor.* Therefore, he asked Emericus if I had been with the Doctor, and he confirmed that I had. The Emperor will be glad of this, he said. And yet, as I began to note, when Emericus came before the Doctor on Tuesday in the *Ritters stove* <note>The Knights' Room or guard room</note>, not one word was spoken to him about whether he had spoken to the Emperor or not.) <margin>I suspect the Doctor does not deal sincerely.</margin> Therefore, I suspect that the Doctor is not dealing honestly, faithfully, or wisely in this very weighty case. And since he told me that his Majesty the Emperor was persuaded that he was pious, etc., perhaps he would be reluctant now to introduce me to speak with the Emperor, seeing that both he and the rest of his counsel were convinced of the contrary regarding this King. Consequently, this great delay might follow from an unfavorable report made to the Emperor, etc.

# A true Relation of Dr. Dee his Actions with Spirits, &c.

Behold the words of Christ, unto the subtle (your father is a liar from the beginning, and the Devil.)
1. Listen to my voice: He that [1] teaches false doctrine, opens [2] his mouth against truth, or defrauds [3] his brother is a liar, and shall not be forgiven.
2. For first, he sins against his Creator, who created all things in truth.
3. Secondly, he offends against the truth and his Redeemer, who is the son of God, the true Christ.
4. Thirdly, he offends against the spirit of God (of the Father and the Son), the Holy Ghost: which shall not be forgiven. And therefore he incurs the rigor of God’s justice, his eternal damnation.
But, I say, give ear to my words: For I will sift the dust and find out the Pearl that for a long time has lain trodden under feet.

->I will come again.<-

->E. K. He is gone.<-

$\Delta$. We read over the premises, and so expected the rest.

->E. K. He is here again.<-

<margin>
Objection.
Solution.
</margin>
Uriel. .... Now let us join these things together.
*All flesh offends and is a liar.* Who, therefore, shall be saved or escape eternal damnation?
*It is he (I say) who, when he has lied and spoken against the truth, does not stubbornly drown and keep down his sin in silence.*

<margin>
A Lie.
The Dignity and Authority of the Church.
</margin>
For lying deserves the vengeance of the Trinity. But he who is willfully stubborn seals up his own damnation. For this cause (my brothers), and to the intent that the mercies of God might always be ready for sinners, he has provided the light and comfort of his spirit, left as a continual worker in the Church and spouse of Christ.

<margin>
Reconciliation to the Church.
</margin>
I teach you briefly: that whoever, opening his mouth against the spirit of truth and with willful stubbornness continues in his lying without reconciliation to the Church, sins against the Holy Ghost and shall be damned eternally.

->I come again.<-

->E. K. He is gone.<-

->E. K. He is here again.<-

Uriel. .... Be now therefore admonished (I say), be warned: And considering you are sinners, acknowledge your offenses, lest in the end your sin be against the Holy Ghost, and so not to be forgiven. But herein they err with you who explain the Scriptures, saying that man sins and cannot be forgiven because he sins against the Holy Ghost.
I teach you, my brothers: that there is no sin against God but it is against the Holy Ghost:

<margin>
Willful silence.
Final impenitence.
Angelic witnesses.
</margin>
If it so happens that, in the end, it is shut up with willful silence.
Whenever (therefore) you have offended, acknowledge, I say, your sins before God and his Angels: That God may forgive you, and the Angels bear witness to your forgiveness; and do not shut up your sins in stubborn silence.

<margin>
Stubborn silence.
* Psalm.
Go to the Church.
</margin>
If you commit adultery, if you blaspheme the name of God, if you are a liar; yes, if you speak against the truth; yes, if you say there is no God (as the * foolish do), do not despair, saying, "I have sinned against the Holy Ghost because I am a sinner and a blasphemer of the name of God, because I have spoken and opened my mouth against the spirit of truth." But go to the Church, which is governed by the spirit of God, and there with hearty and open confession disclose and make plain your offenses, so that the Holy Ghost may bear witness in the spouse and Church of Christ that you have not sinned against him to eternal death: Because you are not drowned in stubborn silence.

<margin>
$\Delta$. Voluntary confession is contrary to stubborn silence.
Ears of God, Hands of God, See regarding Lazarus, John chapter 11.
</margin>
For although God bears witness of repentance—although he hears and opens his ears—yet consider also that he has hands and must untie those bonds with which you are bound. What are the hands of God but his spirit, with which he makes and created all things? Therefore, when you have cried out and are sorry, endeavor also to be lifted up by the hands of God.
Learn a comparison in Christ, who (signifying the power of his Church) commanded the offender to go and wash himself, and so he was made whole. I speak this for your [E.K.] instruction: I say also to you [E.K.], go and wash yourself: For you are a liar, you are a drunkard: And therefore you are a sinner. And if you persevere and hide your sins with willful silence stubbornly, then you seal yourself with the second brand and cannot be forgiven, because you sin against the Holy Ghost.

above.

Monday, September 24. Morning, at 8 o'clock. $\dagger$ Prague.

$\Delta$. At the first looking, Edward Kelley saw Uriel, but he was covered with his scarf, etc. Nevertheless, I said some prayers to God on my knees, and came and said here: *Send your light and your truth, O God: so that they may lead us to the mountain of Zion, etc.*

It is to be remembered that we returned to the show-stone for two reasons: the first because of the letter which I had written to the Emperor; I intended to go and show it to the Spanish Ambassador before I sent it to the Emperor, to have his opinion of it and also to have him deliver it. Secondly, because of foul, slanderous words which were spoken of me here at this Ambassador's table: that I was a conjurer and a bankrupt alchemist, and that I came here to get something from the Emperor; and that I had sold my goods and given the money to the Lord Laski, and that he had deceived me. Note: As I had finished this action and had come to my study door, Emericus had returned again from the Spanish Ambassador, to whom I had sent him, desiring to know when he might be at leisure for me. He had now sent me word by Emericus to come to dinner, and so he would have leisure, etc. For this I was very glad and went there to dinner. He caused me to be brought into his innermost study (where he himself was writing letters). And after I had complained of the injury and violence done to me by foul slanders, and that at his Honor's table (to which his Honor had replied on my behalf, and for which I most humbly and sincerely thanked him), I said that the Emperor's Majesty himself could bear me witness that I used this phrase to him: "I did not come for his riches," as in, *Non veni ad vos O Serenissime Cæsar propter divitias vestras, ut inde ego dives fierem, sed à Deo missus, non audeo aliter facere quam ejus ad vestram Cesaream Majestatem voluntatem declarare, &c.* <note>I did not come to you, O most Serene Caesar, on account of your riches, so that I might become rich from them, but being sent by God, I dare not do otherwise than declare His will to your Imperial Majesty, etc.</note> And therefore, how falsely they slandered me was evident. And because I perceive that Doctor Curtz has not dealt with me with the proper hospitality due to a stranger, or a student, or a mathematician, or as someone to whom (to my face) he gave great praise, as one long since of great fame in Germany and thus in his good estimation, etc. And least of all as one who offered such great courtesies to the Emperor's Majesty as he was made witness to: I thought it good to send this following letter to the Emperor's Majesty, and so I read it to him after dinner. Then I showed him the *Prague or Imperial Book* (Librum Pragensem sive Cesareum); and moreover the *Tenth Book* (whose former title was *The Third Part of the Sixth Mystical Book*), and there showed him various actions already translated into Latin, because translating them from English to him now seemed tedious to me and not as readily pleasant to him. All things on his part considered, his summary final conclusion was as follows, regarding the last offer in my letter as well as the great actions and divine purposes.

Regarding the first, he declared that he was lineally descended from the family of a gentleman who was unlearned at first, who left his wife, children, and family in <margin>The response of the Lord Ambassador of the King of Spain.</margin> *Majorca and ascended a hill there, and remained in that solitary place for a whole year; and at the year's end he came down, but so learned and wise that all who knew him before wondered at it.* And that the same man was called *Raymond Lullio*; and that he made that which is called the Philosophers' Stone, as in *England* (said he), I understand there is good record of it. "Therefore I see," said he, "that it is a truth and possible; and as He has granted the knowledge of it to one man, so He may grant it to another, etc." And as for the other higher matters, "I perceive that God intends some great matter in this world. But I am not able to judge or determine it; but I am of this mind: that in whatever way I can further the service of God, I will be ready and obedient, etc." And as for the Emperor's person himself, "I find him to be of a good nature, courteous, and a most zealously Catholic—indeed, ready to shed his blood in the cause if opportunity required. He understands Latin well and speaks it sufficiently well." "That is true," I said, "for he spoke many things well in Latin to me." "Moreover," he said, "concerning you, I saw him very well-disposed, making great account of your book, etc. Therefore you are not to regard these *Dutchmen's ill tongues*, who can hardly tolerate any stranger, etc."

Upon further matters that I had to show him, I offered to visit him whenever he was at leisure, being called or warned. And he, being desirous to see the Stone brought to me by an Angel, asked me to come to dinner tomorrow as well. I promised him I would, and so with thanks yielded to his Honor, I departed toward my lodging at *Bethlehem* in old *Prague*.

# A true Relation of Dr. Dee's Actions with Spirits, etc.

### The Copy of the aforementioned Letter to the Emperor.

Many (O Most Serene Caesar) and very great mysteries and secrets—concerning almost all of God's creatures, indeed of God himself, and many heavenly matters—have been faithfully, sincerely, and diligently declared and manifested by me (now, fourteen days ago) at your Imperial Majesty's command, in as much as could be done in the space of six hours. I am not so immodestly curious as to try to fish out what simple report was made to you (as if by an impartial judge of things) by that same person whom you wished to see, hear, and understand these things in my possession; nor what judgment was joined to that report; nor what censure of the whole process was devised; nor what caution in proceeding with me you were persuaded to take; nor what plan was entered upon and adopted for the form of your Imperial response. Nor am I anxious about your sacred Imperial Majesty’s prudent and gracious resolution regarding the premises in any other way or for any other reason than what befits me—a faithful, sincere, and devoted servant of Almighty God and (in God, and because of God) of your sacred Imperial Majesty.

I see, however (while I have yet received no response to the premises), that I am somewhat impelled by the stimulus of such deep silence to warn your Imperial Majesty a second time: Do not suspect or believe in any way that this divine mercy—offered by God, so unexpected, so great, so unheard of, so wonderful, so manifold, so necessary to the Imperial state and the Christian Republic, so certain, so ready, and which must be confirmed and administered to you in reality (if your sacred Imperial Majesty had willed it) by the faithful servant of Almighty God and your Imperial Majesty—is a matter of small importance, some human invention, or a diabolical fraud. For I greatly fear that the fury of Almighty God might be kindled by such a grave error on your Imperial Majesty's part; and I strongly dread lest, by rejecting this mercy of God, you provoke his indignant vengeance.

Wherefore, since I see that heaven itself and such heavenly mysteries are not yet of such great concern to your sacred Imperial Majesty as I had indeed hoped: I—rather than let God have no conspicuous judgment, argument, testimony, or experiment among men regarding this his (previously unheard of) Mercy offered to your Imperial Majesty; and rather than let my (often mentioned) faithfulness, sincerity, and devotion (or vow) toward God and your Imperial Majesty lack all credit and the strength of manifest truth among our posterity—in the Name of God and to his praise, honor, and glory, and so that I may satisfy your Most Serene Imperial Majesty’s heroic desire concerning that Blessed Stone (called the Philosophers' Stone) to be infallibly seen, possessed, and used: I declare to your sacred Imperial Majesty that I am able (by Divine help and favor) to produce that same stone.

And therefore, if your Imperial Majesty wishes in the meantime to hold me intimately dear, and if you will deign to treat me graciously according to the dignity of such a great mystery and benefit (to be most liberally and humbly presented to you by me)—honoring me with no other or higher title than what suits your Imperial Majesty’s Philosopher and Mathematician—I promise with these letters, by mouth and heart, and sacredly vow before Almighty God: that I will give that philosophical work, perfect in all its parts, into your Imperial hands (and without requiring your expenses to complete that work), and in the shortest time possible (by God’s will).

Concerning other secrets, I see that I must remain silent for now. But now I desire to understand your sacred Imperial Majesty's gracious, free, and constant will in the premises, and not otherwise than from your own gracious mouth or from your own Imperial letters. For I know of no one now worthy and fit who ought to become my <term>Mercury</term> [messenger] to your Imperial Majesty in these and other secrets of Nature and Art.

---

->Tuesday, September 25. Prague.<-

<note>I went to dinner with the Spanish Ambassador and carried with me the Stone brought to me by an Angel, and the fourth book, in which the manner of its bringing is expressed. I also carried with me the *Sixth Holy Mystical Book* (*Librum Sextum Sanctum Mysticum*).</note>

<margin>A Copy of the letters desired.</margin>
After dinner, when I had shown him these things, his final answer was that he truly believed the work to be done by a good Angel; but rather, that the matters were too great. Therefore (said I), they are for the service of God, and not only man. He said he was a sinner and not worthy to be private to [informed of], much less a participant in them; notwithstanding, whatever he can do therein that is acceptable to God, he would be most obedient to it. He desired a copy of the Emperor's aforementioned letters, so that he might consider the contents circumspectly before he should deliver them; to which I consented. Giving his Honor thanks, I departed.

<margin>E.K. is ready to go to England, as he claims.</margin>
After my return home, I found E. K. resolved to go from here tomorrow, to fetch his wife, and then straightway to *England*: which was a grief to me. But what can I do, but refer all to the mercies of God, upon whom I have called for wisdom with which to serve him? I have put my trust in the Lord; I have not murmured at any such pangs and temptations hitherto.

The mercies of the Highest be upon me, as I have put my trust in him.
->Amen.<-

<margin>Poverty.</margin>
Now were we (all) brought to great penury: not able without the Lord *Lasky’s*, or some heavenly help, to sustain our state any longer.

Besides this, I understood of the Queen’s displeasure at my departure, and of the Bishop of *London's* intent to have begun to accuse me of <term>Conjuration</term>, and so to have had the secret assistance of "you know whom."

->*Tu es Deus fortitudo mea, refugium meum Susceptor meus, & liberator meus.*<- <note>You are God my strength, my refuge, my sustainer, and my deliverer.</note>

### Wednesday, September 26. Before Noon. Prague.

<margin>Dr. Curtz.</margin>
About 10:30, Dr. *Curtz* sent Mr. *Simon Hageck’s* servant to find out where I was lodged: He had passed not far off in a lane on horseback himself while going into the Town, and so met Mr. *Simon Hageck* at the lane’s end, etc.

### Thursday, September 27. † Prague.

<margin>Dr. Curtz.</margin>
*Morning*: About 7:00, Dr. *Curtz’s* servant came from his Master to tell me that his Master would come to see me at 9:00.

At 9:00, Dr. *Curtz* came on horseback to me, to my lodging (at Doctor *Hageck’s* house by *Bethlehem*); he saluted my wife and little *Katharine*, my daughter. Mr. *Kelley* had hidden himself in his chamber, not being willing to be seen.

After he had come up into my little study and sat there, in Mr. *Kelley’s* usual place, and I in mine, I began to complain of the great injury done to me here. For I came as a sincere and faithful servant of the Emperor’s Majesty, intending all goodness and honor toward him—no hindrance, loss, or hurt. Neither did I come *propter divitias Caesaris mihi colligendas* <note>to collect for myself the riches of Caesar</note>, as I said expressly to his Majesty. I was, before I came here, of good name and fame, both in this Court and all over *Europe*, as you yourself, Mr. Doctor (I said), can bear me witness, as can various others in this Court. And yet here my name and fame should suffer shipwreck, where I thought I had been in a sure haven under my principal patron. It seems to me that great injury is done to me. I know no way to help it, but to give you warning of the envious, malicious backbiters who are also about this Court, so that as you find occasion, you might encounter this evil and foul monster that is intruding itself into so mighty a Prince's cause.

The Doctor seemed not to know what I meant. I told him that at a nobleman's table, there was someone of great account who said that there was an *Englishman* come to the Emperor’s: a bankrupt Alchemist, a Conjurer, and Necromancer, who had sold his own goods and given the money to Lord *Lasky*; *and that he had beguiled him*; and that now he would gladly get some of the Emperor's money from him, etc. The Doctor seemed greatly to dislike these slanderous words, and said that he never heard of any such, with some few more words about the wicked manner of backbiters.

After this, concerning the report made to the Emperor about what I had shown to him at his house (as is noted before), he said that he had made a plain and sincere report. To which the Emperor’s Majesty has (as yet) given no answer. "And to be plain with you," he said, "his Majesty thinks them almost either incredible or impossible, and would like some leisure to consider them. He is desirous to see those *Latin* Actions you showed me, or a copy of them, and especially that which contains a *paraphrase of the Apostle's Creed*." I answered that I would not deliver my books out of my hands. As for a copy of them, I would (at leisure) write it, so that his Majesty might have it. And then I told him further that because it was so long before I heard any word from him, I had letters ready to send to the Emperor’s Majesty to further declare my mind to him; I declared the tenor of them to him. He told me that about 3:00 in the afternoon, his man would go to the Court, and if I would send them then, his man <column-break/> should

He said that he had never seen it before; I told him then to take it with him to read, and that if I had another copy, I would give it to him, but I had none other but that. After this, with mutual courtesies offered on both sides (after the fashion of the world), he mounted his horse and returned home.

->Friday, September 28. Prague.<-

Intending to send the Emperor's letter (written here before) to his Majesty by my good friend, the Spanish Ambassador, I wrote this letter to send to the Ambassador on that behalf, and concerning the credibility of these actions.

->To the most Illustrious Lord, Lord Don William of Saint Clement, Ambassador of the most Serene and Catholic King of Spain to the Sacred Imperial Majesty, etc., his most respected Lord.<-

Illustrious and Magnificent Hero: This can be proved by many testimonies and examples, that those mysteries which (beyond the rules of common arts and sciences) are divinely revealed to men (even to those who are pious and sincere)—mysteries that are new and beyond the usual expectation of studies—are understood by very few with the greatest difficulty, or are hardly admitted without suspicion, or believed by most. But what kind of suspicion can there be in our actions (if a right and piously informed judgment is applied to them)? For wisdom has been faithfully, ardently, and constantly sought from Almighty God through prayers for many years now: this alone (at least as far as we are concerned) seems to be the root and occasion for obtaining such a great gift. But in His heavenly palace, determined and assigned before the world was founded, the mercy and grace of Almighty God toward us is to be considered the chief, solid, and immovable foundation of this so great a mystery. In this mystery, such introductory information shines through powerful and faithful angels concerning the secret counsels of God, both in the creation of the world and the natures of creatures and their true use, as well as in the present and soon-to-be future state of the world. And furthermore, concerning the holiness, dignity, and authority of the one Catholic Church (the most dear bride of Jesus Christ and our pious mother), as well as that in which there is the communion of saints and the remission of sins; and concerning many of God's great secrets and determinations not yet to be revealed by us. So far from any Christian (of sound mind) contending or even suspecting our mystical actions to be diabolical frauds, he would instead incredibly admire such a secret purpose of God, subdue human reason in examining the same, and most humbly and with the greatest trembling wish to confess that the admirable mercy of God toward His elect is manifest in these things. Indeed, so far in these matters, I find myself to be almost nothing other than the pen of a scribe, writing rapidly through me. For I am accustomed to note down most faithfully those things seen and heard (in my presence), sometimes letter for letter, sometimes word for word, sometimes receiving many words together (at the very moment they are delivered). But now into how many volumes has such labor of ours grown? From all of which we expect that fruit and success which He has ordained, to whose nod all things obey. These letters of mine to his Sacred Imperial Majesty: when your magnificence finds the first opportunity, if you will deign to present them most humbly in my name, I shall be relieved of a great burden (divinely) enjoined upon me, and by a great benefit of affection from your magnificence. In the meantime, while the answer of his Sacred Imperial Majesty to those letters is given (if it were to be waited for 14 or 16 days beforehand), or immediately after the answer is received (if I can receive it as quickly as the one I received last), I must prepare myself for the journey, in order to transfer my family, books, and some of my furniture here (before the harshness of winter). Where, with the gracious favor of the Imperial Majesty and under his Imperial protection, I might be ready from time to time to fulfill the will of Almighty God to the best of my ability, and to serve his Sacred Imperial Majesty faithfully (as his philosopher and mathematician).

->To your Illustrious Magnificence<-
->Most devotedly,<-
->John Dee.<-

I annexed to this a post-script, which follows:

### *Post-script.*

I thought it my duty, and considered it advisable, to inform your Magnificence in very few words that yesterday morning at nine o'clock, the excellent man and faithful Counselor to his *Imperial* Majesty, Dr. *Curtz*, most kindly visited me in my study and heated room near *Bethlehem*, where he could see that my current library consists of almost nothing else besides the Holy Gospels of God, the Sacred Bible, and the books of our own mysteries. I, however, in a humble manner (among my other complaints), complained about the long delay that has occurred; I said that I expected the Emperor's arrival during those days, and then that an Imperial response regarding these matters was to be received. He, indeed, asserted that he had reported what he had seen and heard (while with me) to his *Imperial Majesty* in the simplest manner, without adding any judgment of his own regarding them. But, he said, they seemed to the *Emperor* to be almost impossible or incredible. And regarding the giving of a response to me (in this matter), his *Imperial Majesty* still wished to deliberate with himself. Whereupon I mentioned these letters of mine to be sent to his Majesty, and I briefly explained their contents to him. He wanted to have them immediately, to be sent to his *Imperial Majesty* in the afternoon. I, however, said that I wished to wait a few days for the *Emperor’s* arrival. Then, after a very brief conversation between us about mathematical matters, and after giving him a certain geometric book to look over (published formerly by me and *Federico Commandino of Urbino*), and after mutual promises of kindness and goodwill on both sides, he departed.

->1584. Sept. 28.<-

->Friday, *October* 5.<-

In the afternoon, one of Doctor *Curtz’s* servants came from his master to tell me that his master would come to me tomorrow morning around seven, eight, or nine o'clock, as I wished, etc.

---

->Saturday, *October* 6. Morning.<-

Before seven o'clock, I thought it better to go to Doctor *Curtz* myself rather than allow him to come so far to see me, for several reasons. So I went to him and arrived before he was ready. When he was ready, he came out, but with a countenance not nearly as cheerful in welcoming me as he had at first. I guessed that he suspected I would take his words badly—the words he had to say to me from the Emperor. (After I had spoken somewhat of the book I lent him and another who had written something on the subject of the division of <term>superficies</term> <note>surfaces</note>, and he had told me that my book was the most excellent on that subject, he made a pause). He then began to divide his speech into two parts and said that: *his Imperial Majesty, regarding his sins (which I had reproved), is accustomed to consult a Confessor <term>Confessionarium</term> at appropriate times and places, and he does not despair of divine mercy. As for what concerned me, his Imperial Majesty was ready to favor and benefit me in whatever matter was subject to his authority.*

To this I answered and said: *I am sorry my words were understood or conceived by his Imperial Majesty in a sense other than how they should have been understood or conceived. For I did not desire to become his Confessor, but I was commanded to signify to him that his sins had been reproved from heaven, as I did. From this he could have drawn more consolation than from the advice of any of his friends or his Confessor rebuking his sins, for it declared the Lord God’s exceptional favor, etc. As for the grace his Imperial Majesty offered me, I accepted it most humbly. Now, however, the reason I desire to be honored with the title of Imperial Philosopher and Mathematician is manifold: both in respect to my secret service to the Emperor, and under that pretext to conceal my greater authority and favor among the Imperialists and my English countrymen, lest I seem to the former to be dealing in trifles and of no reputation, or appear to the latter to be a fit target against whom they might exercise their envy and most slanderous tongues with impunity, as they have begun to do, etc.*

I therefore prayed Dr. Curtz to advise his Imperial Majesty of the improper interpretation of those words by which his vices were reproved, etc. Then he spoke of the second letters to the Emperor, the substance of which he had heard from me and had sent a note and advice regarding them to his Majesty on the eve of *Michaelmas*, as he now said. He wished that they had been delivered before the Emperor had decided on the previous answer. "Those letters," I said, "are in the Spanish Ambassador's hands; and if he will not deliver them today, I will fetch them for you." "If you do," he said, "I will deliver them immediately, for at eight o'clock you shall find me in the *Ritter stove* <note>The Council Chamber or Chamber of Presence</note>, or hear of me there." Then I said, "I will go immediately to the Ambassador."

I went to the Spanish Ambassador and reported all that had passed between me and Dr. *Curtz*. He said that because of his various affairs, he had not had a good opportunity since receiving my letters to go to the Emperor’s Majesty. However, he determined to deliver my letters with his own hand to his Majesty today. So, having given thanks to his honor, I departed. I went to the *Ritter stove* (or Chamber of Presence) where I found none of the guards, but many people sitting outside. In the chamber were three or four people, one of whom went immediately into the privy chamber, and shortly after Dr. *Curtz* came out from the Emperor to see me. I asked him if he had told the Emperor of the grief I felt at his misunderstanding my words. He said, "Yes," and that the Emperor did not take it badly; and so we talked of various other things, walking up and down together for about a quarter of an hour. Among other things, I told him that the Lord Ambassador would deliver my letters himself to the Emperor’s Majesty; then I departed, and he returned to the Emperor in the privy chamber.

---

->Sunday, *October* 7. Morning, 7 o'clock.<-

I sent to the Lord Ambassador’s house, and there I learned that the Ambassador had delivered my letter to his Majesty yesterday, and that an answer was to be expected through Dr. *Curtz*.

After dinner, I went to Doctor *Curtz’s* home at his lodgings, and he had nothing yet to say regarding the letter delivered by the Lord Ambassador. But we fell into other talk, and I told him plainly that I had not lived obscurely until now, nor without care for maintaining and increasing my good fame and name. Therefore, if I should seem to be despised or disregarded here for my sincere dealings, or to be seen as only a trifler, I thought I would suffer a great injury. And I was sure that the Emperor’s Majesty was much ruled by him, and as he framed his judgment, so his Majesty very often resolved matters such as mine; wherefore if I were

...were not used in my affairs as was reasonable, and for the Emperor’s honor it should not be blamed on any other man but him, etc. He promised that he would deliver everything in the best words he could, in a friendly manner, etc. After this, he showed several of his labors and inventions, mathematical and especially arithmetical tables, both for his method by squares to obtain the minutes and seconds of astronomical observations, and also for improving *Nonnius's* <note>Pedro Nunes, a Portuguese mathematician</note> invention of the quadrant, dividing it into 90, 91, 92, 93, etc. I then revealed to him the secret of my glass for signaling in a dark night, etc. He said that discovery would be very acceptable to his Majesty; I told him that the glass was at *Cracovia* <note>Cracow</note>, and his Majesty should see it, God willing.

After this, I told him that I would very much like to have a passport, or safe conduct, to travel quietly and safely throughout any of the Emperor’s dominions. He thought his Majesty would willingly grant that and asked me to write three or four lines as I would have it, and he advised me thus:

> John Dee, Englishman, a most devoted servant of his most Serene Majesty, most humbly prays his Imperial Majesty that for his greater security in traveling through his Imperial Majesty’s vast empire, he would deign to grant him letters of safe conduct.
->John Dee.<-

When I returned home, I reconsidered that I would like the said passport, safe conduct, or letters of passage to be more extensive and beneficial—including my wife, children, family, servants, and all my goods—and to last for one whole year from the date of these documents, as follows:

---

->Wednesday, on Monday morning, October 8.<-

> John Dee, Englishman, a most devoted servant of his most Serene Majesty, most humbly prays his Sacred Imperial Majesty that his Sacred Imperial Majesty would deign to mercifully grant to the same John—for himself, his wife, his children, his family, his servants, his maids, and all his household goods—favorable and gracious letters of safe, quiet, and free passage through all and any parts and roads of his Imperial Majesty’s vast Empire, for the duration of a full year (following the date of these present documents).

->Year 1584, October 8.<- ->John Dee.<-

---

->Monday, October 8.<-

I went to Doctor Curtz with these last letters, neatly written, and I found him to be in the *Hofrat* chamber <note>Imperial Council Chamber</note> in council. While waiting until they rose (at half-past eight o'clock), he came out with my letters in his hand, which I had left with him last night. I showed him these latest ones, and he said they usually do not limit the time but make them indefinite. So he took the last version, and I received the previous letters back again. He went with them into the Privy Chamber. He said I would not need to send for the letters, but he would send them home by his man. I left him to go toward the Ambassador *Don Guillermo de San Clemente*, whom I found coming with the Spanish Ambassador (who had arrived three or four days earlier to give the Order of the Golden Fleece to the Emperor) and the Marshal of the Court to go to the Emperor immediately for an audience. As I stood in the courtyard of the Ambassador's lodging and the three of them arrived on horseback, my friend the Ambassador tipped his cap to me, as did the new Ambassador and the Marshal, twice very courteously. I saw it was no time to offer speech to the Ambassador regarding my thanks, taking leave, and inquiring about his wishes toward Lord *Lasky*; so, following them toward the court, I continued home toward my lodgings.

IN THE YEAR 1584, December 20 (Gregorian Style), we set forth—I, Mr. Kelly, Rowland my infant, with his nurse, and John Croker—in a horse-drawn coach which I had bought from Mr. Frizer, from Cracow toward Prague.

->P R A G U E.<-

December 30. We arrived in Prague in the afternoon.

<margin>December 31.</margin> I wrote to Don Gulielmo de Sancto Clement, the Spanish Ambassador, as follows:

Most illustrious and magnificent Hero, although I have not yet attended to my own private business—to arrange which I have, in the meantime while I was away from here, both endured many labors and incurred many expenses—nevertheless, I did not wish to keep the letters sent to your magnificence by that most noble Lord Palatine of Siradia in my possession for many hours after my return. This is so that I might not seem to fail in my duty in any respect, either toward your magnificence or toward the Lord Palatine himself. As for the progress of the incredible Mysteries, I have both things to say and there are many things for me to hear to clarify the cause of truth (despite any of its most unwilling adversaries). Regarding these matters, when it is appropriate, I will be most ready both to listen and to be heard, in a manner that will be most consistent with my sincerity and faithfulness toward his Imperial Majesty. In the meantime, I require an interval of a few free days, both to rent a house suitable for myself and my family (if possible) and to arrange other matters pertaining to my domestic affairs. May God, the Best and Greatest, deign to honor and bless your magnificence.

->Prague, the last day of December 1584.<-
->Of your most illustrious magnificence,<-
->Most obedient,<-
->John Dee:<-

# In the Year 1585, PRAGUE.
## FRIDAY,

January 4. I hired the house in Salt Street from the two sisters. But Mr. Christopher Christian, who had for a long time been Chancellor, or Registrar of old Prague, made the covenant or bargain with me. He had Anne, one of the sisters, as his wife, and the other sister, named Dorothea, had <note>The husband's name is missing in the original text.</note> as her husband. This Dorothea lived in the house and was to move to another house of her own close by, and to deliver to me and mine the whole house, with all the appurtenances of rooms and facilities; and I am to pay 70 Dollars for the year, and that quarterly (every 3 months expired) to pay the quarter's rent for it.

January 6. I wrote to Dr. Jacob Curtius, one of the Emperor's Privy Council, of whom the former records of Prague actions make abundant mention. A letter of his written to me on the 8th day of October, 1584, is at the beginning of the book written just before this one. The copy of the letter which I wrote now is this:

### To the illustrious and magnificent man, Lord Jacob Curtius, of the secret councils of his Sacred
### Imperial Majesty,
### my most esteemed Lord.

Illustrious and magnificent man. Whether I should be affected with greater joy from your good health and my safe return to Prague, or be tormented with grief by the insults fabricated against me in the meantime while I was away, and the various reproaches and excessive criticisms cast at me, could seem almost uncertain. What I determined to do, I have so far done: namely, I have now arranged for my furniture and my whole family to be brought here from Cracow, indeed with great labor and no small expense. Since my arrival, I have rented a house—such as it is—though with some difficulty. And in this present week, the nature of my business requires that all our things be moved there as quickly as possible, and my family and domestic affairs be settled in a basic way. In the meantime, I would have your magnificence earnestly entreated not to take it ill in any way that I have not yet visited you, and I hope I have accurately satisfied my duty in this regard; I hope that you are willing to agree with me that this saying has rightly and deservedly become a proverb:

->*Quick enough, if well enough.*<-

Not only were your letters to me at my departure a great comfort in the meantime, but even in my absence, your good opinion of me, often testified, has soothed me with great joy. Concerning the insults, then, and your letters and true opinion or judgment of me, when I have found suitable leisure (having finished my aforementioned business), I will come to your magnificence to speak further; and I will be most ready to do all that I can, so that it may be clear to you and to posterity that I have faithfully and sincerely (as I had intended) applied my mind to the excellent service of his Sacred Imperial Majesty.

->*Prague, January 6, 1585.*<-

### + Prague, In the Year 1585.

Saturday afternoon I moved completely from Doctor *Hajek's* house near *Bethlehem*, and came with all my household to the house which I had hired from the two sisters (who are married) not far from the Marketplace in old *Prague*.

<margin>January 14.</margin>
### Prague: The first action after the return.

Monday, around 9:00 a.m. With prayers to God poured out as usual, and having invoked the light and help of God to understand his truth and to handle it with virtue, etc.

<margin>
$\triangle$ LEVANAEL, as may appear in the last part of *February 5 following.* *E. K. Note:* The house is round on the outside and square on the inside.
</margin>
*E. K.* Here is $\triangle$ one with a veil before his face, as it were, a haircloth of ash color. I do not know him yet. I see a garden full of fruit of various sorts. In the middle of it is a place higher than the rest. On that place stands a round house; it has four corners [within] and four windows; and every window is round and has four round partitions, also round. It has four doors, and at the east door is one step, at the south two steps, at the north three, and at the west door, four steps. The first door is white, like crystal, transparent. The south door is red of a deep color, transparent. The north door is bright black, not to be seen through like the rest. The west is green, like an emerald stone; similarly, the south door is like a ruby. The doors are all plain. The house within (as it may be judged by the transparent doors) seems to be white and empty.

<margin>
1.
Fire.

2.
Water.
</margin>
*E. K.* He who has his face covered opens the east door, and all the house seems to be on fire, like a furnace. The fire within weaves and moves about the house and by the roof. Now he opens the west door, and there it appears as if all the house were a fountain full of water. And various streams run in that same water, of which one goes and comes as if it ebbed and flowed; this stream goes around all the rest by the sides of the house, that is, as it were, the ocean sea encompassing the world. The next stream within that moves from the four sides and forms (in a manner) four triangles, or rather cones, of water, whose tips are cut off (as it were) by the middle stream of water which occupies the middle or center of the house and is surrounded in a circular form.

Another type of stream exists which comes from the four corners of an innermost square, and so they run *diametrically* or *crosswise* toward that circular middle stream.

The middle stream seems to issue out at the very center of the place and to mount up, and making an arch of its course, seems to fall *circularly* into one circumference.

*E. K.* The fire also had diversity in it.

$\triangle$ I would you had noted the diversity of the fires also.

...... *Those that learn truly, learn by parts.*

*E. K.* The color of the water in the center is the purest white.

The waters of that Saint *Andrew's* Cross are like water colored somewhat like saffron. The waters of the triangles are somewhat like a watery blue, which appears most at the top of the arches of their flowing.

->For all spring otherwise.<-

The outermost water has the appearance of quicksilver, as if it were somewhat <term>mortified</term>.

E. K. They run at a great pace to the aforementioned rocky cave from which they first emerged. Now they come again with great mallets of iron and wedges. They knock their wedges (as we do with wood) and so break off great slabs of stone, like slate, and throw them down the hill.

One of them. What a thing is this, that this wedge is broken?

Another. We are in worse condition than ever we were.

E. K. Their wedges are broken, for the most part, and fire flies out of the stone in great abundance.

...... The nature of this stone is not to cleave. Therefore, if you have no other instruments, you must cease.

E. K. They are in great disquiet among themselves.

...... Those who go on a journey provide themselves clothes against all weathers. He who is worthy of the name of a Conqueror carries with him all engines of war. So should true laborers do, considering what they work in. For the Earth is a monster with many faces, and the receptacle of all variety. Go home, do not stand idle. Provide by arts for the hardness of nature, for the one sister weeps without the other.

E. K. They go away speedily.

...... They have their tools to harden and their steels to temper. It will be more than an hour's space before they return. Therefore, you may spend the time in your necessity, and use the time of day as you are accustomed or wont. I also must oversee them, or else their labor will be without fruit.

E. K. Now he is gone.

They make something like square holes and put in their wedges, and break up the rock or blackish stone (like <term>iron ore</term>, or <term>Magnes stone</term>) in roundish lumps as big as a two-penny loaf, about two or three inches thick. And so after the first digging, they fetch three or four cakes or pieces out of one hole, and then they go to another. Now one of them has fallen into the ground up to the armpits. Now another has fallen in to the knees. Now the house standing thereon begins to shake and waver from one side to the other. Now the men have gotten out of the holes they stuck in.

<margin>The fear of the Lord</margin>
