not the sin of concupiscence by consent (I speak this for your understanding.) Take heed, therefore, that you do not offend yourselves: for you must become little ones: and the power of the highest must abound in you.

He who offends his brother offends God: but he who offends his own innocence is abhorred by the Lord. Look, you are the children of promise, and in you is the mystery of a great and mighty Seal. Therefore study to humble yourselves, for humility is the root of innocence. But (my brothers) you cannot be innocent by nature, nor can you serve God in the imagination of the cleanness of your own flesh. Now (therefore) since you are fleshly, will you become innocent? Or how can you seek that which Nature has lost?

<margin>In Christ we may become innocent and be born anew.</margin>
The Scriptures teach you that in Christ you were born anew: And by him you may become innocent when you are cleansed in him. Therefore, if the state of your innocence remains in him, if in him you are renewed and made clean (being rotten and defiled), why do you not seek him as you should do?

No man who seeks the brightness of the Sun goes under the earth: neither does he creep into unknown caves. Tigers do not seek their prey upon the earth where there are no waters. Neither do eagles seek it upon the waters.

<margin>Temptation.</margin>
No more should you complain that the Lord tempts you, nor be offended when the world offends you.

Is it not said to you that you shall fight a great fight? What fight is it, my brothers, but a battle against the worldlings and the Devil?

<margin>Kings.</margin>
I say to you that Kings shall be offended by you.

The Sun does not cease, yet it shall cease; yes, it shall not be.

The lights of heaven keep their course; but they shall suddenly stagger and forget their long-worn way. Much more shall the wickedness of those who rise up against you have an end, for in them is no course but error, and the fire-brands of Satan are prepared in their own hands for their own destruction.

<margin>* Our victory shall be.</margin>

Behold, they are opposite to you because they are opposite to me: for I have gathered you from among them, and they have become your enemies. Since, therefore, they are your enemies (because you must fight against them): Be not grieved, therefore, when their wickedness offends you: But put on the armor of patience, and become innocent.

<margin>Ministers of truth.</margin>
Do you think that from the heavens can come the dew and life of all things? Even so, think also that no untruth comes from us.

Be therefore innocent and be not deceived by the flesh; cast reason aside, covered with her cloud: And lift yourself up in him—unto him (I say) who has lifted you from the doors of death, taken you out of the hands of butchers, and continued you as a member of his glory.

<margin>O, your great mercy, Lord.</margin>
Behold, I say to you, the brightness of Truth overshadows you. If, therefore, you dwell in truth, why should you be afraid? Considering that she conquers and resists all her enemies.

Behold, the world despises you; you also shall despise the world.

When the Angel of the Lord pours his wrath and vial upon the earth, and the enemies of the Son of God run in among the sheep; when the self-same plague that was in the land of Egypt rains in the houses of all who dwell upon the earth—those whom the Lord abhors; when the Lord with his hand shall gather up the fruits of the earth from them—where then shall be their honors? What then shall be done with money, with that harlot and strumpet of the earth? Of what value shall their love be then, or who shall regard their friendship?

*I am sufficient strength and will be your buckler; and if they intend evil, it shall rest upon them; yes, when they imagine it, it shall take hold within them. # A true Relation of Dr. Dee his Actions, with spirits, &c.

$\Delta$ Let us bless the Lord our God Almighty, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, *Amen*.

---

-> January 18. + Prague. <-
-> Friday morning, about 8:30 <-

After pouring out prayers to God, so that the Mysteries shown to us (yesterday) might be explained, and so that, once the outer layer of the letters is removed, the juice and spirit of the manifest truth might be made clear, etc., at last he appeared with the gray veil.

E. K. Here he is, upon a green endless plain field, and as I see out in the field, so the Heaven appears, and all the conditions of the air outside: but it seems to me that I am high above the earth, and see everything beneath me, as if it were in a valley.

$\dots \dots \dots$ Now what have you learned from that Lesson?

$\Delta$ We perceive the grace and favor of God, to deliver us Mysteries determined in outward terms, but in the fruitful inward truth, as yet unknown to us.

<margin>The use and fruit of the former Lessons.</margin>
$\dots \dots \dots$ Behold, I have delivered to you (*through the Will of God*) the true, perfect, and most plain science or understanding of all the lower creatures of God: their natures, their fellowship together, and their perfect joining together, which is fourfold.

*The first: the joining together of celestial influence and the creatures below. The second: the center of every essential body. The third: the combination of many parts or bodies converging toward one principle. The last: the true use and knowledge of every substance to be joined and distributed. Take a pause—*

<insert>[E. K. He speaks a language which I cannot sound out after him.]</insert>

$\Delta$ We read the premises and discussed them.

E. K. Now he is here again.

$\dots \dots \dots$ In the Lesson which I have taught you is this knowledge, with the rest contained. Therefore seek, and turn the earth upside down. Labor, so that you may receive fruit, for to him who works and has strength, strength shall be given, and the reward of a workman. Many years, the daughter of long time, are not necessary for the opening of this Mystery. Many months have nothing to do here: For lo, it is a labor of one day, for in one day you may understand how to tear this Lesson in pieces and to understand what every word signifies.

<margin>Note</margin>
But here, in the learning of this Lesson, three things are to be considered: the place that every word occupies; the place that every letter occupies, and the number that every word and letter refers to. For here, place and number are separate, and bear an image of the work that they treat of.

<margin>
Note
The place of words and letters.
The number of words and letters.
</margin>
But number and place must be joined together, and thereby you shall taste of that which follows: true wisdom.

<margin>The joining of number and place.</margin>
Be therefore diligent, and pray for the grace of God, so that you may learn and understand. Do not look for the manner of man's teaching in me; for I have nothing to do with man. See how you can digest this:

E. K. He has stepped aside. -> $\Delta$ I discoursed. <-

E. K. He is here again.

$\dots \dots \dots$ ¶ Now hear what I shall say to you. I will open to you a Mystery: the key and foundation for the entrance into and knowledge of divine wisdom, delivered to you in a tangible science, contained in letters and words placed out of order, like a Chaos; and therefore not to be understood except by being reduced to order and drawn into their places, and thereby understood.

<margin>Cabalistically</margin>
For you do not have a letter, nor the form of a letter, nor the place of a letter, but they are all counted with us, just as the stars are counted with God. The letters and words work into all reason, just as the stars do into the lower creatures: Therefore, as obedient scholars, humbly receive what I have to say to you, or shall open to you, while kneeling.

*First, praise God with me a little—* E. K. He is on his knees.

E. K. prayed the 142nd Psalm, *Lord, hear my prayer*, and I consented with my heart, and greatly rejoiced in the appropriateness of the prayer: as E. K.’s case chiefly required, and mine also.

.. .. I come again.

E. K. He is gone.

*Saturday.*
*January 19 Morning, 9:00.* Having looked into the Stone, he who was there yesterday immediately appeared. After prayers to God.
...... Hear what I shall say to you. The Word and Testament of Jesus Christ, the bread of life, left for the comfort and instruction of the faithful, is such that it informs according to the dignity and purity of Spirit in him who seeks to be informed. For why, the Holy Spirit helps not such as are lepers, nor heals such as are sick, unless they come seeking him truly for medicine.

Many read the Scriptures in the same manner (my brothers), but they are confounded, because they seek their own glory, and not the glory of him of whom they treat. Herein does Satan rejoice that the Word of God has become an instrument for him to spoil the life (and state to come) of man.

Herein does he rejoice, that with the same meat that God feeds, even with the self-same he confounds.

# A true Relation of Dr. Dee his Actions, with spirits, &c.

*Now then, if you are a man, then you are of the earth, earthy. But according to your likeness, grafted in the image of God in his Son Jesus, you are heavenly.*

*But behold, God is opposed to you, and his spirit does not clarify itself to you, in that you are flesh, in that you are earth, in that you are filthy: in that you are the children of Satan, and therefore take part with him against Christ, the anointed of the Lord.*

**E. K.** *He is out of sight now.*

*Now if you are opposite, or more contrary to the image of him who dwells in you—if you dwell in him—what are you doing here? Why do you presume to enter the doors of him to whom you are an adversary?*

<margin>Bread</margin>
*In this you show your ignorance and the lumpishness of your fragility, in that you seek from him to whom you are odious, or crave the bread which is due and necessary for his children and servants. But hear my voice: He gives to those who ask, but to the children and servants who ask, and not to strangers.*

*Nevertheless, out of his mercy, and because he knew before the beginning of all worlds the corruption of your vessels, and remembering that you have been of his household, he has mercifully winked at you and your presumption until now, and fed you with that bread which is not the bread of sinners.*

*But now, considering that you continue in your wickedness, continue in your rebellion against his Majesty, and fight daily under his banner which is accursed, he takes his bread from you, shuts his doors against you, warns his servants against you, and has become a firebrand of wrath against you.*

<margin>Upon condition.</margin>
*But here you will say: "Were we not among the number of those to whom he made a promise?" You were. But upon this condition: That you would bridle your tongues from speaking evil and become wholly his. But you are neither his, nor do you bridle your tongues; instead, you speak blasphemy before the Lord and the messengers of his light and covenant. Therefore, you are not inheritors of his promise. Behold, while the grapes grew and the corn ripened, God expected your return, for no hour is unacceptable to him.*

*But now the harvest comes when the corn must be cut down and the grapes pressed, and you are not as you said you would be, nor as you promised.*

*Therefore you are excluded, for no strangers come into the vineyard, nor do any hirelings come into this harvest, for it is not a harvest of man.*

Δ

*Now, either fulfill your promise and return from the multitude of your sins, or do not murmur even though you are shut out of doors.*

<margin>Hell.</margin>
*The earth of itself brings forth nothing, for it is the lump and excrement of darkness, whose bowels are a burning lake.*

*But where the heavens yield and the Sun pours down its force, she opens herself and becomes spongy, receiving a mixture for generation, and so is exalted above herself and brings forth for the use of man. Even so is the body when it lies in the puddle and hotchpotch of its earthly filthiness and darkness, making itself equal with beasts, whose dignity lies only in their use.*

**E. K.** Now he is here again.

*...... Two things you have to be instructed in: in <term>Rlodnr</term>, and in the Law of Coition and Mixture.*

*The first is the instrument working and drawing things of one nature together. The second is the bonds and limits within which every mixture consists, and beyond which it cannot go.*

*The first of 4 parts, every part containing, contains its contained double.*

*The first is <term>Tepens</term>; this teaches the rest.*

*I can open these two things to you in two revolutions, which is only one day's work.*

*But now I cease to reveal any more to you until I see the favor of God more open toward you.*

*After 7 days I will come again; until then, I neither exist nor speak.*

Δ *The mercies of God be upon us, now and ever, Amen.*

# A true relation of Dr. Dee his Actions, with Spirits, &c.

Do not harden your hearts against the Lord, nor exalt yourselves above him who has created you. But humble yourselves, and consider that you are flesh, mortal, transitory, and full of sin.

My brethren, my brethren, sin and flesh do not appear before the Lord, nor are those who are sinners and fleshly vessels suitable or fit for the Lord to dwell in.

Understand what the Lord is, and how great he is: a Judge to the wicked, great and terrible; a father to the holy and sincere, just, full of mercy, and loving kindness.

<margin>If</margin>
*If you now, therefore, are holy, and put on the garments of Innocence, and walk before him in righteousness; then expect to have the reward of Children; then look for his fatherly mercies and loving kindness; then, then rejoice at the garments of glory prepared for you.*

<margin>But if</margin>
*But if you seek him in judgment, and stir him up to wrath and anger: if you cause him to call the terrible thunders (provided for the wicked) around him, in the most furious flames of his indignation, to gather you together like whirlwinds; if you draw his holy Angel away from you, and strip you of your armor; if he sits down upon the mouth of vengeance and arms himself with righteousness against your wickedness.*

Then look for the horrible and unspeakable reward of the wicked, and the consuming fire of Justice, sharper than the two-edged sword.

Who has stood before the Lord in Justice? Or who dares to quarrel with the Highest? What flesh has seen the Lord in his Majesty? Or can appear before him as righteous?

Tear yourselves, therefore, into pieces, and fall down before the Lord; worship him as a father, and become his children: for his judgments (my brethren) are terrible, and his wrath is without measure. Many ways you are bound and tied to God, as you learn through discipline.

But there are three special ways you have been advanced by him more than your brothers or sisters have been:
The first is in the visitation wherewith he has comforted you, and exalted you above the worldly people, by his good, pure, and just Ministers of eternity and light.
Secondly, in that with his own hand—yes, with the wink of his own eye, beyond the ministry of Angels—he has in various ways protected you: defended you, yes, and snatched you from imminent and violent envy, and the prepared destruction of Satan, at home, abroad, and in various other ways, secret and not to be revealed.
Lastly, that by the means and ministry of those who are his good Angels and minister to him, he has guarded you from the wickedness of your own Country, and has brought you, ready to place you into the lap of a Virgin, with whom, if you take part, you shall ascend into that Jerusalem which shall descend, and there live forever.

Therefore, above all men, you ought to lift up the horn of the Lord, and blow his praises abroad.

Therefore, when others are full of idleness and the dalliances of sin, you ought to humble yourself upon the earth before the Lord, and praise his Name.

Therefore, even if all flesh forsook the Lord and cried out against his anointed, you ought to stand stiffly against the malice of the hills and be without fear.

O my brethren, therefore you ought (in very deed) to shake off your wickedness and to cleave (before the Lord) to the innocence of Angels, delighting in the one as eternal food and despising the other as a firebrand for Hell-fire and the wicked.

> $\Delta$ O Lord, *Velle adest nobis, ast absque tuo singulari favore, & auxilio non possumus perficere, quod ita debemus præstare. Igitur Deus.* <note>O Lord, the will is present with us, but without your singular favor and help, we cannot perform what we ought to provide. Therefore, O God.</note>

<margin>World.</margin>
Lo, behold, your humility is not; you are sealed to the World, and you measure the Lord according to the World; therefore, you shall be judged with the World. Therefore, the Lord shall sit in judgment against you.

> $\Delta$ O Lord, what does it profit us that we are born? Or what does it profit us that we have heard of the most merciful mysteries and promises of the Highest concerning our Election, if the Lord will not help us in our great frailty and misery? Where shall we become on the face of the earth? etc.

...... Hear me. Do not fret in spirit, for it is not in you. $\Delta$

E. K. Now a flame of fire flashes in my face.

<margin>$\Delta$ The abyss, the depth.</margin>
<margin>$\Delta$ Our appointed office.</margin>
> ...... O you of little faith! O you of little faith! O you of little faith! I have gathered you together as Prophets. But you fly from me. If I had known or foreseen that to sit on the seat of Kings had been suitable for you, or that having a residence or dwelling with the crafty Counselors of the Earth would have made you fit for me; if I had seen that pride in loathsome heaps of ill-gotten money could have sanctified you before me; then I could have lifted you up, placed you among the worldly-wise, or opened to you the depths of the Earth. But I provided for you against Kings, against Counselors, against the Governors of the World, to open my judgments and to bear witness to my power. But since you are so full of rebellion and will rise up against the Lord who made you, and disdain to take part with his holy Spirit so that you may be rectified and sanctified for the performance of his holy will; hear [$\Delta$] my voice.

<margin>Concerning the choosing of a new seer and future Nazirite of the Lord.</margin>
Take whomever you want, in whose face the Lord shall seem to dwell, and place him with this Seer, and let him stand seven times by him: I will take the spirit from him, and will give it to another—to the same one who stands by—and he shall have power to see: and he shall fulfill my word that I have begun. But if you do so, take care that no razor touches his head; but keep him for me.

I come again.

> Δ *O Lord God, you have joined us two together in your election, and what the Lord has joined, no fleshly whim of mine shall willingly separate. E. K. Here he is now.

E. K. He reveals his face, he puts on a white garment, he takes up the four corners of his garment, and puts them under a broad girdle he has: on his head is nothing but hair, reddish and waving.

E. K. He holds up his hands, and looks up to heaven, and seems to pray <term>exsentis manibus</term> <note>with outstretched hands</note>.

..... *If he IS, then it follows that nothing exists but that which is God. But God did not make all things (made and created) out of himself, nor from himself: therefore, he made them out of nothing.*

*Understand therefore, that God from the beginning, and beyond the beginning in himself—in himself as God—contained "I am" and "is," proper to himself and for himself. But also by the knowledge of himself, he contained also that Nothing, out of which (in his secret and determined purpose separated from himself) he intended to make all things. It follows necessarily, therefore, that that which was not—having no power of itself—must remain after the Image of "I AM," brought or knit together by the Wisdom of God, substantially in himself, whereby Jesus Christ appeared in his Godhead.*

*But behold, when God the Father and the Son, through one spiritual substance and illumination, from one center, had gathered together <term>Ictu Divino</term> <note>by a Divine stroke or flash</note> that <term>Nihil separable</term> <note>separable Nothing</note>.*

E. K. He seems to be consumed to ashes in a fire, and so lies as if in ashes, prostrate.

E. K. Now he is up again, I know not how.

E. K. He seems now to be very clear, and in a way transparent.

Δ I read, "But behold, when God," etc., as in the 8th line above.

..... *Then did he separate that Nothing from himself, and as it marvelously lay hidden in him, so marvelously and secretly he wrought upon it: Not in one instant, for then it would have been like himself.*

<margin>Time.</margin>
*But in time, which he first made out of nothing: which being consumed, Nothing shall return to the place from which it came. And that which has offended in nothing shall be a second, opposite from God, and out of God; which shall have continuance, world without end. And it shall be always vexed, the Spirit of God mediating: not of the substance or purity of God, or of his Spirit, but with the self-same Nothing out of which God created all things. Seeing therefore that the Will of God (which is his Image) separating Nothing from eternity, in time made all things (being the work of six days). [But I teach you a Mystery.]*

<margin>Angels Men's souls.</margin>
*All things that through God are moved to the Center by the Spirit of God (which is the center of the Godhead) are not—after the world and after the consummation of the world—to be reckoned with that Nothing, as Angels and the blessed souls are. But they are of God, because they dwell in him, of whom it is said: "There they shall not need the Sun nor the Moon, the Lamb himself shall be their light, and a shining lamp forever." Note here that the Trinity—first, second, and third—was totally unmoved except by himself, in himself; and time, bringing forth all things according to his Word, made all things except Man. Why? When all things had pleased him—not because they existed of themselves, but because by the Word (the Image of himself, and in which he is delighted) they were made—he made man, as the Scripture teaches you through the Spirit of God in Moses: that he should enjoy and use the benefit of all this "something" proceeding from "nothing" in the Creatures of God in their kind. He did this so that in him God might be glorified; not only in this world, which is your earth and vale of misery, but also and chiefly that the memory of his exceeding and great mercy and omnipotence might remain before him in heaven, in the image of man and the most excellent Creatures, world without end.*

E. K. Now he stands up again, as before.

# A true relation of Dr. Dee his Actions, with spirits, &c.

<margin>Creation of man.</margin>
...man, as a thing knit or tied in the curve of his own sphere, not sharing in "Nothing" materially, but in "Nothing" Immortal.

<margin>The soul of man; the Book of Esdras.</margin>
The soul was made spiritual and increasing, in which the philosophers—the wise men of this world—are deceived; and it has been a secret shut up in the Book of Esdras, not fit for the world.

<margin>Note on the soul's spiritual increase. A rare mystery.</margin>
For just as flesh, by the joining and mixing of similar things proper in their own nature, brings forth its own image; so does the most excellent part of man, sharing in the closeness of God (and so perpetually moving), bring forth every living soul after the manner of eternity; the Spirit of God (joined with the Trinity) working with him in his infinity.

<margin>$\Delta$ So that it may be said that God, as if by creating, and man, as if by generating, produces the human soul.</margin>
Behold, in the beginning, God did not formally number all souls that shall enter into these vessels, or other parts. But the material matter in himself he knows and has limited, beyond which—the material being deficient—there cannot be any. Therefore it is contained in number: not that it is contained in number to be counted, but within the proportion of number contained in the knowledge of Jesus Christ, sharing with man, and so to be numbered.

Adam fell; he transgressed God's commandment, and therefore was his soul darkened, bare, and naked, because he lacked the beauty and excellence of God's Spirit, with which God dignified him and made him like himself, being a living soul.

<margin>The Trinity distinct.</margin>
He was cast out, and now casts off misery, lacking the knowledge of those things for which he was created. Now God, the image of his Father, grieved at the fall of man and moved with pity, deigned—because of the excellence of man—to enter into man (having been previously separated) into this part of nothing, into man. Not that he would beautify himself with anything that man had, but that, having become man, begotten of the Holy Ghost, he might (as you know by the Scriptures) make man acceptable again to God his Father—God himself, with God in unity. For justice and terror is God the Father; mercy and love is God the Son; wisdom and knowledge is God the Holy Ghost.

He, since he became man, did not put on the flesh of man to become a liar, but so that the flesh of man might be full of the spirit of truth and understanding.

-> E. K. Now he has fallen again into ashes. <-
-> E. K. Now he is up again. <-

And so receive forgiveness of sins, and be at one with God—which is to say, in his favor—taking hold of God, not as created and from creation (sinful by the fall), but by ransom and redemption as bought and made free in Jesus Christ, who offered up the sacrifice of frankincense, gold, and myrrh, of true propitiation, for the living and the dead.

Now, my brethren, listen well to what I say to you.

The wisdom of the Father, in love, created and made man, dignifying him and exalting him as the lord and master over all mortal creatures. But how? By <term>plasmation</term> <note>shaping or formation</note>. For it is written, *Let us make man.*

<margin>Earth.</margin>
Here you also see the Scripture says that God took of the Earth. Mark this word, and consider it when I shall apply it.

Now if this power, if this shaping, if this taking—which was the Word—became man, perfect man; then it follows that man was and is, God creating and created. If therefore this conjunction or knitting together of God and man bears the image of him in excellence and power (who created all things, and by whom this "Nothing" was spread abroad and had form in its parts): then it follows that the self-same God and Man being truth, speaking of himself to his disciples, said, *This is my body.*

-> E. K. Now he has fallen again into ashes. <-
-> E. K. Now he is up again. <-

. . . . . Read.
$\Delta$ I read, *Now my brethren listen well, etc.*
-> E. K. Now he holds up his hands. <-

. . . . . did in the breaking of bread—which signifies the earth—signify in taking it the power of making and his own office; and breaking it before his disciples, according to the secret sense of man's soul, then being yet alive, gave himself in the bread, and in the breaking, to his disciples, as the sense of his word spoken.

-> E. K. He speaks things I do not understand. <-

. . . . . did import and truly signify himself, his very body, to suffer, and he suffered in that; in him, in his Godhead and wisdom before the worlds it was so: <gloss>his very true body and very true blood. But nevertheless mystically.</gloss> Consider this.

-> E. K. He is gone. <-

$\Delta$ Blessed be.
-> E. K. Now he is here again. <-

. . . . . Note here for whom, and to whom Christ took and broke bread; he also took the chalice and called it his blood of the New Testament, which shall be given.

<margin>Note: In faith and sacramentally.</margin>
Here you see that in faith, and sacramentally, it was given to his disciples there, which was also to be given upon the Cross for the redemption of mankind; for otherwise, why should he have said, *which shall be given*?

But here, my brethren, because it was to be given, it was to seal the perpetual and everlasting memory of it for the destruction of Satan and the comfort of his chosen. But in spirit, before this, he had pacified the wrath of his Father: Therefore it was given and to be given.

But to whom? To his disciples, and not to strangers; not to the Scribes and Pharisees, but to those who grasped him through faith.

Here you see that to grasp through faith is to be included in the love of God.

But when Christ said "shall be shed," it signified until the world's end: for his blood is always shed before his father as a satisfaction for the stubbornness and sin of man.

Christ can be everywhere.

But the remembrance of it is the power of action that he gave to his disciples, which consists in the Act that must be performed in the Church of God, yes, even until the end. For as God (*Jesus Christ*) is said to be a Savior and anointed, so is he an eternal King and a continual Savior of those who fly to him, containing in man (being dignified through his Godhead) the eternal power of presence and Being in all places wherever.

Consider (my brethren) what use the body of Christ would be if the Body itself were not a Sacrament and the holy sign of peace between God and man.

Behold, it is said: unless you eat of the flesh and drink of the blood, you cannot, etc.

If the disciples ate the body of Christ while Christ was ministering to them himself and standing nearby, not yet crucified, why then should you not eat the body of the same Christ who dwells in you, and in whom you have your dwelling?

But here the manner of eating is to be considered.

->E.K. Now he falls into ashes again.<-
->E.K. Now he is up again.<-

..... But from whom shall we learn this manner of eating? My brethren, from his disciples. For although Christ himself, alive, visibly and substantially stood beside them and ministered to them, he nonetheless took bread, broke it, and gave it to them, saying, "This is my body." They simply believed it, considering and acknowledging his Omnipotence (which Peter had established by saying, "You are the Son of the living God.")

If therefore he is acknowledged by us (I speak for you) to be the Son of the living God, then we must truly confess that all things are possible for him, and that by faith we ought to believe the mysteries, works, and wonders of God, sacramentally opened and to be used for the cure of our own sores.

And not as the wicked usually do: tie the power and majesty of God and his Omnipotence to the tail or end of reason, to be pulled wherever she wills.

If his Apostles have left us examples of belief, have taught us how to believe, and upon what rock and foundation to fasten our belief, then simply and plainly follow the steps of true Faith, and laying reason aside, believe.

But note here that this Sacrament is to be administered among the Apostles—among the ministers and true servants of God in his church—and not in the temple of the Scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, and deceivers; who, while they tear Jesus Christ and his body according to the perversity of their own sense, eat (as *Judas* did) and so perish eternally.

But I say to you and teach you: that wherever in the true Church of God remembrance is made and the use of this Sacrament is celebrated—the true body and blood of Jesus Christ crucified—there is also the true body of Christ, God and man, substantial bread of eternal comfort and food for those who humbly, plainly, and penitently receive it; propitiatory for the living and the dead; not for those who are dead in sin and in hell and out of this life, but for those who are sinners here, and thus dead, and are to be revived. For he who dwells in Christ is alive, because he dwells in life and light. But he who goes out of Christ through sin, and in whom Christ does not dwell, he is dead. This I have said.

Δ Lord, what shall we say to the priests when they want us to acknowledge Transubstantiation, etc.?

Under the form of bread.

->+ Prague.<-

1585. January 29. Tuesday. Morning at 10:15.

Prayers being finished, after the reading of yesterday's action, he appeared with a veiled face, as before.

...... *I demonstrated to you yesterday how the visible sign or matter appearing was united and knit to the invisible thing signified: wherein and whereunto I answered in my own form and person; for whoever talks of God and Christ, expounding the Scriptures, ought to talk plainly, truly, and openly, so that what they speak may be understood. This is the office of a preacher. Even so, I, talking of God and illuminated for this office for the time, was bare, because I spoke not of myself. But the doctrine I taught you was true and is worthy to be engraved on golden tables and monumentally placed upon the altar, wherein man may see, as in a mirror, how God, through his Sacraments and holy institutions, sanctifies, regenerates, and purifies man unto himself.*

<margin>Holy Art. GEBOFAL. The first gate of the holy book. 48 Gates of Wisdom. Discourse with God, the highest gate of wisdom.</margin>
*Now to the intended work, which is called in the Holy Art Gebofal, which is not (as the philosophers have written) the first supernatural step, but it is the first supernatural step naturally limited to the 48 Gates of Wisdom, where your holy Book begins. The last is speaking with God, as Moses did, which is infinite: All the rest have proper limits in which they are contained.*

*But understand that this one work receives multiplication and dignification by ascension through all the rest that are limited according to their proper qualities.*

<margin>Multiplication. Dignification. What has been taught. What yet is lacking.</margin>
*Of this knowledge I have laid a sure foundation, have taught what it is, and the instrument with which and by which it exists: the manner of proceeding and its basis. So that nothing is lacking but the simple and easy unknotting of those things that are wrapped, not with its own bands, but with the obscurity and gloomy cloud of your own ignorance.*

*But if the cloud is in you, then by your own help and consent it must be removed.*

Δ By the favor and help of the Highest, we trust the cloud shall be removed.

...... *Take heed, therefore, that you do not lift yourselves up in your minds, presuming against reason (by which you are joined together) and the will of God, by which you are taught obedience.*

<margin>Pride: Self-love.</margin>
*For pride is hateful before God, and to be in love with yourselves is the greatest ignorance. Shall a dark cellar brag or boast of her beauty because she receives light and clarity by a candle brought into or shining into her?*

*No more can you, [E. K.], for the ripeness of your wit and understanding is through our presence and our illumination.*

*But if we depart, you shall become a dark cellar and shall think too well of yourself in vain.*

*Matter is lacking among you; the fire cannot continue; but when you bring more wood, you shall have more fire. I will not visit you again until the seventh day.*

Δ To our Almighty God, eternal, true, and living, be all praise, honor, glory, and thanksgiving, now and forever. Amen.

# A true relation of Dr. Dee his Actions, with spirits, &c.

ways forsaken themselves; yet, for their own sake, they followed his commandments; therefore I say forsake yourselves, and do the will of God, so that for your own comfort and your eternal salvation, you may seek God.

<margin>Patience, afflictions, temptations, the World.</margin>
But he who seeks God, seeks him through patience, through afflictions, through temptations. Therefore despise this monster that tempts you, and ignore her in the midst of her pride, for she is poor, miserable, and prepared as a firebrand for destruction; if you seek riches from her, she has none; if you seek wisdom from her, she does not know it; if you desire quietness and the joys of rest, she cries out against you, "Watch, watch, and gird yourselves up."

And if you seek eternal life, or study to please God and to glorify him, for which purpose you were created, separate yourselves from the harlot.

<margin>We must be strangers to the world and worldly things.</margin>
Declare yourselves her enemy, and hate all those who take her side; for, behold, she has become an enemy of him who created you, a blasphemer of him whom you seek to glorify, the daughter of him who set himself against the Highest.

Therefore, for the sake of your creation, you ought to despise her.

For the sake of your redemption, you ought to ignore her, and for the glory that you seek to attain, you ought to utterly despise or scorn her.

But here, perhaps, you will say to me, as he said to *Christ* the Son of the living God.

*E. K. He bows and kisses the ground.*

What shall I do to inherit everlasting life?

I say to you, follow the commandments.

<margin>Love.</margin>
Behold, it is written, "I give you a new commandment: Love one another."

How can you love one another without charity?

But what is charity? Is it not the gift of the *Holy Ghost*? You know it is so; you also know that the *Holy Ghost* is called a Comforter.

But consider within yourselves why he is called a Comforter: not because he comforts himself, for he is all comfort, but because he is the comfort of those he has spoken to, saying, "I have given you a new commandment: Love one another." But who are they? They are those who eat the flesh and drink the blood of the Son of Man, *Jesus Christ*, the Son of God—true God and man. Unless you do this, you are not part of that company to whom *Christ* said, "I give you a new commandment."

For by doing so you are grafted into *Christ*, are subject to the commandment, and tied to charity, in which you are refreshed by the *Holy Ghost*, the continual comforter and giver of wisdom to those who dwell in *Christ*.

See, therefore, that no one belongs to *Christ* who does not have charity; nor does anyone have charity who is not among the company of those who feed on the flesh and blood of *Jesus Christ*, without which there is no salvation. Therefore, you, *E. K.*, are a liar when you say, "I fear God, I love God, I intend to live well and in obedience," for you do not follow his commandments; you fly from him; therefore, you are not with him.

<margin>* Δ E. K. confessed that he thought so at this moment. Penance. The Church. One must take refuge in the Catholic Church.</margin>
But I hear you saying, "I confess myself to *Christ* before the throne of God."

But you have not offered yourself to the priest, nor have you laid down your sacrifice.

I say to you, you do not confess yourself or your sins before God, because you do not go where he is.

It is not that God does not see you, but it is said that he does not hear sinners unless they are penitent. However, penance is defined by the Church, and sorrow is not to be judged by yourself; it is necessary for you, therefore, if you wish to fly to *Christ*, to enter into the company of those who profess him, where he is and with whom he dwells.

There, at the time you repent of your sins and confess them with sorrow before him who holds office in the mystery, there also through the mystery (which is *Christ*) shall you receive forgiveness for your sins.

For if he who ministers is heard in the power of his administration and sacramental vow, he has much more power to forgive sins; for behold, what he does is not of himself, but his dignity comes from that which makes him a priest.

Now, therefore, I say to you, *E. K.*: until you make yourself clean, you shall continue to be filthy; and to the unclean and impure, God does not reveal his mysteries.

But just as you, being unclean, see and yet see nothing, so once you are cleansed, though not seeing, you shall see—and see all things.

I have finished.

... Against divine necessity there is no prayer nor resistance.

Mandata tua justa sunt Domine. <note>Latin: "Your commands are just, O Lord."</note>

*What, was this the reason that God visited you: so that you should fulfill his commandments and teach his people the way of salvation?*

*Behold, the commandments of God are just and true, whose sons you are; if, therefore, you do not follow the commandments of your Father, you are disobedient. But as to why your Father has commanded you: Lo, I teach you.*
*When God of very God—the true light, beauty, and honor of his Father—contained or was full of the image of a heaven and earth, and by the omnipotent, conjoined, and equal power and strength of them both, joined in one, was brought forth and had his real beginning, he also determined, in the self-same Image and Idea, the due and proper order, just law, and determination of all things that were comprehended; which law and things together have their co-essential course both in heaven and earth, distinguishing all things into their real beginnings, limitation of time, and determination between their extremes. This order or law, begun in the bosom of the Word of God, keeps its proper course, and order, and law of its own establishment, so that those things that were previously wrought in God might also receive work and substantial being until the end of God's progression.*
*This is the same thing that we spoke of before, by the name of divine Necessity, against which no prayer prevails, nor can any resistance be made.*
*This Necessity was the reason, O you Prophets and children of God, that God dwelt among you.*
*This Necessity was the instrument that brought you to the stage of your election.*
*This Necessity was the reason that God chose you.*
*This Necessity makes honey from wax; milk from tar; return from long wandering; Christians from infidels; holy ones from the disobedient.*
*Finally, out of the imperfect and evil, the rage and roaming astray of mankind, it creates the true number of those who return from wickedness and are chosen for eternal joy from the beginning.*
*But this may seem to you a strange and stumbling doctrine.*
*I have laid the foundation.*
$\triangle$ We read the premises, which seemed to us very pithy, and weighty, and full of mysteries.

*****
> *This Necessity is twofold: one (that is to say, the first) contemplative and fixed.*
> *The other, working and leading to an end.*
> *In the first dwell two great and mighty Judges, Justice and Mercy.*
> *In the second dwells the son and image of Justice, leading on by order for the course of things; for those that are led on by the latter do not have true Justice, but the image of Justice.*
> *This is the cause why the elect and chosen may err and go astray, and lose the benefit both of the end of their Election and first determination.*
> *For: All things come on, and keep their course, even as they are led, by the image of Justice, man only excepted: who by reason of his free will, draws* <margin>[E. K. He teaches himself.]</margin> *out of order, runs from the mark, refuses that which is good, and through the burden of his flesh, inclines toward evil.*
> *In which evil, while he dwells and continues, lo, the course of necessity takes hold of him, and draws him to the scope or end toward which he inclines himself.*
> <margin>If he continues.</margin>
> *For, behold, although he was previously sanctified to the Lord and made a chosen vessel—in which if he continues, necessarily he shall enjoy the reward and glory of the sanctified—yet if he loses that Necessity and flies from his own law and condition, taking part with the filthiness and iniquity of his enemy, through Satan or his flesh, of Necessity he must perish.*
> <margin>If</margin>
> *For as those that are good, tied to the law of goodness, are glorified if they continue; so likewise are the evil tied to the law of wickedness, the Necessity of which is damnable.*
> *This is the cause why the Prophets are visited.*
> *Because God found them punishing their flesh, despising the vanities of the world, and resisting Satan.*

But is there a mercy fixed, and does this mercy also fix Justice; or as I have called it, the Image of Justice?

It is evident; so also is there a Justice that is fixed, a Justice triumphing, a Justice mighty, a Justice unable to be resisted, a Justice that prayer does not prevail against, yes, a Justice in which Hell and the Devil are condemned.

This is that Justice, this is that two-edged sword, this is that Iron Maul, with which those who refuse their Election, or are not elected, following the necessity of wickedness, are and shall be cut in pieces, beaten into small powder, and be cast into the lake of fire and brimstone.

This is he who seals up the second Hell, with the second death.

This is what you—O you starvelings, you vagabonds, you stiff-necked and stinking sinners—ought to dread and fear!

Has God elected you, and do you disdain it?

Has he provided a seat for you, an honor for you, a crown for you, a wedding garment for you, his eternal glory for you? And will you force him to cast it into the fire?

Shall the finger of God write you down, and shall the vengeance of God root you out?

Repent, I say, and flee from your iniquity.

Return to the way of the Lord, lest God, seeing your wickedness, your unnatural and inhuman rebellion, your disobedience against your father, thrust himself upon your necessity with his justice and vengeance.

If you do this, prayer does not prevail, much less is there resistance.

Are you not afraid to lose the sight of God, and to be deprived of the glory of his Majesty?

Are you not afraid of the unspeakable flames and firebrands of Hell, which are prepared for the wicked?

What shall I say to you?

Shall I take pity on you?

Why do you not care for yourselves?

Shall I pray to God for you?

You do not pray for yourselves.

Shall I bestow goodness upon you?

Hah, you despise it.

<margin>Three sheep.</margin>
Shall I bring three sheep from the mountains, and shall I lose two of them before I come home?

O you mortal men, be merciful to yourselves, take pity on yourselves. Fall into the true judgment of light and darkness, of good and evil, of eternal glory and damnation.

For, behold, I tell you, that God is ready to thrust himself, yes, to throw himself like a mighty stone upon you.

Against which there is no time of prayer, nor anything that can prevail.

I have here taught you, and exhorted you.

Exhorted you to forsake your wickedness, and to cling to the Lord.

Taught you that those who are elected may lose their election, and may be established in their election. Also that those who are not elected run by the rule of necessity to the end of their wickedness, which is rewarded with eternal fire.

From which God in his mercy, and through his Son Jesus Christ—who has redeemed you—is yet ready, if you will, to deliver you.

# Of the Confirmed PRAGUE Mysteries

->P R A G U E,<-

# Of the CRACOVIAN Stephanic Mysteries,

## Beginning April 12, 1585.

### Stephanic Mysteries.

Take common Audcal <note>an angelic or alchemical term</note>, purge and work it by Rlodnr <note>an angelic or alchemical term</note> of four different digestions, continuing the last digestion for fourteen days, in one and a swift proportion, until it becomes Dlaſod <note>an angelic or alchemical term</note> fixed, a most red and luminous body, the Image of Resurrection.

Take also Lulo <note>an angelic or alchemical term</note> of red Roxtan <note>an angelic or alchemical term</note>, and work it through the four fiery degrees, until you have its Audcal, and there gather it.

Then double every degree of your Rlodnr, and by the law of Coition <note>union or joining</note> and mixture, work and continue them diligently together. Nevertheless, work backward through every degree, multiplying the lower and last Rlodnr—once its due office is finished—by one degree more than the highest.

Thus does it become Darr <note>an angelic or alchemical term</note>, the thing you seek: a holy, most glorious, red, and dignified Dlaſod.

But watch well, and gather it thus, at the highest point: for in one hour, it descends or ascends from the purpose.

->Take hold.<-

**E. K.** came to me and asked me for the *Circle* or the *copy* of it which was shown to him at *Oxford*, and which he had written out or described by the light shown to him by the spirit. I, being occupied with writing a letter to the Queen's Majesty, said that as soon as I had leisure I would give it to him. He said he would wait for my leisure. I told him that would hardly be within this week, as I had so many letters to write. He thereupon flew into such a rage that he said I should not move one foot past him before I delivered it to him. But two things are to be considered here: whether the temptation be greater than the resistance, or the resistance more dignified than the rigor of temptation.

<margin>Parable about the two of us.</margin>
Michael ...... A wood grew up and the trees were young, and lo, there arose a great tempest from the North, and the seas threw out the air that had subtly stolen itself into them, and the winds were great; and behold, there was one tree which was older than the rest, and had grown longer than that which shot up by him. This tree could not be moved by the wind, but the tree that was young was moved to and fro with the wind, and struck himself oftentimes against the stiff-set tree. The forester came and beheld, and said within himself, "The force of this wind is great; see how this young tree beats itself to pieces against the greater. I will go home and bring my digging tools, and I will uproot him and place him further off. Then if the winds come, he shall have room to move." But when he came home, the Lord of the wood, seeing him in readiness with his mattock and his spade, asked him about his errand, and he told the matter in order to his Master. But lo, his Master rebuked him, and he said thus: "When the winds are not blowing, they grow together; they are not hurtful to one another. Suffer them, therefore. When the young tree takes root and reaches some years, his roots shall link themselves with and under the roots of the greater; then, though the winds come, they shall not be hurtful to one another, but shall stand so much the more fast, by how much the more they are wrapped together. Yea, when the old tree withers, he shall be a strength to him, and shall add to his age as much as he has added to his youth." And he ceased to dig.

Do not, therefore, be pulled asunder, nor be offended at one another; perhaps Reason would set you aside, but God will not. Behold, if you break the yoke that you are in and run astray, he who errs shall perish, and even so shall he who stands also be desolate. For why? The angry driver does not continue with only one, but he shall return home and shall not see the end of the harvest.

-> + In Prague. <-

**April 5.**
Friday, I took my journey from *Prague* toward *Krakow*; may God give us good speed. *E. K., Thomas Kelly*, and *Hugh Brycket* were my servants.

---

-> Friday. + Krakow, 1585. <-

**April 12.** In the afternoon we came to *Krakow*, and as we were within an *English* mile of the city, on a fair and calm day, several whirlwinds passed about half a mile ahead of us, crossing from the right hand to the left, one after another, swirling up the dust with great intensity high into the air, and continuing to move forward, and then mounting into the sky, and so went southerly from us. Likewise, some began on the right hand and came furiously, raising and swirling the dust up into the air southerly also, but did not cross the path.

When we came to our house, we found that a stranger had been placed into it by the landlords (*Mr. John Long*, the judge, and *Martin Plutner*). Having with me the keys of the storehouse and of the street door, I caused my belongings brought with me to be moved in, and that night we managed with great difficulty to find lodging. But the new and intruding tenants gave me leave to have one of my bedsteads, which was in one heated room <note>stove: a room heated by a stove, common in Central Europe</note>, and cleared the same for us with much difficulty.

*Saturday* and *Sunday* we were heavily confronted, or rather threatened, that we should have no house there; also, a man named *Bonar's* coat of arms was set upon the door, as if the house had been granted to him officially <term>ex officio</term>. *Monday* I made the Rector aware of the injustices I endured, and he courteously sent two Masters of Arts with me to the Proconsul to obtain a summons for the landlords to appear on Tuesday by 7 o'clock to answer our complaint.

This *Monday* night, the Lord *Lasky* came from *Lasko*, following a letter he had received from me from *Nisso* concerning my arrival.

Tuesday (*April 16*), the Lord *Lasky* came to the house, and in the morning he would have immediately thrown all their belongings out of doors, but by my entreaty he permitted them to empty everything into the lower heated room <note>stove</note>.

In the meantime, I appeared with my lawyer or attorney, **Mr. Tetaldo** (an *Italian*), a long-time practitioner in *Polish* and *Krakovian* cases. To conclude, I received a decree against my landlords stating that I was to have at least a half-year's notice; whereupon *John Laugh* gave me notice to vacate at *Michaelmas*, and so we left the Court or Town Hall, called *Praetorium* in *Latin*. This same *Tuesday* afternoon, my Lord *Lasky* went to the King of *Poland* at the Castle and told him of my arrival and how poorly I was treated; and the King said, "Why did he not throw them out of doors?" "I have done so now," said the Lord *Lasky*; and the King granted that the house be held officially <term>ex officio</term>. The next day, the King was desirous to speak with me.

**April 17, Wednesday**, I went with the Lord *Lasky* to the King, to whom I said:
> "Comfort, peace, and the mercy of God be with you, O most serene King. Before whom, having been divinely admonished to present myself, I now most humbly do so; most ready with all faithfulness and sincerity to handle those things with your Royal Majesty which are divinely commanded of me. I shall not refuse to relate the histories of these mysteries in order, as occasion is given, and to perform all other things which I understand to be pleasing to God and your Royal Majesty, etc."

The King answered:
> "As I have heard many good things about your person in your absence, so now your arrival is very pleasing to me; and if there is anything in which my grace and favor may be of help to you, I will not fail to show myself as your supporter and protector. And concerning these and other greater matters, there will be a more convenient time to speak after these feast days, at which time I will arrange to have you summoned to me, etc."

Upon this, I made a bow, as was appropriate, and stepped back somewhat from the King. Then the Vice-Chancellor and other officers, and the chief secretary, brought documents to be read and signed or authorized by the King's own hand, which he did. After the Lord *Lasky* had watched for a fit time to tell the King of his desire to speak a few words to His Majesty about some of his own affairs, and was told to return immediately after dinner to His Majesty, we took our leave with a respectful bow and went out of the private chamber—or rather the withdrawing room—through his private chamber, where he had said Mass when we arrived, and so into the Guard-chamber, and downstairs, etc.

*Friday*, I took spiritual counsel from **Doctor Hannibal**, the great theologian, who had recently published some of his commentaries upon the *Pymander* of *Hermes Trismegistus*.

*Saturday (April 20)* I received Communion at the *Pernardines* <note>Likely the Bernardines</note>, where that Doctor is a professor.

This day *E. K.* received spiritual counsel and comfort, as his case required.

L.*'s last letters, explaining how he was in a monastery of his own, belonging to the Castle *Rithwyan* (which he had now by a stratagem won from the unjust delaying of his adversary), and what penance and contrition he was in, what meditations, and what godly purposes, etc. But **E. K.** would not hope for his conversion, and thereupon utterly and resolutely intended with all speed to be gone from here toward *Prague*, and desired me (if I would) to prepare my letters. He became very blasphemous against God to my great grief and terror: the blasphemy and rebellion against God and his holy purposes in us were so great that almost nothing greater could be uttered. I used as quiet words as I could, assuring him of God's mercies which are always ready, and his helping hand for all such as put their trust in him and call upon him in their troubles and times of need; and so I committed him to God for that Tuesday night, it being past 9 o'clock.

*Wednesday* morning, as I was at my prayers in my study over his chamber, and had made a declaration of this cause and of the most grievous perplexity I was in to see my friend and partner (**E. K.**) thus carried away with such a grievous, manifold, and vehement temptation.

**E. K.**, still lying in his bed, called his brother *Thomas* to him and desired him to call me. *Thomas* came for me (when I had nearly ended my devotions and prayers). # + Niepołomice, in the Court of the King of Poland.
## Year 1585.
### May 23. In the afternoon, at about 6 o'clock.

The King sent for Lord Laski and me by his Vice-Chamberlain. We came to him in a chamber within the chamber or room where he usually gives audience, or eats with his Palatines and others. He sat by the window which faces south, and through which he has a view of his new garden, which is being made. He began thus (Lord Albert Laski being present, as requested by the King) and said to me very nearly what these words import:

**St.** The Lord Palatine [Laski] has urged me to hear you speak of these great and rare things, which I have done willingly. However, it should be considered that all prophets and revelations ceased long ago, in the time of Christ. Nevertheless, if there is nothing in these things against the honor of God, they are all the more worth hearing. And I indeed do not doubt that God can now reveal certain secrets to men in many ways, even in these times, by unusual commands.

### Hereupon I answered to this sense, although I cannot express the same words.

<margin>$\triangle$</margin>
I consider three main points in your royal order, which contain the very marrow of your whole order. First, concerning the cessation of prophecies and revelations. Second, whether anything in our actions or exercises is contrary to the honor of God. And third (which is very pleasing to my mind), that you do not prescribe to God certain modes or times in which he wishes or ought to reveal his secrets to men. Regarding the first, we can assert to your Royal Majesty that the passage of Scripture is not rightly understood by many, and is worst understood by those who wish to prescribe certain modes and certain times to the all-encompassing power, mercy, and wisdom of God. They assert that there is no prophecy in these times, or that there would be none after Christ, because all ceased in Christ. That is to say, all the prophecies that were about Him—namely, concerning the Son of God coming in the flesh, the true Messiah, and the future redeemer of the human race (and all that history of Christ which we Christians acknowledge and confess to be completed and finished)—have now ceased. To the extent that those things are neither still to come, as the Jews believe, nor are they to be repeated, since they are already finished and performed just as the Prophets foretold. For this reason, when Jesus Christ, hanging on the cross, knew that all the prophecies about him had been completed—and we understand that the aim of all prophecies (before Christ) was now achieved, and according to the presence and purpose of God the Redeemer, the mystery was fulfilled in human consciousness—he himself said, <margin>* John 19:30, Acts 13</margin> "It is finished." For Paul also said to the Jews that when they had fulfilled all that was written of him, taking him down from the tree, they laid him in a tomb. And after his Resurrection, Christ himself said to his disciples <margin>Luke 24</margin> (who were traveling toward the village of Emmaus, and were arguing and doubting about his death and resurrection), "O fools and slow of heart to believe all that the prophets have spoken! Was it not necessary for Christ to suffer these things and so enter into his glory?" And beginning from Moses and all the prophets, he interpreted to them in all the scriptures the things concerning himself, etc. and a little later again to the same men: "For it was necessary that all things should be fulfilled which were written in the law of Moses, and the Prophets, and the Psalms concerning me."

But as for the other sense—that after Christ there would be a thousand prophets or revelations—the Scriptures themselves most clearly teach the contrary. For what shall be said of Revelation, without that notable Apocalypse of the Blessed John which occurred after Christ? Which is also called "Prophecy" by the same John, when he says, <margin>* Rev. Ch. 1</margin> "*Blessed is he who reads and hears the words of this prophecy and keeps those things which are written in it*," and in the last chapter of the same Apocalypse or revelations, he calls it the book of prophecy three times. Therefore, it is manifest that there are revelations and prophets after Christ. Furthermore, what was 그 revelation made to Paul at his calling and conversion by Jesus Christ himself, as appears in the book of the Acts of the Apostles, Chapter 9? What about the one given <margin>* Acts 10</margin> to Cornelius the Centurion?

<margin>Acts 11</margin>
What about the one given to Peter concerning clean and unclean animals? And Paul himself says, <margin>$\triangle$ 2 Cor. Ch. 12</margin> $\triangle$ "If I must boast (though it is not profitable), I will come to visions and revelations of the Lord," etc. And a little later: "And lest I be exalted by the greatness of the revelations, there was given to me a thorn in my flesh, a messenger of Satan to buffet me... the mystery was made known to me, as I wrote above, as you can understand by reading my wisdom in the mystery of Christ, which was not made known to the sons of men in other generations, as it has now been revealed to his holy Apostles and Prophets in the spirit," etc., where it also appears that there are Prophets after Christ. And in Chapter 4: "And he gave some as Apostles, some as Prophets, others as Evangelists, others as Pastors and Teachers, for the perfecting of the saints, for the work of the ministry, for the building up of the Body of Christ, until we all come into the unity of faith, to the measure of the age of the fullness of Christ," etc. Here it appears that there will be Prophets in the Church of Christ for as long after Christ as it takes for us all to meet in the unity of faith, etc. Since we know this has not yet happened after Christ, and now in our own age we are especially discordant regarding the business of faith, not only Prophets but also very express revelations concerning Divine Mysteries seem most necessary. And concerning the angelic speech <margin>* Acts ch. 8. Philip carried from place to place by the Spirit of God.</margin> * to Philip, and his invisible translation, as it were, from place to place by the Spirit of God.

<header>A true Relation of Dr. Dee his Actions with Spirits, &c.</header>

...the Spirit of the Lord, which must be believed. And concerning the Prophets after the times of Christ, the eleventh chapter of *Acts* testifies, where we read that at the same time when the disciples of Christ were first named Christians at *Antioch*, Prophets came from *Jerusalem* to *Antioch*. And one of them, named *Agabus*, rising up, signified through the spirit that there would be a great famine over the whole world, which happened under *Claudius*. To the second point of your Royal Majesty’s chapter, I respond thus: before God and his blessed Angels, I assert that my conscience has discovered nothing yet, nor known, nor been able to judge—nor can it in all our actions or any one of them—that is against the honor or glory of God. On the contrary, we can say that they greatly pertain to the honor and glory of God.

Finally, in the third place, I am greatly glad that you exist with such great, truly pious, and Royal discretion: that Almighty God in these times can manifest his mysteries and secrets to certain men in his various ways. And all the more so, because this has been able to consist of many of our past Actions, as well as future ones, at which your Royal Majesty may be present and attend (if it should so please Him). I am prepared to show 24 books of our past Actions (at whatever time it pleases your most serene Majesty) to be seen; some of which are written in the *Latin* tongue, others in *Greek*, others in the *English* tongue, but for the most part they are written in *English*. These are the actions of the Angels themselves—namely, the instructions, warnings, exhortations, sermons, and prophecies of God's good spirits, and by whatever other name the revelations made to us, real or verbal, are to be judged—which have been received and recorded by us for the space of nearly three years now, etc.

We, as your servants here, meeting in your Name and with one mind, may you deign, by your Fatherly mercy, to purge us of all the filth of my whole life: and by the interceding merits of the Name of your most dear Son, our Lord and Redeemer Jesus Christ, forgive us whatever we, all and each, have offended against your holy and just laws—whether willingly, unknowingly, or negligently—in word, deed, or thought until this hour; so that we may now be offered to you as a pure and unleavened mass, to be fermented by one Divine and most abundant grace; and by the fire of your charity kindled in our hearts by you, we may be made as the loaves of proportion and sacrifice in your Temple. And let your Son, our Lord Jesus Christ, be meanwhile the Bread of Life to us: whom, by tasting most sweet and swallowing most lively by the strength of faith, may we have the same Manna with us forever. Send forth now, therefore, your Light and Truth, O Almighty, eternal, Living, and True God, and let it appear to your Stephen (our most Serene and most gracious King), that You, our true and living God, are our Almighty Teacher in these actions and Mysteries: and that I (though subject to sins) have previously been preserved as your faithful and sincere servant by great vow and effort: that all your commands are of the greatest care to me: and that we, each and every one, were foreordained with specific gifts for you before the beginning of the world, to be employed in your Holy service, etc.

<meta>This page continues the "Puccian Action," specifically a discourse delivered by a spirit (likely Uriel) rebuking those who interpret the Scriptures through their own imagination rather than through the established tradition of the visible Church.</meta>

with acceptable truths, as the chosen servants and ministers of the Highest.

<margin>Malice, Worldly Pomp, and Vanity.</margin>
*The whole world lies in wickedness*, and has become the open shop of Satan, to deceive the merchants of the earth with all abomination. But what, are you the peddlers of such wares? Or the carriers abroad of lies and false doctrine? Do you think it is a small matter to tie the sense of God’s Scriptures and mysteries to the sense and snatching of your imaginations? Do you count it as nothing to sit in judgment against the Spirit of God, leaving him no place except within your limitations? Is it lawful before the Son of God to spend whole days—yes, many years—with the sons of Satan, the lying imps and deceivers of the world? Are you so far entered into the shop of abomination that you point out to the Son of God the time of his coming, the descending of his prophets, and the time in which he shall visit the earth? Moses dared not speak except from the Lord’s mouth; the prophets did not expound the Law, but the voice of the Lord. The Son of God did not speak his own words, in that he was flesh, but the words of his Father; his disciples did not teach except through the Holy Ghost. Dare you (therefore) presume to teach and open the secret chamber of the Highest, not being called?

Tell me, have you left your merchandise and the counting of your money deceitfully gotten, to become teachers of the word of God? Are you not ashamed to teach before you understand? Yes, are you not ashamed to lead away where you cannot bring home? You are hypocrites and void of the Holy Ghost; you have become liars and the enemies of Christ and his holy Spirit.

Perhaps you will say, "In reading the Scriptures we understand." But tell me, by what spirit do you understand them? What angel has appeared to you? Or by which of the heavens have you been instructed?

It may be you will say "by the Holy Ghost." O you fool, and of little understanding! Do you not understand that the Holy Ghost is the schoolmaster of the Church, of the whole flock and congregation of Christ? If he is the schoolmaster (therefore) over a multitude, it follows then that one doctrine taught by the Holy Ghost is a lesson or an understanding for a multitude. But what multitude is of your understanding, or of what congregation are you? Will you say you are scattered? You speak falsely; you are a renegade. But behold, I teach you, and your error is before your face.

Whoever understands the Scriptures must seek to understand them by ordinance and spiritual tradition. But by what spiritual tradition do you understand? Or by what ordinance are the Scriptures opened to you? You will say you are informed by the Holy Fathers, and that you understand by the same spirit by which they taught. You say so, but you do not do so. Which of your forefathers has tied reason to the word of God, or the understanding of the Scriptures to the discipline of the heathen? I say to you that your forefathers were dear to Christ and were partakers of heavenly visions and celestial comforts; these visions and celestial comforts did not teach them a new exposition of the Scriptures, but did confirm and give light to the mysteries of the Holy Ghost spoken by the Apostles, the founders and builders of the Church. Whatever, therefore, you learn from your forefathers, you learn from the Apostles, and whatever you learn from the Apostles you have by the Holy Ghost. But if you expound the Fathers according to your own sense, and not after the sense of the Apostles, you do not have the Holy Ghost, but the spirit of lying.
<margin>Reason. The visible Church.</margin>
Therefore humble yourself and fall down before the Lord. Lay reason aside and cling to him. Seek to understand his word according to his holy Spirit. Which holy Spirit you must certainly find, and shall find, in a visible Church, *even unto the end.*

I will plainly say to you (so that truth may appear mightily in light): Whoever is contrary to the will of God—which is delivered to his Church, taught by his Apostles, nourished by the Holy Ghost, delivered to the world, and brought to Rome by Peter, and taught there by him and his successors, held, and maintained—is contrary to God and to his truth.
<margin>Luther. Calvin. Wilfully, obstinately erring. The definition of a heretic.</margin>

*Luther has his reward.*
*Calvin has his reward.*

The rest, all who have erred and willfully run astray, separating themselves from the Church and congregation of Christ obstinately and through the instigation of their father the Devil, have their reward. Against whom the Son of God shall pronounce judgment, saying,

*Go, you deceivers, into hellfire, prepared for your Father and his children from the beginning.*

<margin>The Pope is not Antichrist. Antichrist.</margin>
*You rise up among yourselves, saying, "The Pope is Antichrist"; for by this name you call him. An evil man he may be, and he may fall from his vocation, but he can never be Antichrist. For Antichrist is he: the son of the Devil, a man, flesh and blood, born of a wicked and deceitful harlot, who shall seduce the people, swell with the strength of his father, and resist God on earth among men, as his father did in heaven among the angels, utterly denying his omnipotence and setting himself against him.*

<margin>The Keys of Heaven given to the Apostles.</margin>
*O you fools, and of little understanding: When the keys of heaven were given to the Apostles—that is to say, the same authority and power of Jesus Christ, the Son of the living God, to forgive sins and to exclude sinners from the kingdom of heaven—and when it was also said to those same Apostles, "Get behind me, Satan," you do not have the understanding to see into the mysteries of the Highest. If the Son of God did commend and reprimand his disciples, why may a bishop not, therefore, be counted as both good and evil? If it follows, therefore, that a bishop may be both good and evil, it follows also that neither good nor evil adds to the authority of a bishop, but only to his own life. If he is good, he reaps the benefit of his goodness, but if he is evil, he is a liar because his doctrine is against himself. If, therefore, because of the sin of man, God has allowed many in the spirit of * Ananias to sit in the holy place, it is for the sake of your sins and your rebellious nature that you are punished, and not for the obscuring or darkening of his Church.*

<margin>Remember to ask for an amendment of this place; perhaps "belongs." * Acts 23:A.</margin>
<margin>No one can assume authority for himself.</margin>
*Open your eyes, therefore, and understand; and cleave to the Church for the sake of the Church, and not for the love of man. Do not despise the Church because of the transgressions of man, but submit your neck under that holy yoke and ordinance which shall lead you to the congregation governed by the Spirit of God. In it, you shall understand the secrets of God's Book, to be interpreted according to the sense of your fathers, whose understanding was the finger of the Holy Ghost. You cannot authorize yourselves, and without authority, you can do nothing. Therefore, if your authority is nothing, why do you take upon yourselves the work of the Church? For it is one thing to seek to understand the Scriptures, and another thing to teach the Scriptures according to one's own understanding; for he who teaches, teaches by authority, but if he has no authority, he is an usurper.*

<margin>An usurper.</margin>
<margin>The Church, our Mother: and yet a Virgin. Simplicity. Obedience. Curiosity is of the Devil. Matthew 7:15. Children, Dogs. Dogs.</margin>
*My brethren, remember yourselves and consider that you are children: you are not your own masters [vestri juris], but belong to another [alieni]. Therefore, do nothing that is of yourselves, but follow (as good children) the steps of your Mother—which Mother is a pure Virgin and is always instructed with the wisdom of the Comforter. She knows what meat she shall give to you, her children, and how she shall bring you up and instruct you. Simplicity is worth much, and obedience is a garland before the Lord. But curiosity is of the Devil. Have you not read that the bread of the holy ones is not to be cast to dogs? Look to yourselves, whether you are dogs or not. See if your life is holy, your doings straight and just, your patience manifold, and your affliction great for the Lord. If you do not find yourselves to be so, you are not children. If you are not children, you are not sons; if you are not sons, you have no mother; if you have no mother, you are dogs. You are devourers of the bread of children, currish, senseless, and against God.*

<margin>Let us descend into judgment of our own state. Father, Son, Holy Spirit, Church. The bread of life is understanding.</margin>
*Enter, therefore, into judgment with yourselves.*
*Consider that you are created by God.*
*Consider that you are redeemed by God.*
*Consider also that you are left to the spiritual tuition and comfort of God, who has made of you a congregation: a holy and sanctified fellowship, feeding always as brethren together under his wings and at his table. He feeds you with the bread of life and understanding, with the body and blood of Jesus Christ, the Son of the living God.*

<margin>Obedience is the end of our vocation.</margin>
*He feeds you with understanding so that you may know the will of your Father who is in heaven, and knowing him, be obedient—which is the conclusion of your vocation. Do not shake off the yoke of obedience, lest you also put away the cup of understanding, and so do not know the will of your Father.*

*But it seems to me that you are starved; your guts are shrunk up; your bones and sinews are withered. What is the cause of this? When did you receive the bread of the Lord? When did you receive nourishment? O you of little faith and less understanding! You err and run astray; you are blind; you do not follow the will of your Father. Return, return, and say within yourselves,*
