Finally, setting these things aside, I asked for my book by *Postellus* again. He denied that he had it when asked where I had heard he did; and when I praised Dr. Dee, he again denied having seen it, unless, he said, "you mean some book without a title from the hands of *Lord Sevenbergius*." And finally, he gave no hope of returning it. I, not wishing to argue with him, left; and I encountered your boy *Stanislaus* in the courtyard. From him, I understood that you had come as far as *Erfurt* with *Lord Gregory* and *Lord Carpione*; that eight days ago *Lord Carpione* set out from there to *Bamberg* to collect some money or other; and that he had come here with *Lord Gregory*. I asked whether he carried a letter or any small word from you to me; he replied, nothing at all, "because perhaps they thought," he said, "that you were not here." He said he would return to you in three or four days. I praised his plan and his constancy in serving his Masters, and I showed him my house, so that he would not return to you without my letters. He promised he would not leave without greeting me. Meanwhile, *Lord Gregory* noticed me talking with him, and angry (as far as I can judge from his shouting voice), he called the boy back. I departed, thoughtful. On the fifteenth day of this month, finally finding your little servant *Stanislaus* in an open place, I questioned him more carefully about your affairs and status; and not without great pleasure of mind, I heard that larger houses have been granted to you. That the *Illustrious Lord Landgrave* bestows much upon and favors the most excellent Dr. Dee, and I give great thanks to the highest God for such a gift. I led the boy to my bedroom and showed him the letters prepared for you, so that he would not return to you without them. But a little later, the father of *Carpione* warned me that he wanted to send a single express messenger to you before night, and that I should write if I wished; for he had been advised by *Mr. Kelley* to signify this to me. I give immense thanks to *Mr. Kelley*, who has not entirely forgotten me, and I decided to signify these things through this messenger, whom I hope is faithful to you, intending to write again through *Stanislaus*, if it seems worthwhile.

I pray and beseech you by that living God, who is the Author of our friendship, and who clearly commanded that we love one another mutually, that you do not forget me when the occasion is given to visit me through letters or through messengers, and to keep me informed of the state of your affairs and ours; for I certainly will not forget you, and my services will testify to it, not only before God but also before all men. If your return is delayed for some time, I will visit you next month in *September*, for I can hardly live far from you—indeed, if I must speak properly, I am weary of life. And in person, I will deal with several matters which it is not at all proper to write.

Eighteen days have already passed since I have seen the *Most Illustrious Apostolic Nuncio*; and since I have more than sufficiently satisfied obedience, I will not go to him, lest he persuade himself that it will be so easy to deceive us. He showed the letters of Dr. Dee to the *Venetian* and *Florentine Ambassadors*, and both to me...

*He praised them highly and said they seemed eloquent, weighty, and of more than an ordinary spirit, and the best example of such things. Prague, September 17, 1585.*

-> + Trebon, *Second Action out of seven.* <-

Year 1586.
October 14, Tuesday. *Morning, after sunrise.*

<margin>Around 7:00.</margin> *After prayers were poured out and thanks given for the infinite mercies of God toward us, both in predestination and in execution, in our country, at sea, and in this pilgrimage; and for our liberation from the hands of enemies during our exile from Prague, and for his continuous protection, and for our restoration with honor and glory in him, to rest and security with William Rosenberg; we now weighed what he might especially wish to propose to us from his mysteries, and what should be decided about Pucci, what about $\odot$ <note>Gold or the Sun</note> and the philosophical works according to his purpose, and what should be decided about the error recently made in practice, and what else we should now and especially do. We are ready to call William according to God's pleasure, etc.*

$\Delta$ I had set up the *Table of the Covenant* [*Mensam foederis*], with its appurtenances, and had set the Angelical Stone in the frame of gold on the table, only E. K. and I being in the beautiful little chapel next to my chamber, appointed for our use.

> A voice ...... *Let him come, who is to come.*

$\Delta$ I went for Lord *Rosenberg*, whom I found in his oratory in the church hearing Mass; and he came with me and sat in his place.

E. K. I see a great plain like a field, <margin>Vision.</margin> as though it were a mile across. In the end of it there is a tall, rotten tree. All the grass is as though it were withered and burned. A beam, as if of fire, comes from heaven and strikes the tree. Now water comes out of the root of the tree, like a sea, and spreads over the whole plain. And the tree opens and a man comes out of it; his hair hangs down to his waist, his garment covers him from his shoulders and hangs behind him down into the water.

The earth has now drunk up all the water, and the man stands upon the dry ground.

The whole place is full of green grass about a cubit high.

Now the man is out of sight.

It seemed to be beyond and outside the Stone.

The vision has completely disappeared.

$\Delta$ I explained this vision in Latin to Lord *Rosenberg*.

E. K. In the middle of the Stone there seems to stand a little round thing like a spark of fire, and it increases, and seems to be as large as a globe of 20 inches in diameter, or thereabouts.

And behold, behold, behold (I say), you who are the kings and princes of the earth tied and knit together upon one stem, you are all rotten and barren; behold, you bring forth no fruit. But even as the grass that withers, he is a disgrace to the place; even so are you, who are the grass of your location and dwelling. For behold, you have no leaves, much less fruit. Woe, woe, woe to such a generation, which lacks moisture and the fire of comfort! The stem that carries you is the seat and holy place, which also is contaminated. <margin>E. K.</margin> A wood appears, a great wood on the left hand by a river. There are two things like hawks, one of which is white, and the other is black. The black one is on a branch in the water; the other is on a withered branch on the land.
<margin>The first bear.</margin> A great bear comes out of the wood. Now he runs toward them; he catches the black one in the water and swallows him, then stands up on his hind legs. Now he goes to the other and shakes him in his mouth, then stands up on his hind legs. He has pulled off both its wings; he returns into the wood again. The body of the white hawk lies on the ground. Now he turns his feet up. Now he stands on his legs again. He follows the bear the same way he went; he tries to lift himself up as if he would fly, but he cannot. All of this—the wood, the bear, and the two birds—have vanished.
<margin>E. K.</margin> Below stands a great castle at the foot of the hill on which that wood stood; down in a valley from the hill goes a great, long stone bridge, appearing to be about ten English miles long. Beside the entrance, on the right hand of that castle, is something like a dial, with celestial movements of the Sun and Moon within it.
<margin>The second bear.</margin> Now comes a bear (black like the other), a very great and monstrous bear. The bridge quakes under him as he passes it toward the castle. He roars, looking toward the castle. He steps up to the dial, takes the moon out of it, and tears it all to pieces with his teeth. The castle falls, and the bridge where he stands is broken. The castle is entirely in ruins. The bear stands upon the edge of the bridge and beholds the ruin of the castle, which has fallen down as if into a pit. Now he goes back, and the bridge falls down after him. Now the wood appears again, and he goes into the wood. Now that vision has all vanished away.
> A Voice ...... *You shall shortly see against what stone Pucci has stumbled. My peace and blessing be upon you.*
<margin>E. K.</margin> Now everything has gone away.

## MEMORANDUM.

In the year 1586, on the 17th of October, in the afternoon, after new disturbances and quarrels with Francisco Pucci regarding the money he desired to have from us—out of generosity, and in the name of God, and as if from the servants of God, and not from Edward Kelley as Edward Kelley—we [ $\Delta$ and E. K. ] decided (to avoid many scandals which he himself had spread and devised against us regarding his 800 Florins, which were offered to God and returned through him, and previously refused when we were ready to pay him; and we showed him 630 Ducats before God, so that he might take from them what he judged to be his own). We decided, I say (with the good hope that we would not offend God), to set out the sum of 800 Florins before him in the presence of witnesses; and if he asserted that it was owed to him, he could receive it if he wished. But if he denied the 800 Florins, or that any money was owed to him by us, then we wanted that also to be pronounced before witnesses, and made known by testimony and a signed document at appropriate times and places.

From the chest, we then went to the Primate’s house, and having called together several primary citizens, the senior priest, and several scribes of the illustrious Supreme Prince (Lord Rosenberg), we displayed two large bags of money. There, two thousand ducats and more than 400 dollars and 800 florins were counted on the table. A dilemma was proposed to him (which I noted above), and he was content to accept the money, but he wanted to sign that he had received it in the name of God, and from us as servants of God. However, we protested that we would in no way take it upon ourselves to say this was enjoined upon us by God, as if we were presenting those funds to him to be either accepted or refused by him. Rather, only to avoid many great scandals against us, we left it to his own free will there, so that he might say what seemed better to him and what would be <unclear>pleasing</unclear> to him. He therefore took the money, counted it, and a receipt was written by the hand of the Supreme Prince’s scribe (Paul Welsy), who was present with various witnesses who signed their names, as can be seen in the document itself.

# 1587. THIRD ACTION.
## General Action at Trebona.

<margin>April 4. Morning, around 8:00.</margin>
After prayers to God and the recitation of that catalog of our petitions to Him, we rested, waiting for divine counsel, warnings, and oracles.

**Voice.** ...... *Happy is he whose mind thirsts after the knowledge of such things as are spiritual and celestial, of such things as are in the everlasting place and glory of Him who is, and was, and shall be forever: for to him belongs rest in the harvest of the Highest, and comfort in the midst of many worldly sorrows. For to him, thus says the Lord, the Lord of Rest: You have returned my blood again with comfort to me, and have made a blood of eternal rest for yourself forever. Ascend, therefore, and dwell with me, and receive eternal comfort: for to such belongs the Kingdom of my Father; for I am* <margin>* Rest in all cessation, Sabbath, etc.</margin> \***Zebaoth** unto all such as trust in me. But behold, the earth does not bring forth my mighty praise because of the wickedness that abounds in all mankind: Neither do I have many such children among the sons of men as I have spoken of before; for why? The giants of this world are a stumbling block to the poor people and to their subjects: for lo, behold, behold! (I say) vile and base things (because they are misused) have become gods within their houses: so that gold and silver, precious stones, and soft clothing, which used to be brought out of their houses to adorn mine with, have become their gods and the idols of their destruction: for who is he that does not exalt himself in his riches and despise me, who was the author of them? Where is he who does not love his wife and children, pomp and worldly glory, more than the ordering of my little flock or the advancement of my glory? Who (I say) is he who does not make more of himself than of me? Woe be to you who do so: and woe be to the generations that shall follow you.*

$\Delta$. Be merciful to us, O God of Mercies.

...... O wretched and miserable mankind, look, look in and upon yourself. Have you made yourself? Or when you are afflicted, can you remove your own affliction? Do you have anything of your own which my Father has not given you through me, in one provident and eternal will? Can you hide yourself where I cannot see you? Or can you do that which lies hidden from me? Look again upon yourself and consider what parents and root you had your beginning in Nature: behold, they and their fathers have become the dust of the earth; even so shall you. And even as a strict account of life is required of them, even so shall it be of you: for I, who made you and gave you breath, made you a partaker and user of my creatures, led you in and out, gave you the sun to shine upon you, and the moon as the mother of your <term>radical moisture</term>. I, who lifted you up, either to the honor of a King or Magistrate, and made you a governor over your brothers, will at last take a strict account of you, how you have used yourself toward me, and where you have advanced my Name in such things as I have lent you: And be very sure that you shall pay even the uttermost farthing. Woe be to you if you do not make a just account; miserable shall you be forever if your deserts condemn you. Therefore while you have time and space, look, look up to me; for I am the Well of comfort and the God of peace; the true reward of righteousness to all those who faithfully love and trust me.

->Pause.<-

$\Delta$. I read this over ...... Oh, how comforting are these lessons! Give us and confirm to us your graces and blessings, O God, to do your blessed will in this and in all our duty toward you whatsoever.

William, the son of Ursine, the Lord talks with you this day, saying: Do you wish that I buy a kingdom for you with gold or silver? Do you wish that the kings and princes of the earth shall laugh the Almighty God of heaven and earth to scorn?

Have I at any time promoted (those who trust in me) to the government of my people by giving them the excrements of the earth?

Look down upon my servant Abraham.

Look down upon his children.

Recall to memory my servant David.

Set Solomon before your eyes.

The kings and princes of Judah and of Jerusalem.

Consider within yourself the calling of the twelve: the government and state of those who have been princes among the Christian flock.

Have they been hired or promoted? Have they been lifted up by me with gold or silver, or similar trumpery, the monsters of the earth? In necessity, to pay tribute, the fish served, by which means tribute might be paid according to custom.

In the calling of Abraham, the multiplication of his seed was promised, which was to be a multitude of people, mighty and great upon the face of the earth.

David was brought in (the least of his brothers) even to be King of Israel, not by a multitude of precious stones, gold, or silver. He had a sling and a satchel with a few stones.

Solomon was commanded to build me a temple, without any fixed sum or limit. The Apostles went from place to place, intending to teach; they carried neither gold nor silver, but only a scrip or bag prepared for their common food and nourishment.

Many princes and kings have published my name without any promise made to them from heaven.

Nevertheless, I gave plenty to Abraham as his necessities required, and to his children as I had limited.

To David, being King, riches followed his state; and to his son Solomon, plenty both at home and abroad to build my temple.

To the Apostles I gave (at the time of the calling of my people) the spirit of understanding, by which they understood and had power to teach. And to those who stretched out their hands for my name, I have given abundantly; and it has been faithfully taken in hand for the love of me.

Believe, therefore, with Abraham and with his children.

Bring your sling and bag before the people of the Lord against Goliath.

Strive, as Solomon did, to build a commonwealth in which I will be exalted, as the servant of the Son of God and as his follower.

Go forward, as your own power and ability shall serve you; for thus says the Lord of Hosts:

You have nothing but what you have received from me—neither you, nor your father.

Provide, therefore, from what you have (which is mine)—that is to say, from what your power can reach in your own faculty and riches—to show your goodwill and ready efforts in bringing these things to pass, as you have learned from me. Δ. **Upon** this former part of the Third General Action, where my first-born son (namely *Arthur*) was assigned to the Ministry of seeing and hearing, in place and stead of E.K. if he should utterly refuse the same office (hitherto executed by him, and to be executed by him until the seven general actions are finished); and that the same child and son, in the meantime (that is to say, between the day that part of the Action was received, and the end of the same: determined to be fourteen days later) should be exercised before God. But when E.K. said to me that I should exercise the child and not he, and that he would not, I thereupon decided to bring the child to the place myself, and to offer him and present him to the service of Seeing and Scrying from God, and by God's assignment; and of the time of fourteen days yet remaining—being the 15th, 16th, and 17th days of *April*, and just before the 18th day (the day assigned to end the Action)—to have the child exercised in them. Enlighten (therefore), O Almighty God, my eyes, and open my ears; quicken, instruct and confirm in me, and for me, my discretion, judgment, understanding, memory, and utterance, so that I may be a true and perfect Seer, Hearer, Declarer and Witness of such things which—either immediately from your Divine Majesty, or mediately by the ministry of your holy, mighty, and faithful Angels—shall be manifested, declared or shown to me, now, and at all times and occasions, for the advancing of your Praise, Honor and Glory. Amen.*

$\Delta$. Finally, by wonderful fortune or divine fate, Mr. E.K. came to us, and I noted what followed.

Uriel.

$\Delta$. He sat down by us; and while Arthur was still standing before me at the table, which was covered in the best manner, with only the stone set on it, he asked if anything appeared. Then he said, "I wonder if you had no appearance here; for thinking somewhat of Arthur and his progress in the feat of scrying, I came here into the gallery, and I heard you pray. Opening the window, I looked out, and I saw a great number going in and out of this chapel at the little hole in the glass window. I saw Madimi, Il, and many others who had dealt with us before, but they showed themselves in a very filthy manner. And Uriel appeared and confirmed all to be from God and good. Therefore I wonder that you have no vision here; perhaps there is something, but Arthur does not see it."

$\Delta$. It is true; and how should I help him in this, seeing I cannot yet see or scry?

E.K. I will come and see if there is anything.

$\Delta$. I pray you do. <note>And so E.K. looked toward the stone, and he immediately said, "Something appears here," and pointed out where to Arthur, and asked him if he saw anything; and he said No. Then E.K. said:</note>

E.K. I see something like a white marble square table or book lying on a wooden desk.

$\Delta$. I pray you, Sir, take the pains to look and discern what is shown here.

E.K. I see written upon that book:
> Blessed is she who, through sin, restores to me the falling house and makes it whole for men.

E.K. Now a leaf of that book is turned open, and there is something written on it, but I cannot read it yet. Now I see it:
> I am he who has given and will give you the law, from which eternal rest and happiness shall come to mortals.

E.K. Now another leaf is turned over, and there appears written:
> Therefore, be such as befits me and my own, and walk thoughtfully before me.

E.K. Now the leaf turns over by itself:

E.K. Now the leaf turns:

E.K. Now the desk and book or table are gone.

E.K. I see a hand appear, a very large one, white, with the fingers spread wide.

## The second part of the third action.

<margin>1587. Saturday, April 18.</margin>
> *Prayers to Almighty God, for the imparting of his truth to us, to the praise, honor, and glory of his name.*

$\Delta$. Note: Arthur was set to the stone, but nothing appeared; E. K. had brought the powder with him as he was commanded to do. Then I desired him to apply himself to see as he was accustomed to do. And so he did.

E. K. Here appear all those in the stone that appeared to me yesterday in the air in that most disorderly and filthy manner. They are in the same clothing as yesterday.

$\Delta$. O God, confirm us in your truth for your own honor and glory, and do not suffer us to be overcome with any temptation, but deliver us from all evil now and ever.

E. K. Madimi, Il, and the rest appeared: and so they are here; but now all the rest are gone, and only Madimi remains.

Madimi opens all her clothing and shows herself completely naked; she also shows her private parts.

E. K. Fie on you! Devil, depart from here with this filthiness, etc.

Madimi: *In the name of God, why do you find fault with me?*

$\Delta$. Because your yesterday's actions and words are provocations to sin, and unsuitable for any godly creature to use.

Madimi: *What is sin?*

$\Delta$. To break the commandment of God.

Madimi: *Record that; so.*

Madimi: *If the very same God gives you a new commandment, taking away the former form of sin which he limited by the Law, what remains then?*

$\Delta$. <margin>$\Delta$. A privilege granted does not abolish a law, but otherwise indicates the force of the law in itself.</margin>
Mad. *The laws of God, and of his Son Christ, established by the testimony of his disciples and congregation, and by the force and power of his Holy Spirit, are not abolished in any particular calling, but rather confirmed.*

*For it often happens that when God is offended by the wickedness of any man, or of some private man, he sends down his Spirit of Death, infecting and tempting another man's mind; so that he becomes void of reason and rises up against the one with whom God is offended, and strikes him so that he dies. In the eyes of man, this is accounted sin; before God, it shall be attributed to him as righteousness. Even so, whatever the Spirit of God teaches us from him, though it appears as sin to man, is righteousness before him.*

<margin>\* Arthur was struck into a faint, and E.K. saw one in a long white garment act as though he would strike him. He was very sick at the time.</margin>
*Therefore, assure yourselves that whatever is seen and heard among you is from above, and is a sign and testimony even this day before you; for I who touched your son\* might also have taken away his breath.*

*But oh, you have little understanding: but behold, I teach you.*

*That for those who are considered righteous (through the good will of God), sin is justly punished, but not as it is for the wicked. For whatever you have done to other men, the very same shall fall upon you; but happy is he who receives justice not through the terror of a curse, but through the grace and mercy of God.*

<margin>Justice. St. Paul's lusts. Good Angels.</margin>
*The Apostle Paul abounded in carnal lust: he was also offensive to his brothers, so that he despaired and was ready to have left his calling, until the Lord said to him, "My mercy and grace are sufficient for you."*

*Believe me, we are from above.*

*Consider this: consider also that just as you cannot comprehend the heavens, you likewise cannot comprehend the wisdom of God, who says, "I will be merciful to whom I please; and to whom I will not, I have none in store." He is foolish who asks "why?"*

<margin>The wisdom of God is incomprehensible to us.</margin>
*And behold, I say to you: do not stumble against God. Who is he that made you? Who is he that has given you power to look up toward heaven? You are fools and have little understanding: today God says to you,*

*Behold, you have become free: do that which most pleases you. For behold, your own reason rises up against my wisdom.*

*You are not content to be heirs, but you would be lords, even gods, even the judges of the heavens. Therefore, do even as you wish; but if you forsake the way taught you from above, behold, evil shall enter into your senses, and abomination shall dwell before your eyes as a reward to those you have wronged; and your wives and children shall be carried away before your face.*

> $\Delta$. May the Almighty God of heaven and earth be my comfort, as I desire comfort in his service; and give me wisdom as I desire it for his honor and glory, Amen.

$\Delta$ I was glad that an offer was made to be taught the secrets of the books already delivered to us every seventh day: thinking that it was easy for us to maintain that unity which was required among us four; understanding everything in a Christian and godly sense. But E.K., who had yesterday seen and heard another meaning of this required unity, utterly abhorred having any further dealings with them, and intended to accept from them the liberty of leaving off dealing with them anymore. Since his interpretation was strange and unpleasant to me, I earnestly requested to be resolved in the matter as follows.

At the same time and in the same place this ensued.

### N O T E.

$\Delta$ Upon Mr. Kelley's great doubt caused to me by Madimi's words yesterday, spoken to him, that *we two had our two wives in such a way that we might use them in common*, it was agreed by us to ask the question: whether the meaning concerned *carnal use* (contrary to the law of the Commandment) or *spiritual love*, and charitable care and unity of minds, for advancing the service of God.

E.K. Upon a scroll, like the edge of a carpet, is written,

->*De utroque loquor.* <note>Latin: "I speak of both."</note><-

$\Delta$ The one is expressly against the commandment of God; nor can I by any means consent to approve of that doctrine. And for my help in that truth, I call down the power of Almighty God, the creator of heaven and earth, and all the good angels (his faithful ministers), to assist me in defending my faithful obedience to the law of the Gospel and of his Church.

E. K. It appears written upon a white Crucifix, as follows:
> *My grace is greater than the command. For this grace of mine is such that bliss might be granted to insane men. And as for the things that have been spoken: Let them either be so, or today your liberty is restored to you. Amen, I say to you, that if I said to a man, "Go and slit your father's throat," and he did not do it, he is a son of sin and death. For all things are possible and lawful for the heavenly beings. Nor are shameful things more hateful to them than the faces of any mortals whatsoever. For so it shall happen: the illegitimate shall be joined with the son (which is even more absurd). And the east with the west; the south also with the north shall be united.*

E. K. Now it has vanished.

$\Delta$. At this, we were in great amazement and grief of mind that such a hard and (as it still seemed to me) so impure a doctrine was proposed and enjoined upon us by those whom I always (from the beginning until now) judged and esteemed, undoubtedly, to be good angels. I had even offered my soul to E. K. as a pledge to guarantee E. K.’s belief in them as the good and faithful ministers of Almighty God. But now, my heart was sorely afflicted for many reasons; and E. K. believed he now had a just and sufficient cause to stop dealing with them anymore, as his prayer to God has been for a long time (as may appear in the earlier part of this Action).

After leaving the chapel, and while we were at dinner—when the four of us (whose heads were united in a pillar as shown before) were together—I found a way to make a small declaration of our great grief (especially mine) now caused by the command, whether to test us or to be actually carried out: the common and indiscriminate use of matrimonial acts among any couple of us four. This matter was strange to the women, and they hoped for some more comforting outcome of the situation. And so we left it there.

<margin>Ben was the one who delivered the powder to E. K. at the excavation in England. Note, unless conditionally. Queen Elizabeth. King Philip.</margin>
After dinner, while E. K. was alone, there appeared to him little creatures about a cubit high. They came to the still where he had the spirit of wine distilling over from a retort. One of them (whose name they expressed as *Ben*) said that it was in vain to hope for the best spirit of the wine in that way; he showed him how to distill it and separate it better. Moreover, he showed how to get oil from the spirit of wine as it burned in the lamps. He then began to ask *E. K.* what countryman he was. When he answered an *Englishman*, the spirit then asked how he came here. He answered "by sea." Then the spirit said, "And who helped you to pass the marvelous and great dangers of the sea?" Thus, he took the opportunity to speak of the many benefits which God had done for us until now. And this *Ben* then said, among many other things (as Mr. E. K. told me on Saturday night after supper, continuing his talk almost until two o'clock after midnight), *that it was he who delivered to him, or gave into his hands, the powder.* He also said, either then or the next day at the latest, *that unless he would be conformable to the will of God in this last declared Action, he would take the virtue and power from the powder so that it would be useless, and he [Kelley] would become a beggar.*

<margin>England.</margin>
And of me also, he said *that I did evil to require proof or testimony now that this last doctrine was from God Almighty; and he said that I would be led as a prisoner to Rome, etc.*
He spoke of *England* and said that about *July* or *November*, her Majesty would be destroyed from heaven, and that about the same time the *King of Spain* would die. He also said that this present Pope, at his Mass, would be deprived of life before two years were over. And that another would be Pope, who would be *the fifteenth* of his name; and that he would begin to reform things, but that shortly he would be stoned to death by the Cardinals. And that after that, there would be no Pope for some years.

Of *England*, he said that after the death of our dear Queen, one of the House of *Austria*, made mighty by the *death of the King of Spain*, would invade and conquer the land, etc. He said one (now abroad) would enter at *Milford Haven* and, with the help of the *Britons*, subdue the said Conqueror; and that one *Morgan, a Briton*, would be made King of the Britons, and after him, one *Rowland, etc.*

<margin>Francis Garland. Edward Garland.</margin>
He said also that this *Francis Garland* was a spy upon us from the Lord Treasurer of *England*; and that *Edward Garland* is not his brother; and that the matter is agreed upon between them in that way, etc.

He said that my Lord *Rosenberg* would be in danger of poisoning for these certain months to come.

<margin>Enoch's Tables.</margin>
That my Tables of *Enoch* were falsely written in some places.

<margin>Antichrist.</margin>
He spoke of the Antichrist and of his appearing.

<margin>Elijah, Enoch. John the Evangelist.</margin>
He spoke of *Elijah* and *Enoch* coming out of Paradise, and of Saint *John the Evangelist*—that he did not die, but had his invisible being on Patmos; and that it was he who gave Julian the Apostate his death wound.

He also said that he has preached visibly at various times since the time he entered *his invisible state.*

<margin>Jane Dee.</margin>
After all these and many other things told to me by the same Mr. E. K., we each went to our beds, where I found my wife awake, waiting to hear some new matter from me regarding Mr. Kelley’s reports of the apparitions. Having continued with him alone for above four hours, I then told her, saying, "Jane, I see that there is no other remedy; as has been said of our cross-matching <note>The spiritual command for Dee and Kelley to share their wives.</note>, so it must be done."

At this, she fell into weeping and trembling for a quarter of an hour; and I pacified her as well as I could. And so, in the fear of God and in belief of His admonishment, I persuaded her until she appeared fairly well resolved to be content, for God’s sake and His secret purposes, to obey the admonishment.

# A true Relation of Dr. Dee’s Actions with Spirits, etc.

<margin>$\Delta$. Note:</margin>
When *E.K.* had shown me this Note, I immediately brought forth my book of Enoch's Tables and found the four letters *r, T, b, d* to be the first four letters of the four principal squares positioned around the black Cross. I found that here they were to be placed differently than I had previously set them. In my first arrangement of them together, I remember having doubts about how to join them, for they were given separately, each by itself.

Secondly, I found the four Characters, except they were somewhat inverted and one of them was closed; I found none exactly like them, but very similar. One of these characters belonged to each square.

Thirdly, I interpreted these numbers contained between the lines (some more and some fewer) as words to be gathered from the Table of letters: there were as many words as there were distinct groups of numbers, namely 41.

Upon this, we began to number the squares where the letters stood in Enoch's Tables as I had them, but we could not find the words exactly, though we came somewhat close. Being tired and desiring to know the meaning of that cipher, we stopped until after supper, and then we tried again. However, we could not figure it out, even though we knew very nearly what was to be done through the instruction of a *spiritual Voice* that occasionally helped us with the procedure.

At length, *E.K.* was directed to go *down* into his chamber, and I remained at our dining table until his return, which was within an hour or slightly more. Upon his return, he brought this in writing.

<margin>

# A true Relation of Dr. Dee’s Actions with Spirits, etc.

...... *The black Cross is right, and needs no mending. But I do this much to let you understand, so that you may consider yourself to be a man: And beneath this understanding, unless you submit everything into the hands of God, for his sake; who otherwise leaving you, all naked, provides for his creatures to his own glory.*

...... *Your wife is dear to you, wisdom is dearer to you, but I am the dearest to you. As one chosen, you tremble, and by hesitating you sin: Therefore, do not seek wisdom according to your own nature and inclination; but obey me: for I am your leader and the author of the spirit of all. All these things are from me, and are lawful for you.*

...... *I admonish you as the children of God, to consider your vocation, and the love of God towards you; and not to prefer your reason before the wisdom of the Highest, whose mercy is so great towards you, that you are chosen from among the number of men to walk with him, and to understand his mysteries, and also to execute his justice and praise throughout the nations and people of the earth. Consider that if he finds you obstinate, the plagues of heinous sinners and despisers of the gifts of God shall fall upon you, to your great overthrow: This is the last time of your trial. Therefore show yourselves lovers of him who has led you, and covered you with a mighty shield: Or shortly look for the reward of such as have despised the Wisdom and Majesty of the Highest.*

*I, Raphael, counsel you to make a Covenant with the Highest, and to esteem his wings more than your own lives.*

<margin>April 20.</margin>
$\Delta$. When E.K. had brought me these things, I greatly rejoiced in spirit, and was utterly resolved to obey this new Doctrine enjoined peculiarly to us, of all people of the world. And after some little discourse and conference about this, we went to bed, this 20th day of April, at night.

## April 21.

<margin>$\Delta$.</margin>
Thus am I resolved, O Almighty God, concerning the case so hard for flesh and blood to be resolved in, as follows: And thus I desire that we all four might with one mind and consent, offer and present to you this writing as a Vow, Promise, and Covenant, if it so pleases your divine majesty to accept it.

WE four (whose heads appeared under one Crystalline Crown, united and enclosed in one pillar) do most humbly and heartily thank you, O Almighty God (our Creator, Redeemer and Sanctifier) for all your mercies and benefits received until now, in our persons, and in those who belong to us: And at this present time, we faithfully and sincerely confess and acknowledge that your profound wisdom in this most new and strange doctrine (among Christians) proposed, commended, and enjoined to us four only, is above our human reason and Christian profession to like. For in the outward appearance of words, it seems to us expressly to be contrary to the purity and chastity which is exactly required of us and all Christians, your followers. Notwithstanding, we will, in this, captivate and tread underfoot all our human, fearful doubting of any inconvenience which shall or may fall upon us, or follow us in this world, or in the world to come, in respect of or by reason of our embracing this Doctrine, listened to by us as delivered from our true and living God, the Creator of heaven and earth; who alone has the true original power and authority to release and discharge sins: And whose pardoning and not imputing of sin to us, through our lively faith in the most worthy merit and precious blood of the Immaculate Lamb shed for us, is and shall be our justification and salvation. We, therefore (according to blessed Raphael's counsel last given), most humbly and sincerely require your Divine Majesty to accept this our Covenant with you (so that your merciful promises made to us may be performed for us; and your divine purposes in us and by us may be furthered, advanced, and fulfilled). *That, as we acknowledge your divine wisdom and grace offered to us in this your last mystical Admonishment; and as you most earnestly will us to accept the same as lawful and just with you; which Admonishment consists of two parts: namely, our true spiritual Christian charity between us four, and also the Matrimonial license and liberty to be used among us four without distinction: So we the same four (who will subscribe to this) covenant with your Divine Majesty, upon the two principal respects before rehearsed, truly and unfeignedly to accept and perform henceforth among us four, in word, thought and deed, Christian charity and perfect friendship, and all that belongs to it: And as for the Matrimonial-like license and liberty,*

I *Edward Kelley* by good and provident (according to the Laws and ordinances of God) determination and consideration in these former Actions—that is to say, appearances, shows made, and voices uttered by those named within this Book, and all the rest of whatever Spirits have from the beginning thereof (which appears at large by the Records)—not only doubted and disliked their insinuations and the doctrine uttered, but also at various and several times (as desiring to escape and avoid the danger and inconvenience that might follow from them, themselves, or the drift of their doctrine, or happen to my injury in various ways) sought to depart from the exercises thereof: and withal boldly (as the servant of the Son of God) spoke out against them: urging them to depart, or render a better reason for their unknown and incredible words and speeches delivered; and at the same time often and several times friendly exhorted the Right Worshipful Master JOHN DEE (the chief follower thereof)—as also appears in the Records—to regard his soul's health, the good progress of his worldly credit (which is great throughout Europe), the better future maintenance of his wife and children, to beware of them, and withal to give them up: in which although I friendly and brotherly labored, my labor seemed to be lost and my counsel despised by him, and moreover I was urged with replies to the contrary made by him, and promises, in that case, of the loss of his soul's health, if they were not of God: Whereupon, after as it were some further taste of them, or an opinion grounded upon the frailty of zeal, he did not cease also to pawn his soul to me, etc. these persuasions of his were the chief and only cause of my proceeding with them for so long: And now also at this instant, and a few days ago, having manifest occasion to think they were the servants of *Satan*, and the children of darkness; because they clearly urged and commanded in the name of God a Damnable Doctrine, and contrary to the Laws of God, his Commandments, and the Gospel delivered to us by our Savior Christ as a *touchstone* <note>A standard or criterion by which something is judged.</note>, I did openly express to them my dislike of their proceeding, and brotherly warned the said Worshipful, and my good friend *Mr.* JOHN DEE to beware of them: And now having just occasion to determine what they were, to consider all

...these things previously mentioned by me, and wisely to leave them; and even more so because they themselves (as appears by their own words), upon our failure to follow that delivered Doctrine, gave us a *Quietus est* <note>A formal discharge or release from a debt or obligation.</note>, or passport of freedom. But the Books being brought <margin>* April 22 at night.</margin> forth, after some discussion of them, and after a day or two had passed and their previously spoken words were perused, they did as it were (because of the possible truth of them, *for with God all things are possible*) give us cause for further deliberation. So that thereby, I did—partly on my own, and partly by the true meaning of the said *Mr.* DEE in receiving them as from God, and in a way because of the zeal I saw him bear for the true worship and glory of God to be promoted by us (as was promised by them)—abandon my own position and yield to his opinion and determination, giving up all reason or anything else for the love of God. <margin>The women.</margin> But the women utterly disliked this last Doctrine, and consulting among themselves, gave us this answer: the former actions did not offend them at all but much comforted them; and therefore this last one, not agreeing with the rest (which they think to be according to the good will and wholesome Law of God), makes them fear, because it is expressly contrary to the Commandment of God. And thereupon, desiring God not to be offended by their ignorance, they required another action for better information in this matter; in the meantime, vowing, fasting, and praying, *Mrs.* DEE has covenanted <margin>An action required by the women.</margin> with God to abstain from eating fish and meat until His Divine Majesty satisfies their minds according to His established Laws, received throughout all Christendom. To this request of theirs to have an action, I absolutely answer that my simplicity before the Highest is such that I trust it will excuse me. And because the sum of this Doctrine, given in His name, requires obedience which I have (as is written before) offered, I think myself discharged. Therefore, I have no further cause to hazard myself any more in any action. Why, I answer that if it is lawful for them to call this Doctrine into question, it is even more lawful for me to doubt of greater peril; considering that to go where we are absolutely answered would be folly, and might result in my great inconvenience. Therefore, beseeching God to have mercy upon me and to satisfy their petitions, doubts, and vows, I finally answer that I will from this day forward meddle no more in this matter. April 22, 1587.

->By me<-

->EDWARD KELLY.<-

## April 24. Trebona.

<margin>April 24. Friday.</margin>
$\Delta$. Prayers were made to God regarding this strange and new doctrine, asking His Divine Majesty to be merciful to us, and to give us wisdom and faith so that we may please him in this; and stating that we cannot find how we may do the thing required, as it is contrary to the Laws of Moses, Christ, his Church, and of all Nations. Therefore, seeing that God is not contrary to himself, we desired that we might not be contrary to him or his Laws, etc.

$\Delta$. Not long after, look, there appeared a great flame of fire in the principal stone (both stones standing on the Table before E.K.). Although he told me this, I did not end my prayer to God. And behold, suddenly someone seemed to come in at the south window of the Chapel, directly across from E.K. (But before that, the stone was lifted up a handful high and set down again steadily, which E.K. thought signified some strange matter approaching.) Then afterward, the man who came in at the window seemed to have his lower parts in a cloud, and with spread-open arms came toward E.K. At this sight, he shrank back somewhat, and then that creature took up the stone and golden frame between both his hands and mounted up, leaving the way he came. E.K. reached for it, but he could not touch it. Because it was taken away in such a manner, and at the sight of it, E.K. was in a great fear and trembling, and had *tremorem cordis* <note>Trembling of the heart; palpitations.</note> for a while. But I was very glad and well pleased.

¶ Here a fire appears in this other stone also, and a man in the fire, with flaxen hair hanging down upon him; he is naked down to his breasts and seems to have spots of blood upon him. He spoke, and said as follows:

> *If I had intended to overthrow you, or bring you to confusion, or suffered you to be led into temptation beyond your strength and power, then the seas would have swallowed you long ago. Yes, not a soul would have lived among you.* <note>Christ speaking.</note>

<margin>The Law and the Gospel.</margin>
> *But the law and the tidings of gladness (to mankind) are both grounded in me. I am the Beginning and the Ending: and behold, happy is he who delights in me, for in me is truth and understanding. Whatever you have received, you have received from me; and without me you have received nothing. Behold, I myself was even the figure of misery and death for your sins. Why (therefore) do you disdain to be shaped after me? I will gather the four quarters of the earth together, and they shall become one.*

<margin>$\Delta$ and E.K. a figure of two people to come.</margin>
> *And as I have made you the figure of two people to come, and among them, the executors of my justice: so likewise have I sanctified you in a holy ordinance, giving you a figure of the first fruits of the time to come. Happy is he who is a serpent in the wilderness hung up upon the Cross, being the will and figure of my determination and Kingdom to come: I am even at the doors; and I will overthrow all flesh. I will no longer delight in the sons of men.*

<margin>$\Delta$. * He answers a phrase of my prayer or discourse. This doctrine is not to be published to any man.</margin>
> ** I teach you nothing contrary to myself.*

> *For this doctrine is not to be published to mortal men: but is given to you to manifest your faith, and to make you worthy in the sight of the heavens for believing in me concerning your vocation to come.*

> *Therefore I say to you: Rejoice, and do not be anxious for tomorrow: for I, even I, have provided for you. Sin no more.*

<margin>Note. One shepherd and one fold.</margin>
> *Behold! None of the Orders, either of Heaven or Earth, are authorized to open their mouths in my Name, teaching or opening this doctrine, unless it were from me, for I am the First and the Last. And I will be Shepherd over all, so that the Kingdom of my Father may come, and that my Spirit may be upon all flesh, where there shall be no law, nor need of light: I myself am their lantern forever.*

<margin>The Devil's attempt.</margin>
> *And behold, I will be as a Rock between you and the teeth of Leviathan, which seeks to set you asunder and to bring you to confusion.*

> *And I am, and am holy, and holiness itself: out of me comes no unclean thing.*

<margin>Moses. Sterility of the Earth.</margin>
> *For even as the time of Moses was wonderful to all the Gentiles, even so shall those days to come be to the nations and kings of the earth. I am a law forever. And behold, power is given to me from above: and I have visited the earth, and have thrown my curse upon her: and lo, she shall become barren.*

<margin>The show of 4 trees, what it means. Pectoral with Urim and Thummim. Numbers.</margin>

Yes, even I it is who have taken you four Trees out of the forest of the world, and have covered you until now with my wings. And behold, this which is taken away shall be restored to you again with more power. And might shall be in it, and it shall be a breastplate of judgment and knowledge for you.*

> *And if there be any of you who seeks a miracle at my hands and believes in my words, let him or her present themselves here next Monday, with the rest, and he shall perceive that I am the Judge of Abiram and the God of Abraham: Walk before me as the sons of my*

<margin>April 18, 1587.</margin>
WE four (whose heads appeared under one crystalline crown, and united and enclosed in one pillar) do most humbly and heartily thank you (O Almighty God, our Creator, Redeemer, and Sanctifier) for all your mercies and benefits received until now in our own persons, and in those who belong to us. And at this present time, we faithfully and sincerely confess and acknowledge that your profound wisdom in this most new and strange doctrine (among Christians) proposed, commended, and enjoined upon us four only, is above our human reason and our Catholic Christian profession to approve of: because, in the outward appearance of words, it seems to us expressly contrary to the purity and chastity which is exactly required of us and all Christians (your followers). Nevertheless, for your sake, we will here captivate and tread underfoot all our human, timid doubting of any inconvenience which shall or may fall upon us, or follow us (in this world, or in the world to come) regarding or by reason of our embracing of this doctrine, which we listened to as delivered from you, our true and living God, the Creator of heaven and earth, who alone has the true original power and authority of releasing and discharging sins; and whose pardoning, or not imputing of sin to us, through our lively faith in the most worthy merit and precious blood of your immaculate Lamb, shed for us, is and shall be our justification and salvation.

<margin>April 20, deep in the night.</margin>
We therefore (according to the counsel lately given by blessed Raphael) most humbly and sincerely require your divine majesty to accept this our covenant with you (to the intent that all your merciful and gracious promises made to the four of us, or any of us, may be performed for us; and also that your divine purposes in us, and by us, may be furthered, advanced, and fulfilled). (This admonition consists of two parts; namely, true and complete Christian charity to be kept inviolably between the four of us. And also the new matrimonial-like license and liberty to be used among the four of us without distinction.)

<margin>* Referring to the mark above.</margin>

And as for the matrimonial-like license, we accept and allow of it. ### 1587. Třeboň, in the small Chapel.

<margin>$\Delta$.</margin>
The aforementioned Covenant being framed by me, *John Dee*, as near as I could according to the intent and faith required of us, to be notified and declared by the works of unity both spiritual and physical. *Now, it was considered necessary by the women as well as ourselves to understand the will of God and his good pleasure: whether this Covenant and the form of words performed is and will be acceptable, and according to the approval of his Divine Majesty. And whether, upon the act of physical intimacy being performed on both our parts, it will please his Divine Majesty to seal and guarantee to us most certainly and speedily all his Divine, merciful, and bountiful promises and blessings; and also promise us wisdom, knowledge, ability, and power to execute his justice, and to declare and demonstrate his infallible truth among men, to his honor and glory.*

Upon this, E.K. and I went to the Chapel to the South Table. <margin>$\Delta$.</margin> To this end, I prayed to Almighty God, Creator of heaven and earth, that he would fatherly, favorably, and mercifully regard the sincerity and distress of my heart, desiring him to increase my faith and to open the eyes of my heart, that I may see *Opera digitorum & mirabilia ejus, nobis sicuti necessaria* <note>the works of his fingers and his wonders, as they are necessary for us</note>, for his service and glory, and for the confusion and overthrow of his enemies. *Amen.*

I read over the Covenant (*word for word*) before the Divine Majesty and his holy Angels.

*...you have made with me, behold, the time shall come that you shall be torn in pieces yourself, and I will even turn my face away from you for a time. Friday afternoon about four o'clock.

The restoration of the holy stone.

...... $\Delta$ ...... As I and E. K. walked out at the new stairs, into the new orchard toward the little river to view the small fish, and returning to the front stairs again, E. K. saw two figures as high as my son Arthur fighting by the riverside with swords; and about four o'clock, one said to the other, "You have deceived me." Then I, at length, said unto them, "Can I settle the matter between you?" One said, "Yes, that you can." "In what is it?" I asked. Then he said, "I sent a thing to your wife by my man, and this fellow has taken it from him." They fought hard, and at length, he that had it was wounded in the thigh, and it seemed to bleed. Afterward, he that was wounded brought a yellow square thing out of his bosom; then I guessed it to be my Stone that was taken away. The other said unto him, "Let it be carried." Suddenly he seemed to have gone out of sight and to have come again; he threatened the other who had wounded him and said he would be even with him. The other said, "Have you laid it under the right pillow of the bed where his wife lay last night?"

At length they both went (one after another) into the trunk of a little willow tree on the right hand next to the new stairs into the garden; the tree seemed to split open, and they went in.

Hereupon we went away. And I, coming to my chamber, found my wife lying upon her bed (where I lay last night), and there I lifted up the right pillow, upon which she lay resting herself (not being well at ease). And there, beneath her shoulders, I found my precious Stone that was taken away by Madimi. At which E. K. greatly wondered, doubting the truth of the vision. But I and my wife rejoiced, thanking God.

### Saturday, May 23. In the morning, around 9:30

Prayers were poured out to God, etc. And then we requested that the act of obedience performed (according to the faith we conceived of our vocation from the Almighty and Eternal God of heaven and earth) might be accepted. And that from now on, we might be instructed in the understanding and practice of wisdom—both that in which we have already received some mystical introductions, and also in all other things that Almighty God shall deem fit for us to know and execute for his honor and glory, etc.

∆ E. K. took pen and ink and wrote the request joined here; and he read it to me, and he requested me to read it to the Divine Majesty; and so I did. Thereupon we both waited for the divine answer to my first prayer and to this petition.

∆ Almighty, eternal, true, and living God, send your light and your truth so that they may lead us and guide us to the holy mountain, Zion, out of this valley of misery, and to your Heavenly Jerusalem. Amen.

E. K. From the beginning of this our coming, there appeared a purple circle as large as a star in the circumference of the holy Stone, which was brought back yesterday. And that it should be so, Madimi had forewarned E. K. when she showed it to him, at which time she also gave the prints of the letters on the back of the bottom of its gold frame.

<margin>White horse</margin>
...... E. K. There appears here a great man all in bright armor, sitting upon a white horse. He has a fiery spear in his left hand, which he now puts into his right hand. He has a long sword by his side. He also has a shield hanging on his back; it seems to be made of steel. It hangs from his neck by a blue cord; it comes up behind him as high as the top of his head. The horse is milk-white, all studded with white; it is a very handsome horse. The man is in complete armor; the top of his helmet has a sharp point.

Upon his shield are many cherubim, as if painted in circles. There is one in the middle. Around it is a circle with six in it, and then a circle with eight, and then a large circle with ten in it, and in the largest are twenty; and around the circle of twenty <margin>Total.</margin> are seven parts: at each of those points is a cherub. Their faces are like burning gold; their wings are brighter, and as it were, their wings coming over their heads do <margin>Cherub.</margin> not touch together. His horse is also armored in front and behind. The horse's hind legs are armored as if with boots marvelously designed, for the defense, as it were, of its hind legs.

E. K. He has ridden away; he seems to ride through a great field.

E. K. Madimi has come here now.

E. K. She has gone into the field, in the direction he rode.

E. K. Here is another, like a woman all in green.

E. K. Here comes another woman: all her attire is like beaten gold. She has a crystal cross on her forehead; her neck and breast are bare down to below her breasts. She has a girdle of beaten gold loosely buckled around her, with a gold pendant hanging down to the ground.

# A true Relation of Dr. Dee his Actions with Spirits, etc.

*I am the Daughter of Fortitude, and am ravished every hour, from my youth. For behold, I am Understanding, and Science dwells in me; and the heavens oppress me; they covet and desire me with infinite appetite. Few or none who are earthly have embraced me, for I am shadowed with the Circle of the Stone, and covered with the morning clouds. My feet are swifter than the winds, and my hands are sweeter than the morning dew. My garments are from the beginning, and my dwelling place is in myself. The Lion does not know where I walk, nor do the beasts of the field understand me. I am deflowered, and yet a virgin; I sanctify, and am not sanctified. Happy is he who embraces me: for in the night season I am sweet, and in the day full of pleasure. My company is a harmony of many cymbals, and my lips are sweeter than health itself. I am a harlot for those who ravish me, and a virgin with those who do not know me. For lo, I am loved by many, and I am a lover to many; and as many as come to me as they should, are welcomed. Purge your streets, O you sons of men, and wash your houses clean; make yourselves holy, and put on righteousness. Cast out your old prostitutes, and burn their clothes; abstain from the company of other women who are defiled, who are slovenly, and not as handsome and beautiful as I, and then I will come and dwell among you. And behold, I will bring forth children for you, and they shall be the Sons of Comfort. I will open my garments and stand naked before you, so that your love may be more inflamed toward me.*

<margin>
The four: 
$\Delta$ (Dee), E.K. (Kelley), I.K. (Jane Kelley), & I.A. (Jane Dee).
</margin>

Behold these four: who is he that shall say they have sinned? Or to whom shall they give an account? Not to you, O you sons of men, nor to your children: for to the Lord belongs the judgment of his servants.*

A blessing for obedience according to faith.

And power shall be given to you from henceforth to resist your enemies, and the Lord shall always hear you in the time of your troubles. And I am sent to you to play the harlot with you, and am to enrich you with the spoils of other men. Prepare for me, for I come shortly. Provide your chambers for me, so that they may be sweet and clean; for I will make a dwelling-place among you. And I will be common with the father and the son, yes, and with all those who truly favor you: for my youth is in her flowers, and my strength is not to be extinguished by man. Strong am I above and below; therefore provide for me. For behold, I now salute you, and let peace be among you; for I am the Daughter of Comfort. Do not disclose my secrets to women, nor let them understand how sweet I am, for all things do not belong to everyone. I come to you again.*

### 1587. ->Saturday the same day.<-

After dinner, about four hours later, or somewhat less, we resorted to the place.

A voice to E.K. Kneel toward the East; so he kneeled at the table of the Covenant, with his face toward the East; and I at my table opposite to him.

Δ ...... In the Name of God the Father, God the Son, and God the Holy Ghost. *Amen.*

*Teach us to know and understand rightly (O Lord), for your wisdom is all that we seek. Put your word in our mouth and fix your wisdom in our hearts.*

E. K. The Book remains hanging in the air.

A voice ...... Kelly, I know it is troublesome for thee to kneel: Sit. <note>A great pause.</note>

Δ ...... So E.K. rose from kneeling, and sat down.

...... E. K. Now she is here, who last advised us.

<margin>
The book divided.
</margin>
She takes the book and divides it into two parts: and it seems to be two books: one half-cover adjoining to one, and the other half-cover belonging to the other; the sides with the covers are toward me.

<margin>
He was made in the image of God.
</margin>
*...... Wisdom is a piercing beam, which is the center of the spiritual being of the holy Spirit, touching from all parts from where the Divinity sends it out: and is proper to the soul, or to substances that have a beginning but no ending; so that whatever shall have an end can never attain to that which is called Wisdom: Neither can things that are subject to the second death receive any such influence, because they are already noted and marked with the seat of destruction. Happy is he whom God has made a vessel of salvation; for to him belong joy and a crown of reward. Adam (your forefather and first parent), in respect of his creation—that is to say, in respect of his imaginative composition—received no strength except by the Holy Ghost; for the soul of man is free from all passions and affections until it enters into the body to which it is limited: so that, being neither good nor bad (but apt for both), he is left, by Divine providence and permission, joined together to the end of the one or the other. But wherever wisdom dwells, it dwells not with the soul as any property of it, but according to the good will of God, whose mercy concurs on every side into him and takes up a mansion therein, to utter out and manifest his great goodness. And even as the heavens are glorified continually with the Spirit of God, so is the soul of man glorified that receives sanctification thereby; for no man is illuminated who is not sanctified: neither is there any man perfectly sanctified who is not illuminated. I speak this (my brothers) so that you shall understand that no man did, or can ever, attain to wisdom (that perfect wisdom I speak of) unless he becomes a center in his soul to the mercies and good will of God, comprehending him and dwelling in him; therefore lift up your eyes and see, call your wits together, and mark my words. To teach you or explain to you the mysteries of the Books that you have already received is not in my power, but in the good will of God, after whose Image I am:*
<margin>
The understanding of the explanation of our former books.
The good will of God.
The knowledge of Adam.
</margin>
*This good will of God is the descending of his holy Spirit abundantly upon you and into you, opening all your senses and making you perfect men: for Adam understood by that grace, and his eyes were opened so that he saw and knew all things that were within his understanding. So have all those, more and less, who have been counted wise, received the gifts of the Holy Ghost, which sets the soul of man so on fire that he pierces into all things and judges mightily. The Apostles, who knew even the thoughts of men, understood all things because the holy Spirit made a dwelling place in them: even so shall it happen to you. For you are the chosen of these last days, and such as shall be full of the blessings of God, and his Spirit shall rest with you abundantly. Mark, therefore, what I have to say to you.*

The Apostles.

Magnificent men, brothers and dearest friends. Today at 9:00 in the morning, these letters were brought to me from Lord Schomberg, which were sent on March 5, and should have already come into my hands before now. From these, I understand that he, along with Lord Holek, is awaiting a response from Münsterberg. Since that Almighty moderator and ruler of all things has delegated you to this ministry and to the completion of this work, I know nothing of what is to be done, nor can any counsel of mine be added to it, so that I might arrange, know, or wish for anything; except that which has seemed best to that most wise Moderator. Therefore, I transmit everything to you. Pray diligently, and whatever pleases the Highest and Most Powerful Lord, let it be done; and also inform me in all things, for I gladly desire and wish to obey in such great matters. And so, I would not wish to let this day pass without immediately sending these back to you. Meanwhile, I commend both you and myself to the goodness and immense mercy of Almighty God. Given at Krumlov, March 16, in the year 1587.

->Your friend and brother,<-

->Guilielmus <note>Vilém z Rožmberka (William of Rosenberg), Dee’s patron in Bohemia.</note> with his own hand.<-

->To the magnificent men, Lord John Dee and Lord Edward Kelley, and into<-
->their own hands.<-

1587. We finally received this at Třeboň on April 2. For we had departed from Reichstein <note>Rychleby or Reichenstein.</note> and returned before the messenger arrived at Reichstein.

---

Magnificent Lords, dearest friends and brothers, I could not respond to your letters, since Lord Schomberg, through his letters to me about his and his companion's arrival, had signaled... I wanted first to hear what was... intended for me. And if there were any new things or things not yet heard, I would again inform your magnificent lordships. Last night, Lord Schomberg came to me alone, leaving his companion in my monastery at Koruna, half a mile from here, and he explained many things to me about the business; from which, as I understood from him and your letters, he has informed your Magnificences. As I was able to understand, the business has been handled with enough circumspection and foresight until now, and I hope also faithfully. To all these things I responded just as you have very often heard from me, and as I also recently wrote in the letters to your Lordships which I thought should be said to him. 

The whole matter seems to consist of assisting certain persons with some financial help; and according to the written memo or memorial he gave me, which I am sending to your Lordships to read and consider, and afterwards, I pray it be returned to me. Dearest Lords, you know what the will of the Lord is; the next action and others (it seems to me) agree that they should be helped. Let it be done according to the will and most merciful disposition of Him to whom all things belong, and let them be dispatched the more quickly, just as we spoke with Lord Edward. Let them answer to the highest and most powerful Lord concerning the faith which they shall show; but if it has seemed otherwise to the Almighty Lord, let it be so. I ask your Magnificences as lovingly as possible, through your pious prayers to God and the means delivered and granted to you by the Lord, promote and help to carry out the work and will of our Lord God.

The companion remained in the monastery, as was said above, and I concluded with Lord Schomberg that I would neither see nor deal with him, for certain reasons which he will signify to you, and which you will also understand from me. However, so that he may be better satisfied, two or three thousand thalers <note>An early modern silver coin.</note> will be provided for him to purchase certain necessities for himself; he hopes he will be well-satisfied for the time being, provided that the other larger matters are managed as I wrote above.

<meta>This page continues the correspondence from Vilém z Rožmberka (William of Rosenberg) to Dr. John Dee and Edward Kelley. I was not called by the Emperor, but his Majesty requested my opinion on certain matters, about which I wrote back as was fitting.

Concerning the action, I understand that your Lordships are prepared to be ready on the prescribed day; that is good. It is always right and fitting for us to be prepared. May He, most kindly, in His unspeakable mercy and clemency, perfect what is lacking in us. I am pleased with your Lordships' opinion and what you would wish to propose at the beginning and in the prologue of the action, about which you will inform me; I will prepare myself for this and humbly await a response.

->*The things I thought should be proposed are none other than these:*<-

1. *If the Emperor should wish to inquire anything from me about Polish affairs, or if he has conceived any suspicion about me, or is feigning something, how I ought to behave.*
2. *If the Emperor should wish to negotiate anything regarding the succession of this Kingdom for his brother, how I ought to behave.*
3. *If the Polish election should proceed, what the Lord disposes regarding my paternal goods, and what I must do.*
4. *Whether I ought to confidently confer about the Polish business with the Elector of Brandenburg or any Prince of the Empire, or not. With whom, when, and in what manner.*
5. *Whether any soldiers should be hired, and when.*
6. *If the Pope or the Emperor should wish to attempt anything regarding your Lordships' persons, or to exile them again, or disturb them in any way, what should be done and how to respond to them.*
7. *If anything regarding the Treasure <note>Likely referring to the alchemical "philosopher's stone" or spiritual knowledge discovered through their actions.</note> entrusted to us should be communicated to the Caesar <note>The Emperor Rudolf II.</note>, when, how much, and in what manner.*
8. *If the Emperor should wish to use my services for conducting the Diets in **Moravia and Silesia**, whether I should undertake this duty.*

Regarding the rest, let them humbly pray that the Most High may deign to dispose me so that I may please and serve Him alone faithfully and constantly, for the eternal glory of His name and the salvation of the Christian Republic.

If your Lordships think anything should be omitted, or anything that might give offense, I pray for the love of God that you consider it well: omit or amend it according to your piety and prudence.

There is one thing I omitted from the propositions: that I had determined in my mind to establish some foundations here in this country from the Treasure of the Lord kindly granted to me. God, from whom nothing is hidden, knows my mind. Whether this proposal of mine pleases the most merciful Lord or not.

And especially if I must move elsewhere (divine grace so disposing), I would wish my country to know, and all posterity, that I loved it, and felt the best for their safety and that of posterity.

Given at Krumlov, Thursday after Easter, in the year 1587.

->**Your brother and sincere friend**<-
->**from the heart,**<-

William, ->with his own hand.<-

### In the Third Action, to be proposed:

1. *To Almighty God—Father, Son, and Holy Spirit—we offer ourselves most humbly, ready to receive, understand, and execute the Divine Oracles, warnings, instructions, information, and whatever else may be undertaken in this general Action, which His Divine Majesty has foreseen and decreed to be for His glory and our greatest consolation.*

2. *We humbly ask whether this Action shall be fully transacted here, or whether we must hasten to Krumlov with our necessary belongings (and which ones specifically).*

3. *We humbly offer these 12 general questions of our Lord Rosenberg, and whatever else is particularly contained within them, in both his name and ours, expecting such responses as are always accustomed to proceed from the seat of Divine Majesty in the consultations of His servants.*

4. *And because in those same questions no mention was made of the use of the powder which he holds as a gift from God, and since it was previously said several times that in this Action he would be informed about the use of that powder, we now humbly desire that information.*

5. *And because this extraordinary and vehement favor of the Prince of Muscovy <note>The Czar of Russia</note> toward me is now witnessed and made manifest to me and many others (for which I give the greatest possible thanks to God, the Best and Greatest), and because I am uncertain to what end God wishes to direct that favor toward me, I humbly ask that information be given to me by You (Almighty God) concerning that end and Your will in this matter, and how I ought to respond to his messengers if any should come hereafter.*

6. *Whether we ought not to prepare ourselves (as has been warned several times elsewhere) to make the <term>Philosophers' Stone</term> here according to the method of Dunstan. Because that method is not clear to me, it has often made me appear slow, idle, or lazy in this labor; whereas, on the contrary, You know how ready my mind, hands, feet, and all the strengths of both my soul and body are—and You, O God, be my witness.*

7. *That practice involving the iron cup, the glass channel, lime, etc., is not yet succeeding for us; therefore, to obtain the practical truth of that conclusion, we would gladly know what it is that has hindered us so far, or what we lack to truly understand and perfect that practice.*

8. *We commend the health and well-being of the bedridden Thomas Kelley to You, O God, and we pray that You will be merciful to him and to us, and deign to restore and strengthen him to health for the praise, honor, and glory of Your name, through his faithful service and duty toward Your Divine Majesty hereafter. Amen.*

9. *Joanna, the wife of our Edward Kelley, prays to Your Almighty Divine Majesty through me; and I most humbly (in the name of the same Joanna) pray to You, O God, that You would be merciful, clement, and kind to her. Look with fatherly love upon her many prayers to You for the obtaining of fertility with this, her husband; and grant her this joy, and as it were a reward for her faithful service toward this her husband, so that she may be blessed to rejoice in offspring by and with him. Look, we beseech You, upon this our petition, as You once received and even gran—*

*10. For my Jane (O God), I most humbly give thanks that you have thus far so mercifully and piously delivered her from the contagion of her deep-seated infirmity: against which you also taught me to make a medicine, and helped me to make it, and granted such power to the medicine once made that it provided us signs of the desired remedy—signs which our lack of skill hopes are good and certain, rather than being able to judge them by right reason. ### March 20, in the afternoon at 4:15

->J E S U S<-

->Almighty, eternal, and one God.<-

**M**ay you send your light and your truth, so that they may lead me and bring me to your holy mountain and Tabernacles. Amen.
*...... I am blessed Raphael, a blessed messenger of the Almighty; I am sent by God, who is blessed forevermore. Amen.*
*John Dee, I am sent by God for your comfort: first, to certify to you that you shall overcome this your infirmity; and when you are strong in body, as God in his goodness will make you, THEN you shall have all made known to you regarding such things as have not yet come to pass, which have been spoken of before. This is so that you should take comfort in God, knowing that you are not left without the comfort of God's blessed creatures. *Ask as you wish.*
